definition_zh: 遗忘；被遗忘的状态；湮没；失忆
definition_en: the state of having been forgotten, or the loss of memory that makes forgetting possible
core_image: 退潮后的沙滩上，一行字被水一遍遍抹平，最后连写过的痕迹都找不到
scene: 他离开十年后，名字从所有档案里消失，再没人提起。Within a decade his name had passed into oblivion.
sceneCN: 这里 oblivion 指被遗忘的状态（第 1 个义项：被遗忘）；句意为十年之内他的名字已被人遗忘。

senses.title: State of being forgotten
senses.definition: the condition of having dropped out of memory, record or notice
senses.definitionCN: 从记忆、记录或关注中消失的状态
senses.example: Within a decade his name had passed into oblivion.
senses.exampleCN: 十年之内他的名字已被人遗忘。
senses.why: The word names a place things go when no one keeps them: not destroyed, simply unremembered.
senses.whyCN: 这个词命名一个去处：无人保存之物所去之处——不是被毁，而是无人记得。

senses.title: The act of forgetting
senses.definition: the process by which a mind lets go of what it once held
senses.definitionCN: 头脑松开曾经记住之物的过程
senses.example: She sought oblivion in long walks and louder music.
senses.exampleCN: 她用长途散步和更响的音乐寻求忘却。
senses.why: Forgetting can be chosen, and the word then describes an act rather than a fate.
senses.whyCN: 遗忘可以是主动选择的，此时这个词描述的是一种行为，而不是命运。

senses.title: Loss of memory
senses.definition: a condition in which memory fails or is wiped away
senses.definitionCN: 记忆失灵或被抹去的状况
senses.example: After the fever he sank into a fog of oblivion.
senses.exampleCN: 高烧之后，他陷入一片失忆的迷雾。
senses.why: Medicine uses the word for the blank itself, not for what fills it.
senses.whyCN: 医学用这个词指空白本身，而不是填补空白的东西。

senses.title: The sleep of forgetting
senses.definition: the old literary sense of a deep, unremembering sleep
senses.definitionCN: 旧时文学用法：深沉而不留记忆的睡眠
senses.example: He lay in the oblivion of a long anaesthetic.
senses.exampleCN: 他躺在漫长麻醉带来的遗忘之中。
senses.why: Sleep and forgetting were once the same image: a mind switched off and answerable to no one.
senses.whyCN: 睡眠与遗忘曾是同一个意象：一颗关掉、不必向任何人交代的心。

senses.title: Erasure from the record
senses.definition: the removal of a person or event from official or public memory
senses.definitionCN: 把人或事件从官方或公众记忆中移除
senses.example: The regime worked hard to push the protest into oblivion.
senses.exampleCN: 当局竭力把那场抗议推入遗忘。
senses.why: Here the forgetting is organised: archives close, names are dropped, photographs are retouched.
senses.whyCN: 这里的遗忘是被组织的：档案关闭、名字删去、照片被修。

senses.title: Oblivion as relief
senses.definition: a welcomed absence of memory, especially of pain or shame
senses.definitionCN: 对记忆的欣然缺失，尤其是对痛苦或羞耻的记忆
senses.example: Sleep offered him a few hours of oblivion.
senses.exampleCN: 睡眠给了他几小时的忘却。
senses.why: The same blank can be a punishment or a mercy, depending on what it covers.
senses.whyCN: 同一片空白，可以是惩罚，也可以是仁慈，取决于它盖住的是什么。

senses.title: The oblivion of death
senses.definition: the literary image of death as an endless, unconscious darkness
senses.definitionCN: 文学中把死亡想象为无尽无知的黑暗
senses.example: The epitaph spoke of peace, but the word it used was oblivion.
senses.exampleCN: 墓志铭说的是安宁，但用的词是湮没。
senses.why: Death is imagined as the final editor: it removes the name from every list.
senses.whyCN: 死亡被想象为最后的编辑：它把名字从每一份名单上删去。

senses.title: Unawareness of one's surroundings
senses.definition: the state of not noticing what is happening around one
senses.definitionCN: 对周围发生之事毫无察觉的状态
senses.example: He walked through the crowd in complete oblivion of the danger.
senses.exampleCN: 他穿过人群，对危险浑然不觉。
senses.why: This sense moves the word inward: the world is there, but the mind has stopped receiving it.
senses.whyCN: 这个义项把词转向内部：世界仍在，但心已停止接收。

intro.en: Oblivion comes from a Latin verb meaning to forget, and the flatness of that verb is the point: the word has no drama in it.
intro.cn: oblivion 来自一个意为「忘记」的拉丁动词，而那个动词的平淡正是要点：这个词本身没有戏剧性。

items.en: Latin oblivio meant 'forgetfulness', the noun of a mind that has let something go.
items.cn: 拉丁语 oblivio 意为「遗忘」，是松开某物的心智的名词。

items.en: Oblivisci 'to forget' is the verb behind it; its deeper origin is uncertain, and the word does not pretend otherwise.
items.cn: oblivisci「忘记」是它背后的动词；更深的来源并不确定，这个词也不假装知道。

items.en: Old French passed the word to English in the 14c., first in religious writing about sin and death.
items.cn: 古法语在十四世纪把这个词传给英语，最初见于关于罪与死的宗教文字。

items.en: Sixteenth-century writers used it for the darkness after death, giving English its solemn tone.
items.cn: 十六世纪作家用它指死后的黑暗，为英语定下了庄重的语气。

items.en: Today it covers both forgetting and being forgotten, from amnesia to the silence of old records.
items.cn: 今天它同时涵盖「遗忘」与「被遗忘」，从失忆到旧档案的沉默。

note.en: The look-alike group is the oblivious family; the near-meaning group separates forgetting, obscurity and death.
note.cn: 形近组是 oblivious 词族；近义组把「遗忘」「默默无闻」「死亡」分开。

entries.definition: not aware of what is happening.
entries.definitionCN: 对正在发生的事毫无察觉的。

entries.definition: the condition of being little known.
the habit of failing to remember.
the complete disappearance of a thing.

normalIntro.en: The hooks keep the picture of writing on wet sand and the tide returning to erase it.
normalIntro.cn: 以下联想留住「在湿沙上写字、潮水回来把它抹平」的画面。

normal.en: Oblivion hides oblivisci, the Latin verb to forget; forget the Latin and you forget the word.
normal.cn: oblivion 里藏着拉丁动词 oblivisci（忘记）；忘了这个拉丁词，你也就忘了这个词。

normal.en: Think of a name carved in sand at the waterline, erased by the next wave.
normal.cn: 想象一个刻在水线上的名字，被下一道浪抹掉。

normal.en: O-blivion: an 'oblivious' person walks past the sign; the state he leaves behind is oblivion.
normal.cn: o-blivion：一个 oblivious（浑然不觉）的人走过牌子，他留下的状态就是 oblivion。

normal.en: Stress the second syllable: uh-BLIV-ee-un, like a wave folding over.
normal.cn: 重读第二个音节：uh-BLIV-ee-un，像一道浪翻卷下来。

normal.en: Pair it with archive: what an archive stops keeping falls into oblivion.
normal.cn: 把它和 archive 配对：档案不再保存的东西，就落入遗忘。

abstract.en: Being forgotten is not being destroyed; it is being left out of every list.
abstract.cn: 被遗忘不是被毁灭，而是被从每一份名单上漏掉。

abstract.en: The word comforts and threatens at once: sleep is a little oblivion, death a long one.
abstract.cn: 这个词同时安慰与威胁：睡眠是小型的遗忘，死亡是漫长的遗忘。

abstract.en: What a culture chooses to remember is visible in what it lets fall into oblivion.
abstract.cn: 一个文化选择记住什么，可以从它任其湮没的东西里看出来。

examples.en: Within a decade his name had passed into oblivion.
examples.cn: 十年之内他的名字已被人遗忘。

examples.en: Sleep offered him a few hours of oblivion.
examples.cn: 睡眠给了他几小时的忘却。

examples.en: The regime worked hard to push the protest into oblivion.
examples.cn: 当局竭力把那场抗议推入遗忘。

dict_mnemonic.text: ob（离开）+ liv（滑走）+ ion（名词）：记忆滑走了，就是「遗忘、湮没」。

root: 拉丁语 oblivio（遗忘），源自 oblivisci（忘记），经古法语进入英语

sensesIntro.en: All eight senses are one blank seen from different angles: the mind that forgets, the record that drops a name, and the darkness that ends both.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项是同一片空白的八个角度：忘记的心、删掉名字的记录，以及终结两者的黑暗。

core.en: A BLANK WHERE A NAME USED TO BE
core.cn: 名字原来所在的一片空白

branches.en: Forgetting as a state, an erasure and a final darkness.
branches.cn: 遗忘作为状态、抹除与最终的黑暗。

branches.en: The act of letting go, its medical form and its image in sleep.
branches.cn: 松手的行为、它的医学形式与它在睡眠中的意象。

branches.en: The same blank welcomed as relief from pain.
branches.cn: 同一片空白被当作对痛苦的解脱。

branches.en: The everyday sense of walking past what is happening.
branches.cn: 走过眼前之事而毫无察觉的日常义。

branches.en: The same darkness welcomed in sleep and dreaded in death.
branches.cn: 在睡眠中被欢迎、在死亡中被畏惧的同一片黑暗。

intro.en: The obliv- family turns on a single slip: memory slides away, and the person is either the one who forgets or the one forgotten.
intro.cn: obliv- 词族围绕一次滑走：记忆滑开了，人要么是忘记的那方，要么是被忘记的那方。

latinIntro.en: Latin oblivisci supplies the stem; English built the adjective and adverb from it without changing the picture.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 oblivisci 提供词干；英语据此造出形容词与副词，画面没有改变。

items.meaning: the state of having slipped from memory
items.example: The old custom fell into oblivion.

items.meaningCN: 记忆从身边滑过而不知
items.example: She was oblivious to the noise.

items.meaning: in a manner that notices nothing
items.meaningCN: 什么也没注意到的样子
items.example: He obliviously stepped into the puddle.
items.exampleCN: 他浑然不觉地踩进水坑。
她的浑然不觉让向导恼火。

items.example: Obliviscence is a rare word for forgetting.
items.exampleCN: obliviscence 是表示遗忘的罕用词。

items.meaning: to erase letters from the page

items.example: The obliteration of the file was deliberate.
items.exampleCN: 那份档案的抹除是故意的。

items.meaning: the common phrase for not noticing
items.meaningCN: 表示「未察觉」的常用搭配
items.example: They were oblivious to the danger.

definition_zh: 强行插入；强加；突出；闯入
definition_en: to thrust something forward or into a place where it does not belong, often without being asked
core_image: 一扇半开的门缝里，一只手硬把自带的椅子塞进别人的房间
scene: 没人请他发言，他却把自己的观点硬塞进别人的报告里。He obtruded his own opinions into the report.
sceneCN: 这里 obtrude 指把意见强加进去（第 2 个义项：强加于人）；句意为他把自己的观点硬塞进了报告。

senses.title: Thrust forward
senses.definition: to push something into a space already occupied
senses.definitionCN: 把某物推进一个已被占用的空间
senses.example: He obtruded the tray between the two stacks of papers.
senses.exampleCN: 他把托盘硬塞进两叠纸之间。
senses.why: The Latin verb is simply 'to thrust'; the prefix adds the direction, and the rudeness is already in the push.
senses.whyCN: 这个拉丁动词本义就是「推」；前缀加上方向，无礼已经在那一下推里了。

senses.title: Impose on others
senses.definition: to force an idea or demand on people who did not ask for it
senses.definitionCN: 把想法或要求强加给没有开口要它的人
senses.example: He obtruded his own opinions into the report.
senses.exampleCN: 他把自己的观点硬塞进了报告。
senses.why: The harm is not the opinion but the absence of an invitation.
senses.whyCN: 伤害不在观点本身，而在没有邀请。

senses.title: Force oneself in
senses.definition: to enter a group, conversation or place where one is not wanted
senses.definitionCN: 进入一个并不需要自己的群体、谈话或场合
senses.example: She obtruded herself into a quarrel between strangers.
senses.exampleCN: 她硬把自己插进陌生人之间的争吵。
senses.why: A person can be the thing thrust forward, and then the word describes social trespass.
senses.whyCN: 人也可以是被推向前的东西，此时这个词描述的是社交越界。

senses.title: Make itself noticed
senses.definition: of a thing, to stand out in a way that distracts
senses.definitionCN: 事物以分散注意力的方式突出
senses.example: A bright red sign obtruded at the end of the quiet street.
senses.exampleCN: 一块鲜红的招牌在安静的街尾格外惹眼。
senses.why: Here the word is about perception: what obtrudes refuses to stay in the background.
senses.whyCN: 这里的词关乎感知：惹眼之物拒绝留在背景里。

senses.title: Push a claim
senses.definition: to press an argument or claim on an audience beyond what is fitting
senses.definitionCN: 把论点或主张超乎分寸地压给听众
senses.example: The salesman obtruded his guarantee at every pause.
senses.exampleCN: 推销员在每个停顿处硬塞进他的保证。
senses.why: Repetition is how a claim tries to become a fact; the word catches that pressure.
senses.whyCN: 重复是主张试图变成事实的方式，这个词捕捉的正是这份压力。

senses.title: Interrupt speech
senses.definition: to break into another person's speech with one's own
senses.definitionCN: 用自己的话打断别人的话
senses.example: He obtruded a correction before the sentence was finished.
senses.exampleCN: 句子还没说完，他就硬插进一句纠正。
senses.why: The mouth can obtrude as clearly as the hand; timing is what makes it rude.
senses.whyCN: 嘴和手一样能强行插入；决定无礼的是时机。

senses.title: Physical protrusion
senses.definition: to stick out beyond a surface
senses.definitionCN: 超出某个表面而伸出来
senses.example: A root obtrudes through the paving stones.
senses.exampleCN: 一条树根从铺石缝里凸出来。
senses.why: The neutral, physical sense survives in anatomy and engineering.
senses.whyCN: 这个中性的物理义仍活在解剖学与工程学里。

senses.title: Self-assertion
senses.definition: to make one's own presence or merits the centre of attention
senses.definitionCN: 把自己的存在或优点放成注意力的中心
senses.example: The memoir obtrudes its author into every scene.
senses.exampleCN: 这本回忆录把作者硬塞进每一个场景。
senses.why: When the narrator cannot stay out of the frame, the word becomes a criticism of style.
senses.whyCN: 当叙述者无法留在画框之外，这个词就变成对文风的批评。

intro.en: Obtrude is built from a Latin verb for thrusting, and its whole meaning is a push in the wrong direction.
intro.cn: obtrude 由一个表示「推」的拉丁动词构成，它的全部含义就是朝错误方向的一推。

items.en: Trudere meant 'to thrust, to push', the plain physical act behind the word.
items.cn: trudere 意为「推、塞」，是这个词背后朴素的物理动作。

items.en: Obtrudere added ob- 'against, towards' and meant 'to thrust in front of'.
items.cn: obtrudere 加上 ob-（对着、朝向），意为「推到前面」。

items.en: English borrowed the verb in the 16c.; the modern sense of pushing oneself forward appears soon after.
items.cn: 英语在十六世纪借入这个动词，现代「硬把自己推到前面」的义项随即出现。

items.en: Eighteenth-century critics fixed the word in its disapproving tone, especially in talk about manners.
items.cn: 十八世纪批评家把这个词固定在贬义语气上，尤其在谈论礼节的文字里。

items.en: Technical writing kept a neutral sense for anything that sticks out, such as a root or a beam.
items.cn: 技术文字保留了中性义，指任何凸出之物，如树根或梁。

note.en: The look-alike group is the obtrusive family; the near-meaning group separates the push, the entry and the bulge.
note.cn: 形近组是 obtrusive 词族；近义组把「推」「进入」与「凸出」分开。

entries.definitionCN: 以不受欢迎的方式惹眼的。

entries.definition: the quality of forcing itself on notice.
to come in where one is not wanted.
entries.definitionCN: 闯进不需要自己的地方。

entries.definition: to put a demand on someone by authority.
entries.definitionCN: 凭权威把要求加于他人。

normalIntro.en: The hooks hold on to the hand pushing a chair through a half-open door.
normalIntro.cn: 以下联想留住「一只手把椅子硬塞进半开的门」的画面。

normal.en: Obtrude contains trude, to push: the same push sits in intrude and protrude.
normal.cn: obtrude 里有 trude（推）：intrude 与 protrude 里也是同一下推。

normal.en: Think of a chair pushed into a room where every seat is taken.
normal.cn: 想象一把椅子被推进一个已坐满的房间。

normal.en: Ob- sounds like 'object', and people object when you obtrude.
normal.cn: ob- 让人想到 object（反对），你硬插进去时别人就会反对。

normal.en: Say ub-TROOD; the long vowel sounds like a door being forced.
normal.cn: 读成 ub-TROOD，长元音听起来像门被硬推开。

normal.en: If a thing obtrudes it cannot be ignored; if a person obtrudes he cannot be excused.
normal.cn: 物 obtrude 是无法被忽略；人 obtrude 是无法被原谅。

abstract.en: Every obtrusion is a claim that the space belongs to the pusher.
abstract.cn: 每一次强行插入，都是一次宣称这块空间属于推的人。

abstract.en: The word judges the invitation, not the idea; good ideas can be obtruded too.
abstract.cn: 这个词判断的是邀请，而不是想法；好想法也能被硬塞。

abstract.en: A quiet thing can still obtrude if everything around it is quieter.
abstract.cn: 安静之物若周围更安静，也一样能惹眼。

examples.en: He obtruded his own opinions into the report.
examples.cn: 他把自己的观点硬塞进了报告。

examples.en: She obtruded herself into a quarrel between strangers.
examples.cn: 她硬把自己插进陌生人之间的争吵。

examples.en: A root obtrudes through the paving stones.
examples.cn: 一条树根从铺石缝里凸出来。

dict_mnemonic.text: ob（对着）+ trude（推）：朝别人的地方硬推过去，就是「强行插入、强加」。

root: 拉丁语 obtrudere（推到前面），由 ob-（对着）与 trudere（推）构成

sensesIntro.en: The senses all show one push: forward in space, into a conversation, onto other people's attention, and finally out of a surface.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都是同一下推：在空间里向前、插进谈话、压到别人的注意力上，最后从表面凸出。

core.en: A PUSH INTO UNWANTED SPACE

branches.en: The physical push, the social entry and the neutral bulge.
branches.cn: 物理的推、社交的进入与中性的凸出。

branches.en: Ideas, claims and selves pressed on other people.
branches.cn: 观点、主张与自我被压给别人。

branches.en: A thing that will not stay in the background.
branches.cn: 拒绝留在背景里的事物。

branches.en: The mouth doing what the hand does.
branches.cn: 嘴做手所做的事。

branches.en: Notice forced through the eye or the ear.
branches.cn: 通过眼或耳被强行索取的注意。

intro.en: The trud- family is about thrusting: intrude pushes in, protrude pushes out, obtrude pushes at someone.
intro.cn: trud- 词族关乎推：intrude 推入，protrude 推出，obtrude 朝别人推。

latinIntro.en: Latin trudere is the engine; the prefixes only set the direction of the same push.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 trudere 是引擎；前缀只给同一下推设定方向。

items.example: The obtrusion of detail spoiled the essay.
items.exampleCN: 硬塞细节毁了这篇文章。

items.example: A nail protruded from the board.

items.exampleCN: 凸出物挂住了他的袖子。

definition_zh: 寡头；少数掌权者之一；财阀
definition_en: one of a small group of people who together control a country's wealth and political power
core_image: 长桌尽头只摆着几把椅子，其余位置空着，空椅前却都立着别人的名牌
scene: 战后那批人瓜分了国有资源，成了人人都要绕道走的寡头。After the war a handful of men carved up the state assets and became oligarchs whom everyone had to walk around.
sceneCN: 这里 oligarch 指凭借财富掌权的人（第 2 个义项：财阀式掌权者）；句意为战后那批人瓜分了国有资源，成了人人绕道走的寡头。

senses.title: One of a ruling few
senses.definition: a member of a small group that holds power in a state
senses.definitionCN: 在一个国家中掌握权力的少数集团的一员
senses.example: The council had seven seats, and each oligarch owned one.
senses.exampleCN: 议事会只有七个席位，每位寡头占一个。
senses.why: The Greek word simply counts the rulers: not one, not many, but a few.
senses.whyCN: 这个希腊词只是在数统治者：不是一人，不是众人，而是少数。

senses.title: Wealth made into power
senses.definition: a very rich business figure who uses money to shape politics
senses.definitionCN: 用金钱左右政治的极富商界人物
senses.example: The port was sold to an oligarch with friends in the ministry.
senses.exampleCN: 港口卖给了一位在部里有朋友的寡头。
senses.why: Here the title comes from the wallet rather than the ballot.
senses.whyCN: 这里的头衔来自钱包，而不是选票。

senses.title: Post-Soviet owner
senses.titleCN: 后苏联时代的资源寡头
senses.definition: a businessman who acquired state industry in the privatisations of the nineteen-nineties
senses.definitionCN: 在九十年代私有化中取得国有工业的商人
senses.example: Three oligarchs split the oil fields between them.
senses.exampleCN: 三位寡头把油田分掉了。
senses.why: The word became a historical label for a particular decade and a particular method of purchase.
senses.whyCN: 这个词成了某个十年与某种购买方式的历史标签。

senses.title: Member of a closed elite
senses.definition: a person inside a narrow group that keeps opportunity to itself
senses.definitionCN: 身处一个把机会留给自己人的狭小圈子中的人
senses.example: The club behaved like an oligarch, admitting only its own sons.
senses.exampleCN: 那家俱乐部行事像寡头，只收自家的子弟。
senses.why: Power need not be national; any closed circle that hoards access can be described this way.
senses.whyCN: 权力不必是国家级的；任何囤积机会的封闭圈子都可以这样描述。

senses.title: Greek oligarch
senses.definition: one of the few wealthy citizens who ruled a city-state in ancient Greece
senses.definitionCN: 古代希腊城邦中掌权的少数富有公民之一
senses.example: Athens once trusted an oligarch more than a crowd.
senses.exampleCN: 雅典曾比信任民众更信任一位寡头。
senses.why: This is the original setting: a city small enough that a few rich men could govern it.
senses.whyCN: 这是原初语境：一座小到少数富人就能治理的城邦。

senses.title: Financial backer behind a party
senses.definition: a donor whose money buys access to legislation
senses.definitionCN: 用金钱换取立法通道的资助者
senses.example: The bill stalled until an oligarch telephoned the committee.
senses.exampleCN: 法案一直搁置，直到一位寡头给委员会打了电话。
senses.why: The person holds no office, yet the office answers the phone.
senses.whyCN: 此人不任公职，可是公职会接他的电话。

senses.title: Local strongman
senses.definition: a regional figure who controls a town's economy and its officials
senses.definitionCN: 控制一城经济与其官员的地方人物
senses.example: In that province one oligarch decides which road gets paved.
senses.exampleCN: 在那个省，一位寡头决定哪条路先铺。
senses.why: Scale does not change the shape: a small territory can have its own small version.
senses.whyCN: 规模不改变形状：一小块地盘也可以有自己的小版本。

senses.title: The type, not the person
senses.definition: the abstract class of people who own the state rather than serve it
senses.definitionCN: 占有国家而不是服务国家的那一类人的抽象称呼
senses.example: Economists speak of the oligarch as a social type, not a name.
senses.exampleCN: 经济学家把寡头当作一种社会类型，而不是一个名字。
senses.why: Used in the abstract, the word criticises a structure that outlives any individual.
senses.whyCN: 用作抽象概念时，这个词批评的是一种比任何个人都活得久的结构。

intro.en: Oligarch is a Greek counting word: it does not say who rules, only how few.
intro.cn: oligarch 是一个希腊语的计数词：它不说是谁在统治，只说统治者有多几个。

items.en: Oligoi meant 'few', the small number that the word puts at the centre of everything.
items.cn: oligoi 意为「少」，这个词把「少」放在一切的中心。

items.en: Arkhein meant 'to rule, to begin'; joined to oligoi it made oligarkhes, 'one of the few rulers'.
items.cn: arkhein 意为「统治、开始」；与 oligoi 合成 oligarkhes，意为「少数统治者之一」。

items.en: In Greek political writing the word named the rich few who took a city's offices for themselves.
items.cn: 在希腊政治著作中，这个词指把城邦公职据为己有的少数富人。

items.en: English borrowed it in the seventeenth century, chiefly to describe ancient constitutions.
items.cn: 英语在十七世纪借入此词，主要用来描述古代政体。

items.en: After the Soviet collapse it returned to daily use for the men who bought state industry cheaply.
items.cn: 苏联解体后，它重新回到日常用语，指廉价买下国有工业的人。

note.en: The look-alike group is the olig- family; the near-meaning group separates the ruler, the rich man and the closed circle.
note.cn: 形近组是 olig- 词族；近义组把「统治者」「富豪」与「封闭圈子」分开。

entries.definition: relating to rule by a few.
organised as rule by a few.
entries.definitionCN: 以少数人统治方式组织的。

entries.definition: a market owned by a few sellers.
entries.definitionCN: 由少数卖家占据的市场。

entries.definition: a ruler whose power rests on wealth.
entries.definitionCN: 权力建立在财富上的统治者。

entries.definition: a very wealthy and powerful industrialist.
entries.definitionCN: 极富且有权势的实业家。

entries.definition: a ruler who answers to no one.
entries.definitionCN: 不受任何人制约的统治者。

entries.definition: a small group with privileged access.
entries.definitionCN: 享有特权通道的小群体。

normalIntro.en: The hooks keep the picture of a long table where only a few chairs are ever filled.
normalIntro.cn: 以下联想留住「长桌旁只坐满少数几把椅子」的画面。

normal.en: Oligarch hides oligo, the Greek for few; the same few sits inside oligopoly.
normal.cn: oligarch 里藏着 oligo（希腊语的「少」）；oligopoly 里也是同样的「少」。

normal.en: Think of a long table with seven plates and forty guests.
normal.cn: 想象一张长桌，七个盘子，四十位客人。

normal.en: Oli-garch: the 'garch' part sounds like gargle, the sound of a room where only insiders speak.
normal.cn: oli-garch：garch 听起来像漱口声，那是只有圈内人说话的房间里的声音。

normal.en: Stress the first syllable: OL-i-gark, a counting word that stops at a few.
normal.cn: 重读第一个音节：OL-i-gark，一个数到少数就停下的计数词。

normal.en: Pair it with arch, to rule: oligarch means a few arch-rulers, not one.
normal.cn: 把它和 arch（统治）配对：oligarch 是少数几个统治者，而不是一个。

abstract.en: The word never says who the few are; that silence is part of its force.
abstract.cn: 这个词从不说「少数」是谁；这份沉默正是它的力量之一。

abstract.en: An oligarch needs the state to be weak enough to buy and strong enough to protect the purchase.
abstract.cn: 寡头需要国家弱到可以收买，又强到足以保护这笔收买。

abstract.en: Count the chairs, not the speeches, if you want to find the oligarch.
abstract.cn: 想找出寡头，数椅子，别数演讲。

examples.en: After the war a handful of men became oligarchs whom everyone had to walk around.
examples.cn: 战后那几个人成了人人绕道走的寡头。

examples.en: The port was sold to an oligarch with friends in the ministry.
examples.cn: 港口卖给了一位在部里有朋友的寡头。

examples.en: The club behaved like an oligarch, admitting only its own sons.
examples.cn: 那家俱乐部行事像寡头，只收自家子弟。

dict_mnemonic.text: oligo（少）+ arch（统治）：由少数人掌权的人，就是「寡头」。

root: 希腊语 oligarkhēs（少数人统治），由 oligoi（少）与 arkhein（统治）构成

sensesIntro.en: All eight senses count the same small number: the classical ruler, the buyer of state assets, and the closed circle that behaves like both.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项数的都是同一个「少数」：古典的统治者、国有资产的买家，以及行事像两者的封闭圈子。

core.en: A FEW CHAIRS AT A LONG TABLE
core.cn: 长桌旁的少数几把椅子

chain: A STATE IS UP FOR GRABS

branches.en: The classical ruler and his modern descendant.
branches.cn: 古典的统治者与他的现代后裔。

branches.en: Money turned into political voice.
branches.cn: 金钱转化为政治话语权。

branches.en: The post-Soviet owners of state industry.
branches.cn: 后苏联时代国有工业的所有者。

branches.en: A closed elite and the class it forms.
branches.cn: 封闭的精英，以及它形成的阶层。

branches.en: The local version, where one town has one owner.
branches.cn: 地方版本：一座城只有一个主人。

intro.en: The olig- family is built on counting: oligarch, oligarchy and oligopoly all begin with a claim that the number is small.
intro.cn: olig- 词族建立在计数上：oligarch、oligarchy 与 oligopoly 都先声明「数目很小」。

latinIntro.en: Two Greek pieces do the work: oligoi supplies the number, arkhein supplies the rule.
latinIntro.cn: 两个希腊部件在起作用：oligoi 提供数目，arkhein 提供统治。

items.example: The city fell under an oligarchy.
items.exampleCN: 这座城市落入寡头统治。

items.example: The office has a strict hierarchy.
The family was run by a matriarch.
items.exampleCN: 这个家由一位女主人掌舵。

definition_zh: 无所不在的；到处都有的
definition_en: present everywhere at the same time, so that no place is without it
core_image: 每扇窗后都亮着同一盏灯，走到哪里抬头都是同一片光
scene: 连锁店的招牌在每条街口都出现，仿佛同一家店被复制到了所有地方。The chain's sign appears at every street corner, as if the same shop were omnipresent.
sceneCN: 这里 omnipresent 指到处都有（第 1 个义项：处处皆在）；句意为连锁店招牌在每条街口出现，仿佛同一家店无所不在。

pos.zh: 无所不在的；到处可见的

senses.title: Present in every place
senses.definition: existing in all places at the same time
senses.definitionCN: 同一时间存在于所有地方
senses.example: The system is omnipresent, from the capital to the smallest village.
senses.exampleCN: 这套系统无所不在，从首都到最小的村庄。
senses.why: This is the literal core: space has no edge that the thing does not reach.
senses.whyCN: 这是字面核心：空间没有一处是它到不了的边。

senses.title: Seen everywhere in daily life
senses.definition: so common that it meets a person at every turn
senses.definitionCN: 普遍到一个转弯就会遇见
senses.example: Plastic packaging has become omnipresent in the shop.
senses.exampleCN: 塑料包装在店里已随处可见。
senses.why: The word moves from space to habit: it now measures how often, not how far.
senses.whyCN: 这个词从空间转向习惯：它现在衡量的是频率，而不是距离。

senses.title: Of a feeling, universally felt
senses.definition: of a mood or condition, felt by everyone in every setting
senses.definitionCN: 某种情绪或状况在任何场合都被每个人感到
senses.example: A low anxiety was omnipresent in the office that winter.
senses.exampleCN: 那个冬天，办公室里弥漫着低低的焦虑。
senses.why: What is everywhere can be atmospheric rather than physical.
senses.whyCN: 无所不在的东西可以是气氛，而不必是物体。

senses.title: Of a power, impossible to escape
senses.definition: of an authority whose reach leaves no outside
senses.definitionCN: 其触角不留任何外部之地的权力
senses.example: The ministry's paperwork was omnipresent in every school.
senses.exampleCN: 部里的表格在每一所学校都逃不掉。
senses.why: This sense is about control: to be everywhere is to deny anyone a hiding place.
senses.whyCN: 这个义项关乎控制：无所不在，就是不给任何人藏身之处。

senses.title: Of a person, always there
senses.definition: of someone whose attention or presence never quite leaves
senses.definitionCN: 某人的关注或存在始终没有真正离开
senses.example: Her mother was omnipresent in the first weeks of the term.
senses.exampleCN: 开学头几周，她母亲总在身边。
senses.why: A person can borrow the word, and then it describes care or supervision.
senses.whyCN: 人也可以借用这个词，此时它描述的是关怀或看管。

senses.title: Theological omnipresence
senses.definition: of a deity, present throughout creation without being confined to any part
senses.definitionCN: 神明贯穿造物而不被任何局部所限
senses.example: The psalm asserts a god who is omnipresent, even in the dark.
senses.exampleCN: 诗篇宣称一位无所不在的神，即使在黑暗中也同在。
senses.why: Theology needed the word to say that no place is outside the divine.
senses.whyCN: 神学需要这个词来说明没有任何地方在神之外。

senses.title: Data carried by the surroundings
senses.definition: of signals or data, spread through an environment rather than held at one point
senses.definitionCN: 信号或数据散布于环境，而不是集中在某一点
senses.example: In a smart building, sensors are omnipresent but invisible.
senses.exampleCN: 在智能建筑里，传感器无处不在却看不见。
senses.why: The modern sense is technical: presence is distributed, not located.
senses.whyCN: 现代义项是技术性的：在场是分布的，不是定位的。

senses.title: Rhetorical exaggeration
senses.definition: used loosely of anything a speaker feels to be everywhere
senses.definitionCN: 松散地指说话者觉得到处都是的任何事物
senses.example: By December the song was omnipresent, or so it felt.
senses.exampleCN: 到了十二月，那首歌仿佛无处不在。
senses.why: The word is allowed to be hyperbole; feeling everywhere is enough.
senses.whyCN: 这个词允许被夸张使用：感觉上到处都是就够了。

intro.en: Omnipresent joins a Latin word for all to a Latin word for being at hand; it is a theological compound before it is a common adjective.
intro.cn: omnipresent 把一个意为「全部」的拉丁词与一个意为「在手边」的拉丁词接在一起；它先是神学复合词，然后才是普通形容词。

items.en: Omnis meant 'all, every', and survives in omnibus and omniscient.
items.cn: omnis 意为「全部、每一个」，仍活在 omnibus 与 omniscient 里。

items.en: Praesens meant 'being at hand', literally 'sitting before' someone.
items.cn: praesens 意为「在手边」，字面是「坐在某人面前」。

items.en: Omnipraesens was coined in Christian theology for a god present in all places at once.
items.cn: omnipraesens 在基督教神学中被造出，指同时在所有地方的神。

items.en: English took the adjective in the seventeenth century, first in sermons and devotional prose.
items.cn: 英语在十七世纪借入这个形容词，最初见于布道文与灵修散文。

items.en: Modern usage extended it to cameras, brands and data, which really are everywhere.
items.cn: 现代用法把它扩展到摄像头、品牌与数据，这些东西确实到处都有。

note.en: The look-alike group is the omni- family; the near-meaning group separates ubiquity, spread and mere universality.
note.cn: 形近组是 omni- 词族；近义组把「无处不在」「弥散」与「普遍适用」分开。

entries.definition: seeming to be everywhere at once.
true of all cases without exception.
entries.definitionCN: 对所有情形毫无例外地成立的。

entries.definition: regularly found in a place or group.
entries.definitionCN: 在某地或某群体中常见的。

normalIntro.en: The hooks keep the picture of one light burning behind every window.
normalIntro.cn: 以下联想留住「每一扇窗后都亮着同一盏灯」的画面。

normal.en: Omni- means all, as in omnipotent and omniscient; add present and you have present in all.
normal.cn: omni- 意为「全部」，如 omnipotent 与 omniscient；加上 present，就是「在全部地方都在场」。

normal.en: Think of one lamp switched on behind every window on the street.
normal.cn: 想象整条街每一扇窗后都亮着同一盏灯。

normal.en: Om-ni-present: say it as 'all-near', the thing is near everyone at once.
normal.cn: om-ni-present：把它读成「all-near」，这东西同时靠近每个人。

normal.en: Pair it with omnipresence, the noun that names the condition.
normal.cn: 把它和 omnipresence 配对，那个名词命名的正是这种状态。

normal.en: If you can find a corner without it, it is not omnipresent, only widespread.
normal.cn: 如果你能找到一个没有它的角落，它就只是分布广，而不是无所不在。

abstract.en: What is everywhere stops being noticed; ubiquity is the surest way to become invisible.
abstract.cn: 无所不在之物会不再被注意；无处不在是变得隐形最可靠的方式。

abstract.en: The word began as a claim about god and now describes cameras and brands, a sign of what has taken that place.
abstract.cn: 这个词起初是关于神的断言，如今描述摄像头与品牌，这本身说明什么取代了那个位置。

abstract.en: To say a thing is omnipresent is to say no exit exists, which is comfort for some and threat for others.
abstract.cn: 说一物无所不在，等于说没有出口，这对一些人是安慰，对另一些人是威胁。

examples.en: Cameras are now omnipresent in public buildings.
examples.cn: 摄像头如今在公共建筑里随处可见。

examples.en: The brand's omnipresence made it hard to remember a street without it.
examples.cn: 这个品牌无处不在，让人很难想起一条没有它的街。

examples.en: A sense of unease was omnipresent in the room.
examples.cn: 房间里弥漫着一种不安。

dict_mnemonic.text: omni（全部）+ present（在场）：在一切地方都在场，就是「无所不在」。

root: 拉丁语 omnipraesens，由 omnis（全部）与 praesens（在场的）构成

sensesIntro.en: The eight senses all ask the same question, where is it not, and answer nowhere: in space, in habit, in feeling, in power, in a person, in theology, in data and in exaggeration.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都在问同一个问题：哪里没有它？答案都是「没有一处」——在空间、习惯、感受、权力、某个人、神学、数据与夸张之中。

core.en: THE SAME LIGHT IN EVERY WINDOW
core.cn: 每一扇窗后都是同一片光

branches.en: Space and the everyday encounter.
branches.cn: 空间上的处处皆在与日常中的不断遇见。

branches.en: A feeling and a power that leave no outside.
branches.cn: 不留外部之地的感受与权力。

branches.en: A person always at hand, and the loose exaggeration.
branches.cn: 总在身边之人，以及松散的夸张用法。

branches.en: The theological claim of being in all creation.
branches.cn: 神学上关于存在于一切造物之中的主张。

branches.en: Signals carried by the surroundings themselves.
branches.cn: 由周围环境本身承载的信号。

intro.en: The omni- family is about totality: omnipresent reaches every place, omnipotent every power, omniscient every fact.
intro.cn: omni- 词族关乎「全体」：omnipresent 及于每个地方，omnipotent 及于每种权力，omniscient 及于每个事实。

latinIntro.en: Latin omnis supplies the whole, and praesens supplies the nearness; both must be true at once.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 omnis 提供「全部」，praesens 提供「在近处」；两者必须同时成立。

items.exampleCN: 它无处不在，让观众厌倦。

items.example: She was present at the hearing.

items.exampleCN: 他的在场改变了房间的气氛。

definition_zh: 繁重的；费力的；苛重的
definition_en: weighing heavily on a person, so that the work or duty is hard to carry
core_image: 一个人背着装满石头的麻袋，每走一步都要停下来喘一口气
scene: 新规定要求小店每月交三份报表，店主说这负担太重了。The new rule requires three monthly reports from every small shop, a burden the owners call onerous.
sceneCN: 这里 onerous 指负担繁重（第 2 个义项：工作繁重）；句意为新规定要求小店每月交三份报表，店主称之为沉重负担。

senses.title: Heavy to bear
senses.definition: carrying a load that the body or mind finds hard to support
senses.definitionCN: 承载着身心都难以支撑的重量
senses.example: The pack was onerous, and the last mile took an hour.
senses.exampleCN: 背包沉重难负，最后一英里走了一个小时。
senses.why: The word begins with weight, before it means anything about rules.
senses.whyCN: 这个词从重量开始，然后才涉及规则。

senses.title: Of work, burdensome
senses.definition: demanding more effort than the task is worth
senses.definitionCN: 要求付出超过这件事本身价值的努力
senses.example: The paperwork was onerous and no one read it.
senses.exampleCN: 文书工作繁重，却没人读。
senses.why: Labour becomes onerous when the effort outruns the point of doing it.
senses.whyCN: 当付出超过做的意义，劳动就变得繁重。

senses.title: Of a duty, oppressive
senses.definition: of a legal or moral duty, pressing on a person beyond what is fair
senses.definitionCN: 法律或道德义务超乎公平地压在人身上
senses.example: The contract placed an onerous duty of care on the tenant.
senses.exampleCN: 合同把一份苛重的照管义务压在租客身上。
senses.why: Here the weight is not physical but obligatory: one cannot simply put it down.
senses.whyCN: 这里的重量不是物理的，而是义务的：不能随便放下。

senses.title: Of costs, hard to afford
senses.definition: of a payment or charge, large enough to strain the payer
senses.definitionCN: 一笔大到让付款人吃紧的支出或收费
senses.example: The licence fee proved onerous for a village clinic.
senses.exampleCN: 许可费对一家乡村诊所来说过于沉重。
senses.why: Money is the modern stone in the sack.
senses.whyCN: 钱是这袋石头在今天的形态。

senses.title: Of imposed conditions
senses.definition: of terms set by a stronger party, harsh and hard to meet
senses.definitionCN: 强势一方订下、严苛且难以达成的条件
senses.example: The lender offered terms so onerous that refusal was the only answer.
senses.exampleCN: 放贷方的条款太苛刻，拒绝是唯一答案。
senses.why: Power shows itself in who is allowed to write the conditions.
senses.whyCN: 权力体现在谁有资格写下条件。

senses.title: Of style, laborious
senses.definition: of writing, so dense that reading it feels like carrying something
senses.definitionCN: 文字密到读起来像在搬东西
senses.example: The report was onerous prose, correct and unreadable.
senses.exampleCN: 那份报告文风沉重，正确却读不下去。
senses.why: The word can judge a sentence by the effort it takes, not by its length.
senses.whyCN: 这个词可以按读者所费的力气来评断句子，而不按长度。

senses.title: Of responsibility, inescapable
senses.definition: of a responsibility that follows a person and cannot be handed on
senses.definitionCN: 一份跟着人、无法转交的责任
senses.example: Caring for both parents fell on her as an onerous private duty.
senses.exampleCN: 照顾双亲落到她身上，成为一份沉重的私人责任。
senses.why: What makes a duty onerous is often that no one else will take it.
senses.whyCN: 使义务变得沉重的，往往是没有别人肯接。

senses.title: Of proof, over-demanding
senses.definition: of a standard of proof, asking for more evidence than a case can supply
senses.definitionCN: 证明标准要求超过案件所能提供的证据
senses.example: The tribunal set an onerous test for a claim this small.
senses.exampleCN: 裁判庭为这么小的索赔设了过苛的举证标准。
senses.why: In law the word criticises a threshold that closes the door it was meant to open.
senses.whyCN: 在法律里，这个词批评的是一道本该打开、却把人挡在门外的门槛。

intro.en: Onerous comes straight from a Latin adjective for something loaded, and its picture has never changed.
intro.cn: onerous 直接来自一个意为「负了重」的拉丁形容词，它的画面从未改变。

items.en: Onus meant 'a load, a burden', the noun that still appears in English legal writing.
items.cn: onus 意为「负荷、负担」，这个名词仍出现在英语法律文书中。

items.en: Onerosus meant 'full of burden, heavy', built from onus with the adjective ending -osus.
items.cn: onerosus 意为「满是负担的、沉重的」，由 onus 加形容词词尾 -osus 构成。

items.en: Onerare meant 'to load down', the verb behind words about loading and unloading.
items.cn: onerare 意为「装载、使负重」，是关于装载与卸载的词背后的动词。

items.en: English borrowed onerous in the fourteenth century from French legal vocabulary.
items.cn: 英语在十四世纪从法语法律词汇中借入 onerous。

items.en: Today the word survives most strongly in contracts and regulations, where burden is a matter of obligation.
items.cn: 今天这个词最常活在合同与规章里，那里的负担是义务问题。

note.en: The look-alike group is the onus family; the near-meaning group separates weight, effort and cost.
note.cn: 形近组是 onus 词族；近义组把「重量」「费力」与「代价」分开。

entries.definition: a duty or burden resting on someone.
entries.definitionCN: 落在某人身上的义务或负担。

entries.definition: to clear someone of a burden or blame.
entries.definitionCN: 免除某人的负担或罪责。

entries.definition: needing great effort over a long time.
asking for much time and energy.
entries.definitionCN: 要求大量时间与精力的。

normalIntro.en: The hooks keep the picture of a sack of stones and the pause at every step.
normalIntro.cn: 以下联想留住「一袋石头与每走一步都要停顿」的画面。

normal.en: Onerous holds onus, the Latin for burden; English still uses onus in legal talk.
normal.cn: onerous 里藏着 onus（拉丁语的负担）；英语法律用语里仍用 onus。

normal.en: Think of a sack of stones tied to your back before a long walk.
normal.cn: 想象长途步行前，背上被绑了一袋石头。

normal.en: O-ner-ous: the middle syllable sounds like 'nearly', nearly too heavy to finish.
normal.cn: o-ner-ous：中间音节听起来像 nearly，几乎重到走不完。

normal.en: Stress the first syllable: ON-er-us, a weight landing on the front of the word.
normal.cn: 重读第一个音节：ON-er-us，重量落在词的开头。

normal.en: Pair it with duty: an onerous duty is one nobody would volunteer for.
normal.cn: 把它和 duty 配对：onerous duty 是没人愿意主动接的义务。

abstract.en: A burden is onerous when the person carrying it could not have refused it.
abstract.cn: 当背负者无法拒绝时，负担才是苛重的。

abstract.en: The word measures the gap between the effort required and the good it buys.
abstract.cn: 这个词衡量的是所需努力与它所换来的好处之间的落差。

abstract.en: Rules are called onerous when they cost more to obey than to ignore.
abstract.cn: 当遵守规则比忽视它代价更高，规则就被称为苛重。

examples.en: The new rule requires three monthly reports, a burden the owners call onerous.
examples.cn: 新规定要求每月交三份报表，店主称之为沉重负担。

examples.en: The contract placed an onerous duty of care on the tenant.
examples.cn: 合同把一份苛重的照管义务压在租客身上。

examples.en: The report was onerous prose, correct and unreadable.
examples.cn: 那份报告文风沉重，正确却读不下去。

dict_mnemonic.text: oner（负担）+ ous（形容词）：满是负担的，就是「繁重的」。

root: 拉丁语 onerosus（有负担的），源自 onus（负担）

sensesIntro.en: The eight senses put the same stone in different sacks: a body, a job, a duty, a bill, a contract, a sentence, a responsibility and a legal test.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项把同一块石头装进不同的袋子：身体、工作、义务、账单、合同、句子、责任与法律门槛。

core.en: A SACK OF STONES ON THE BACK

chain: NO ONE ELSE WILL CARRY IT
THE WORK IS DONE AT A PRICE

branches.en: A physical load and a responsibility that follows a person.
branches.cn: 物理的重量与跟着人的责任。

branches.en: Effort spent on a task and on a sentence.
branches.cn: 花在任务上的力气与花在句子上的力气。

branches.en: Duties and conditions written by a stronger party.
branches.cn: 由强势一方写下的义务与条件。

branches.en: The modern stone, which is money.
branches.cn: 现代的石头，也就是钱。

branches.en: A threshold that demands more than a case can give.
branches.cn: 要求超过案件所能提供的门槛。

intro.en: The oner- family is about loading: onus is the load, onerous is the loaded state, exonerate is taking the load off.
intro.cn: oner- 词族关乎装载：onus 是负荷，onerous 是负重的状态，exonerate 是把负担卸下。

latinIntro.en: Latin onus is the weight; the suffix -osus turned it into an adjective, and ex- later turned it into release.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 onus 是重量；后缀 -osus 把它变成形容词，前缀 ex- 后来又把它变成释放。

items.example: The onus of proof lies with the accuser.
His exoneration came after nine years.

definition_zh: 合适的；恰好的；及时的
definition_en: arriving at a moment or in a way that suits what is being done
core_image: 手刚敲门，门就在那一瞬间打开
scene: 他辞职的消息正好在选举前一天传出，时机再合适不过。News of his resignation came out the day before the election, an opportune moment by any measure.
sceneCN: 这里 opportune 指时机恰好（第 1 个义项：时机正好）；句意为辞职消息正好在选举前一天传出，时机再合适不过。

senses.title: Well-timed
senses.definition: happening at the moment that suits it best
senses.definitionCN: 发生在最适合它的那一刻
senses.example: The rain stopped at an opportune moment for the ceremony.
senses.exampleCN: 雨在仪式开始前恰好停了。
senses.why: The core is a match between event and moment, with nothing forced.
senses.whyCN: 核心是事件与时刻的吻合，毫无勉强。

senses.title: Convenient
senses.definition: placed or offered where it saves trouble
senses.definitionCN: 放在或提供在能省事的地方
senses.example: A bench appeared at an opportune spot on the long path.
senses.exampleCN: 长路上恰好在合适的位置出现一条长凳。
senses.why: The word can describe things, not only times; convenience is a kind of fit.
senses.whyCN: 这个词也能形容事物，不只是时间；方便是一种吻合。

senses.title: Favourable
senses.definition: of a chance, offering an advantage if it is taken now
senses.definitionCN: 机会若当下抓住就带来好处
senses.example: The market was opportune for a small first sale.
senses.exampleCN: 市场对小规模的首笔销售很有利。
senses.why: Here the fit is between a condition and an aim.
senses.whyCN: 这里吻合的是条件与目标。

senses.title: Apt in speech
senses.definition: of a remark, said at the moment when it can be heard
senses.definitionCN: 话在能被听进去的时刻说出
senses.example: His opportune question saved the meeting an hour.
senses.exampleCN: 他那句问得正是时候，为会议省了一小时。
senses.why: Timing is the whole merit; the same sentence a day later would be an intrusion.
senses.whyCN: 全部优点就在时机；同一句话晚一天说就是打扰。

senses.title: Well placed
senses.definition: of a building or place, situated where it is most useful
senses.definitionCN: 建筑或地点位于最有用的位置
senses.example: The clinic stood at an opportune corner of the district.
senses.exampleCN: 诊所正好位于这一区适用的街角。
senses.why: Space repeats the logic of time: the right thing in the right place.
senses.whyCN: 空间重复了时间的逻辑：对的东西在对的地方。

senses.title: Politically timed
senses.definition: of a decision, made when the advantage outweighs the cost
senses.definitionCN: 在好处大于代价时做出的决定
senses.example: The tax cut was opportune rather than principled.
senses.exampleCN: 减税是出于时机，而不是出于原则。
senses.why: The word can be neutral or sly, depending on who is judging the timing.
senses.whyCN: 这个词可中性也可带讥意，取决于谁在评判这个时机。

senses.title: Arranged at the right time
senses.definition: of a meeting or event, set for a time that suits everyone
senses.definitionCN: 会议或活动被定在适合所有人的时间
senses.example: The visit was opportune for both departments.
senses.exampleCN: 这次访问对两个部门都正合时宜。
senses.why: Planning can produce the luck that the word seems to describe.
senses.whyCN: 计划可以制造出这个词看似在描述的那种运气。

senses.title: Seemingly lucky
senses.definition: appearing to be a happy accident, whether or not it was arranged
senses.definitionCN: 看上去像幸运的巧合，无论是否被安排过
senses.example: It was opportune that the witness called that morning.
senses.exampleCN: 证人那天早上打来电话，实在凑巧。
senses.why: The word leaves open whether the fit was luck, skill or design.
senses.whyCN: 这个词不说明这种吻合是运气、技巧还是设计。

intro.en: Opportune began as a sailing word: a wind that blows toward the harbour is a wind that suits you.
intro.cn: opportune 起初是个航海词：吹向港口的风，才是顺着你的风。

items.en: Portus meant 'harbour', the place a ship is trying to reach.
items.cn: portus 意为「港口」，是船努力要抵达的地方。

items.en: Ob- meant 'towards, against', the direction a favouring wind must blow.
items.cn: ob- 意为「朝向、对着」，是顺风必须吹的方向。

items.en: Opportunus first described a wind blowing ships toward port, hence 'favourable'.
items.cn: opportunus 最初描述把船吹向港口的风，因此意为「有利的」。

items.en: English borrowed it through French, widening it from winds to hours and chances.
items.cn: 英语经法语借入此词，把它从风扩展到时辰与机会。

items.en: Today it mostly judges timing, and keeps a faint memory of the harbour in its calm, easy tone.
items.cn: 今天它主要评判时机，平静轻松的语气里还留着一点港口记忆。

note.en: The look-alike group is the opportun- family; the near-meaning group separates timing, convenience, advantage and aptness.
note.cn: 形近组是 opportun- 词族；近义组把「时机」「方便」「有利」与「贴切」分开。

normalIntro.en: The hooks keep the picture of a door opening exactly as a hand knocks.
normalIntro.cn: 以下联想留住「手刚敲门，门就正好打开」的画面。

normal.en: Opportune hides port, the harbour: a wind blowing toward port is a wind that suits the ship.
normal.cn: opportune 里藏着 port（港口）：吹向港口的风，正是顺着船的风。

normal.en: Think of a door that opens at the instant of a knock.
normal.cn: 想象一扇在敲击瞬间打开的门。

normal.en: Op-por-tune: the middle sounds like 'port', the harbour where the timing is right.
normal.cn: op-por-tune：中间听起来像 port，时机合适的那个港口。

normal.en: Stress the second syllable: uh-POR-tune, like a ship arriving.
normal.cn: 重读第二个音节：uh-POR-tune，像船入港。

normal.en: Pair it with moment: an opportune moment is one that costs you nothing to use.
normal.cn: 把它和 moment 配对：opportune moment 是一个用起来不费力的时刻。

abstract.en: Good timing is often the cheapest form of skill.
abstract.cn: 好时机往往是技巧中最便宜的一种。

abstract.en: The word asks not whether a thing is good, but whether it is good now.
abstract.cn: 这个词不问一件事好不好，只问它此刻好不好。

abstract.en: Opportune is not opportunistic: one describes a fit, the other a habit of hunting for one.
abstract.cn: opportune 不是 opportunistic：前者描述吻合，后者描述寻找吻合的习惯。

examples.en: News of his resignation came out at an opportune moment.
examples.cn: 他辞职的消息传出得正是时候。

examples.en: His opportune question saved the meeting an hour.
examples.cn: 他那句问得正是时候，为会议省了一小时。

examples.en: The clinic stood at an opportune corner of the district.
examples.cn: 诊所正好位于这一区适用的街角。

dict_mnemonic.text: op（朝向）+ port（港口）：风把船吹向港口，正是「及时、合适」的方向。

root: 拉丁语 opportunus（顺风的、合宜的），字面为「朝向港口」

sensesIntro.en: The eight senses all describe a fit: a time to an event, a place to a use, a chance to an aim, a remark to a hearing, and a plan to a need.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项描述的都是吻合：时间与事件、地点与用途、机会与目标、话与听众、计划与需要。

core.en: A DOOR OPENING AS A HAND KNOCKS
core.cn: 手敲门的瞬间门正好打开

branches.en: A moment that suits an event and an event that suits a moment.
branches.cn: 适合事件的时刻与适合时刻的事件。

branches.en: A convenient thing and a well-placed building.
branches.cn: 方便之物与位置得当的建筑。

branches.en: An advantage to be taken and a decision timed for gain.
branches.cn: 可把握的好处与为利益择时的决定。

branches.en: A sentence said where it can be heard.
branches.cn: 在能被听进去之处说出的一句话。

branches.en: A fit that may be luck, skill or design.
branches.cn: 可能是运气、技巧或设计的吻合。

intro.en: The opportun- family grows from port: opportune is the favourable wind, opportunity is the harbour it brings you to.
intro.cn: opportun- 词族从 port 长出来：opportune 是顺风，opportunity 是它把你送到的港口。

latinIntro.en: Latin ob- gives direction and portus gives the goal; the adjective names a wind that serves both.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 ob- 给方向，portus 给目标；那个形容词命名一阵同时满足两者的风。

items.example: The opportuneness of the visit was noted.
items.exampleCN: 这次访问的时机恰被注意到。
这个决定带着投机气味。

items.example: He importuned the clerk for an answer.
items.exampleCN: 他反复缠着职员要答复。

definition_zh: 压迫的；压抑的；闷热的
definition_en: weighing on people with unjust power, or making the air and the mood hard to breathe
core_image: 一间没有窗的屋子，屋顶一寸寸压低，屋里的人越来越说不出话
scene: 那个夏天城里查得很紧，街上没人敢多停一步。That summer the city was policed so tightly that no one dared stop on the street, and the whole town felt oppressive.
sceneCN: 这里 oppressive 指政治压迫（第 1 个义项：政治压迫）；句意为那夏天城里查得极紧，没人敢在街上多停，全城都显得压抑。

senses.title: Politically oppressive
senses.definition: using authority unjustly to keep people down
senses.definitionCN: 不正当地运用权力压住民众
senses.example: The regime was oppressive and afraid of its own square.
senses.exampleCN: 那个政权压迫人民，也害怕自己的广场。
senses.why: This is the word's public sense: power that takes away room to speak.
senses.whyCN: 这是这个词的公共义：剥夺说话空间的权力。

senses.title: Crushing burden
senses.definition: of a demand or charge, so heavy that it bends the person under it
senses.definitionCN: 要求或收费重到把人压弯
senses.example: The debt was oppressive and grew faster than the farm.
senses.exampleCN: 债务沉重，增长得比农场还快。
senses.why: Weight here is financial, yet the body feels it all the same.
senses.whyCN: 这里的重量是财务的，身体却照样感觉得到。

senses.title: Stifling heat
senses.definition: of weather, hot and still in a way that leaves no air to breathe
senses.definitionCN: 天气酷热无风，几乎呼吸不到空气
senses.example: The afternoon was oppressive, and the fans only moved warm air.
senses.exampleCN: 午后闷热难当，风扇只是把热风搅动。
senses.why: The physical sense is old and literal: the air itself presses down.
senses.whyCN: 这个物理义古老而字面：空气本身在往下压。

senses.title: Stifling atmosphere
senses.definition: of a room or gathering, tense in a way that stops easy speech
senses.definitionCN: 房间或聚会紧张到让人不能轻松开口
senses.example: An oppressive quiet settled over the dinner table.
senses.exampleCN: 餐桌上笼上一层压抑的安静。
senses.why: Weather moves indoors: the same pressure can be social.
senses.whyCN: 天气转入室内：同一种压力也可以是社交的。

senses.title: Oppressive silence
senses.definition: of a silence, so complete that it feels imposed rather than peaceful
senses.definitionCN: 沉默完整到像被强加，而非安宁
senses.example: The oppressive silence after the question told him no one would answer.
senses.exampleCN: 那个问题之后令人窒息的沉默告诉他，没有人会回答。
senses.why: Silence can be a form of force when everyone is waiting for someone else to speak.
senses.whyCN: 当所有人都在等别人开口，沉默也可以是一种强制。

senses.title: Harsh in law
senses.definition: of rules, written so tightly that ordinary life becomes an offence
senses.definitionCN: 规则写得极紧，日常生活动辄得咎
senses.example: The city's oppressive bylaws fined pedlars for standing still.
senses.exampleCN: 这座城市苛酷的条例对小贩站着不动也罚款。
senses.why: The word judges the reach of a rule, not only its severity.
senses.whyCN: 这个词评判规则的触角，不只是它的严厉。

senses.title: Domineering institution
senses.definition: of an organisation, acting as if its convenience outranks everyone else's
senses.definitionCN: 机构行事仿佛自己的方便高于所有人
senses.example: The ministry was oppressive even in its opening hours.
senses.exampleCN: 那个部连办公时间都透着专横。
senses.why: Institutions can press without violence, simply by making every other life wait.
senses.whyCN: 机构可以不靠暴力施压，只要让所有别人的生活等它。

senses.title: Weighing anxiety
senses.definition: of a feeling, sitting on the chest and refusing to lift
senses.definitionCN: 某种情绪压在胸口，不肯移开
senses.example: An oppressive dread followed him through the week.
senses.exampleCN: 一整周，一种压抑的恐惧跟着他。
senses.why: The inward sense is the same weight turned private.
senses.whyCN: 向内的义项是同一份重量转向私人。

intro.en: Oppressive is a pressing word: something is laid on you and does not lift.
intro.cn: oppressive 是一个「压」的词：有东西压在你身上，而且不肯抬起来。

items.en: Premere meant 'to press', the plain physical verb behind press and print.
items.cn: premere 意为「压」，是 press 与 print 背后朴素的物理动词。

items.en: Ob- meant 'against, towards', giving the pressure a direction.
items.cn: ob- 意为「对着、朝向」，给这份压力一个方向。

items.en: Opprimere meant 'to press against, to crush, to overwhelm'.
items.cn: opprimere 意为「压向、压碎、压倒」。

items.en: English borrowed oppress in the fourteenth century, and the adjective followed.
items.cn: 英语在十四世纪借入动词 oppress，形容词随后出现。

items.en: Modern English keeps both the political sense and the weather sense, and uses the same word for a mood.
items.cn: 现代英语同时保留政治义与天气义，并用同一个词形容情绪。

note.en: The look-alike group is the press family; the near-meaning group separates tyranny, air and weight.
note.cn: 形近组是 press 词族；近义组把「暴政」「闷热」与「重量」分开。

entries.definition: unjust use of power over people.
a person who keeps others down.
in a crushing or stifling way.

entries.definitionCN: 以残酷绝对权力统治的。

entries.definition: so hot or tense that breathing is hard.

normalIntro.en: The hooks keep the picture of a windowless room whose ceiling keeps lowering.
normalIntro.cn: 以下联想留住「无窗的屋子、屋顶不断压低」的画面。

normal.en: Oppressive holds press: to oppress is to press on someone until he cannot stand.
normal.cn: oppressive 里有 press：oppress 就是压住某人直到他站不起来。

normal.en: Think of a ceiling that comes down one inch with every hour.
normal.cn: 想象屋顶每小时下降一英寸。

normal.en: Op-press-ive: three syllables, each one heavier than the last.
normal.cn: op-press-ive：三个音节，一个比一个重。

normal.en: Say uh-PRESS-iv; the stress lands on press, exactly where the weight is.
normal.cn: 读成 uh-PRESS-iv，重音落在 press 上，正是重量所在。

normal.en: Pair it with heat: oppressive heat is weather doing what a regime does.
normal.cn: 把它和 heat 配对：oppressive heat 是天气在做政权做的事。

abstract.en: Oppression is often quiet; the loudest part is the silence it teaches people to keep.
abstract.cn: 压迫常常是安静的；最响的部分是它教会人们保持的沉默。

abstract.en: The same word covers a government, a debt, a July afternoon and a dinner table, because all four take away breath.
abstract.cn: 同一个词覆盖政府、债务、七月的午后与一张餐桌，因为这四者都夺走呼吸。

abstract.en: A thing is oppressive when it removes the option of leaving.
abstract.cn: 当一样东西取消了离开的选项，它就是压抑的。

examples.en: That summer the city was so tightly policed that the whole town felt oppressive.
examples.cn: 那夏天城里查得极紧，全城都显得压抑。

examples.en: The afternoon was oppressive, and the fans only moved warm air.
examples.cn: 午后闷热难当，风扇只是把热风搅动。

examples.en: An oppressive quiet settled over the dinner table.
examples.cn: 餐桌上笼上一层压抑的安静。

dict_mnemonic.text: op（对着）+ press（压）+ ive：一直压着你，就是「压迫的、压抑的」。

root: 拉丁语 opprimere（压向、压倒），由 ob-（对着）与 premere（压）构成

sensesIntro.en: The eight senses are one pressure under different hands: a state, a debt, the weather, a room, a silence, a law, an office and a fear.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项是同一份压力落在不同的手上：国家、债务、天气、房间、沉默、法律、机关与恐惧。

core.en: A CEILING THAT KEEPS LOWERING

branches.en: Power written into a state and into a rule book.
branches.cn: 写进国家与规则手册的权力。

branches.en: A financial weight that bends a life.
branches.cn: 压弯生活的财务重量。

branches.en: Air that will not move and silence that will not break.
branches.cn: 不肯流动的空气与不肯打破的沉默。

branches.en: A tense room and an institution that makes everyone wait.
branches.cn: 紧绷的房间与让所有人等待的机构。

branches.en: The same pressure turned inward.
branches.cn: 同一份压力转向内心。

intro.en: The press family is about what sits on top: oppress presses against, suppress presses down, compress presses together.
intro.cn: press 词族关乎压在上面的东西：oppress 压向，suppress 压下，compress 压紧。

latinIntro.en: Latin premere is the press; the prefixes ob-, sub-, com- and ex- only change which way the weight travels.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 premere 是那一下压；前缀 ob-、sub-、com- 与 ex- 只改变重量走的方向。

items.meaning: to press against, to keep down

definition_zh: 富裕；奢华；丰富
definition_en: great wealth shown in costly things, or an abundance so full that it spills over
core_image: 厅里堆满金器与丝绸，连椅背都镀了金，光从每件东西上反回来
scene: 老宅卖掉时，屋里还留着当年的富丽：金边镜子、丝绒窗帘、嵌着贝壳的柜子。When the old house was sold, the opulence of its former years remained in gilded mirrors, velvet curtains and cupboards inlaid with shell.
sceneCN: 这里 opulence 指物质的奢华排场（第 2 个义项：奢华排场）；句意为老宅卖掉时屋里仍留着当年的富丽。

senses.title: Great wealth
senses.definition: a large amount of money and property held by one person or family
senses.definitionCN: 一个人或家族持有的大量钱财与产业
senses.example: The family's opulence was measured in land rather than cash.
senses.exampleCN: 这个家族的富裕以土地而非现金衡量。
senses.why: The core is quantity: more than enough, held in few hands.
senses.whyCN: 核心是数量：多得用不完，且握在少数人手里。

senses.title: Luxurious display
senses.definition: wealth put on show in costly objects and settings
senses.definitionCN: 用昂贵物件与场所把财富摆出来
senses.example: The hall was built for opulence, not for comfort.
senses.exampleCN: 那座大厅是为排场而建，不是为舒适。
senses.why: Display is the outward turn of wealth: the same money, now aimed at other eyes.
senses.whyCN: 展示是财富向外的一转：同一笔钱，现在对准别人的眼睛。

senses.title: Abundance of something
senses.definition: a fullness of a quality or material that goes past what is needed
senses.definitionCN: 某种性质或材料多到超过所需
senses.example: The essay has an opulence of detail that hides its argument.
senses.exampleCN: 这篇文章细节繁富，反而盖住了论点。
senses.why: The word can leave money behind and simply mean plenty.
senses.whyCN: 这个词可以离开金钱，只表示「多」。

senses.title: Richness of a place
senses.definition: of a building or city, a richness that declares its owner's standing
senses.definitionCN: 建筑或城市以富丽宣示主人的地位
senses.example: The hotel lobby suggested an opulence the rooms did not keep.
senses.exampleCN: 酒店大堂透着富丽，客房却没维持住。
senses.why: Places are judged by what they promise before anyone arrives.
senses.whyCN: 地方靠它在人到达前许下的承诺被评判。

senses.title: Ornate excess in style
senses.definition: of writing or design, ornament piled on ornament until the form is heavy
senses.definitionCN: 文字或设计装饰叠装饰，直到形式变重
senses.example: The baroque church loves opulence more than line.
senses.exampleCN: 巴洛克教堂爱繁复胜过线条。
senses.why: Style borrows the vocabulary of money, and excess becomes an aesthetic judgement.
senses.whyCN: 风格借用了金钱的词汇，过度变成了美学判断。

senses.title: Riches in old use
senses.definition: the older sense of wealth as a power one possesses, not only as goods
senses.definitionCN: 较古的义项：财富是一种拥有的力量，不只是货物
senses.example: Seventeenth-century sermons warned against trusting opulence.
senses.exampleCN: 十七世纪的布道警告人不要信赖财富。
senses.why: Before economics, riches were imagined as a kind of strength.
senses.whyCN: 在经济学之前，财富被想象为一种力量。

senses.title: A comfortable life
senses.definition: a life so well supplied that effort becomes optional
senses.definitionCN: 供给好到努力变成可有可无的生活
senses.example: They retired into a quiet opulence of garden and library.
senses.exampleCN: 他们退入一种安静的富足：花园与书房。
senses.why: Here the word is private and calm, without the show of sense two.
senses.whyCN: 这里的词是私人的、安静的，没有第二义项那种展示。

senses.title: Richness of language
senses.definition: a vocabulary so abundant that it can afford to waste words
senses.definitionCN: 词汇丰足到浪费得起词语
senses.example: His prose has the opulence of a market at noon.
senses.exampleCN: 他的文句有正午集市般的丰盈。
senses.why: The metaphor turns wealth into style: too much is a kind of beauty until it is not.
senses.whyCN: 这个比喻把财富变成风格：过多是一种美，直到它不再是。

intro.en: Opulence descends from a Latin word for resources, and its -ulentus ending already meant 'full of'.
intro.cn: opulence 来自一个意为「资源」的拉丁词，它的 -ulentus 词尾本义就是「充满」。

items.en: Ops meant 'power, resources, wealth', the root of several words about having enough.
items.cn: ops 意为「力量、资源、财富」，是几个表示「拥有足够」的词根。

items.en: Opulentus meant 'rich, abundant', built on ops with the ending -ulentus, 'full of'.
items.cn: opulentus 意为「富裕的、丰盛的」，由 ops 加词尾 -ulentus（充满）构成。

items.en: Opulentia named the condition itself, the fullness rather than the person.
items.cn: opulentia 命名的是这种状态本身，是「丰足」而不是「富人」。

items.en: English borrowed the noun in the fifteenth century through French.
items.cn: 英语在十五世纪经法语借入这个名词。

items.en: Modern use keeps the money sense and adds style, place and language to what can be called opulent.
items.cn: 现代用法保留金钱义，并把风格、场所与语言也纳入可称 opulent 的范围。

note.en: The look-alike group is the -ulentus adjectives; the near-meaning group separates wealth, luxury and show.
note.cn: 形近组是 -ulentus 形容词；近义组把「财富」「奢华」与「排场」分开。

entries.definition: great comfort bought at high cost.
the state of having plenty of money.
a large stock of money or property.

normalIntro.en: The hooks keep the picture of gold on every surface, even the backs of chairs.
normalIntro.cn: 以下联想留住「每件东西表面都是金，连椅背也镀了金」的画面。

normal.en: Opulence hides ops, Latin for resources; opulent and opulence share the same full root.
normal.cn: opulence 里藏着 ops（拉丁语的资源）；opulent 与 opulence 共用这个「满」的词根。

normal.en: Think of a room where the gold is on the furniture, not in the bank.
normal.cn: 想象一个房间，金子在家具上，而不在银行里。

normal.en: Op-u-lence: the last syllable sounds like 'lens', every surface reflecting.
normal.cn: op-u-lence：最后一个音节听起来像 lens，每个表面都在反光。

normal.en: Stress the first syllable: OP-u-lence, the weight of things at the front.
normal.cn: 重读第一个音节：OP-u-lence，物件的重量压在词首。

normal.en: Pair it with velvet: opulence is what velvet curtains are trying to say.
normal.cn: 把它和 velvet 配对：opulence 正是丝绒窗帘想说的话。

abstract.en: Opulence is wealth that has learned to speak; the objects are its sentences.
abstract.cn: opulence 是学会说话的财富；那些物件就是它的句子。

abstract.en: A room can be opulent and uncomfortable at once, which tells you the display was the point.
abstract.cn: 一个房间可以既富丽又不舒服，这说明展示才是目的。

abstract.en: The word is generous: it will also describe detail, prose and a market at noon.
abstract.cn: 这个词很慷慨：它也会形容细节、文句与正午的集市。

examples.en: When the old house was sold, the opulence of its former years remained in gilded mirrors.
examples.cn: 老宅卖掉时，屋里仍留着当年的富丽：金边镜子。

examples.en: The essay has an opulence of detail that hides its argument.
examples.cn: 这篇文章细节繁富，反而盖住了论点。

examples.en: The hotel lobby suggested an opulence the rooms did not keep.
examples.cn: 酒店大堂透着富丽，客房却没维持住。

dict_mnemonic.text: op（资源）+ ulent（充满）+ ence（名词）：资源满溢的状态，就是「富裕、奢华」。

root: 拉丁语 opulentia（富裕），源自 ops（资源、财富）

sensesIntro.en: The eight senses all describe fullness: money in few hands, objects on show, detail past need, a place that announces itself, a style, an old idea of power, a quiet life and a crowded vocabulary.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项描述的都是「满」：少数手中的钱、摆出来的物件、超过所需的细节、自我宣告的场所、一种风格、古老的权力观、安静的生活与拥挤的词汇。

core.en: GOLD ON EVERY SURFACE

branches.en: Money held quietly and a life that needs no effort.
branches.cn: 静静握着的钱与无需努力的生活。

branches.en: A show put on by objects and by a building.
branches.cn: 由物件与建筑上演的展示。

branches.en: Plenty of detail and plenty of words.
branches.cn: 细节的丰与词语的丰。

branches.en: Ornament piled until the form is heavy.
branches.cn: 装饰叠加到形式变重。

branches.en: The old sense of riches as a kind of power.
branches.cn: 财富作为一种力量的古义。

intro.en: The -ulentus family means 'full of': opulent is full of resources, corpulent full of body, truculent full of fierceness.
intro.cn: -ulentus 词族意为「充满」：opulent 充满资源，corpulent 充满身体，truculent 充满凶气。

latinIntro.en: Latin ops supplies the resources and -ulentus supplies the fullness; the noun opulentia names that fullness itself.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 ops 提供资源，-ulentus 提供丰盈；名词 opulentia 命名的正是这份丰盈。

items.example: He wrote of the opulency of the court.

definition_zh: 磨难；严峻考验；痛苦的经历
definition_en: a long and painful experience that tests a person to the edge of what can be borne
core_image: 一个人从没灯的小屋里走出来，脸上还留着里面的黑
scene: 那场手术持续了九个小时，家人守在走廊里，谁都不说话。The operation lasted nine hours, and the family sat in the corridor without speaking, an ordeal none of them would repeat.
sceneCN: 这里 ordeal 指痛苦的煎熬（第 2 个义项：痛苦的经历）；句意为手术持续九小时，家人守在走廊里沉默不语，那是谁都不愿再经历一次的煎熬。

pos.zh: 磨难；严峻考验；痛苦经历

senses.title: A severe test
senses.definition: an event that measures how much a person can endure
senses.definitionCN: 检验一个人能承受多少的事件
senses.example: The climb was an ordeal that few finished.
senses.exampleCN: 那次攀登是一场很少有人完成的考验。
senses.why: The word weighs endurance, not difficulty alone.
senses.whyCN: 这个词衡量的是承受力，不只是难度。

senses.title: A painful experience
senses.definition: a stretch of time that hurts and cannot be shortened
senses.definitionCN: 一段疼着又无法缩短的时间
senses.example: The operation lasted nine hours and was an ordeal for the family.
senses.exampleCN: 手术持续九小时，对家人是一场煎熬。
senses.why: Here the pain belongs to those waiting as much as to the patient.
senses.whyCN: 这里的痛苦，等候的人承受得不比病人少。

senses.title: A drawn-out trial
senses.definition: a process so long that the length itself becomes the hardship
senses.definitionCN: 过程长到「长」本身成了苦
senses.example: The appeal dragged on for years, an ordeal of letters and delays.
senses.exampleCN: 上诉拖了多年，成了信件与拖延构成的折磨。
senses.why: Duration is a kind of weight; the word lets time do the pressing.
senses.whyCN: 时长是一种重量；这个词让时间来施压。

senses.title: Trial by ordeal
senses.definition: a historical test in which a person's fate was decided by fire, water or combat
senses.definitionCN: 历史上以火、水或格斗决定命运的裁判方式
senses.example: In the old accounts, the accused walked over hot iron in an ordeal.
senses.exampleCN: 在旧记载里，被控者要在神判中走过烧红的铁。
senses.why: This is the word's legal origin: the body is asked to answer a question for God.
senses.whyCN: 这是这个词的法律源头：让身体替神回答一个问题。

senses.title: An emotional trial
senses.definition: a period of fear, shame or grief that keeps the mind at full stretch
senses.definitionCN: 恐惧、羞耻或悲伤把心拉满的一段时间
senses.example: Waiting for the verdict was an ordeal of its own.
senses.exampleCN: 等待裁决本身就是一场煎熬。
senses.why: The word does not require a body; the mind can be tested alone.
senses.whyCN: 这个词不要求身体在场；心也可以独自受审。

senses.title: A medical trial
senses.definition: the pain and fatigue of treatment rather than of the illness
senses.definitionCN: 来自治疗而非疾病本身的疼痛与疲惫
senses.example: The treatment was an ordeal, and she counted the days.
senses.exampleCN: 治疗是一场折磨，她一天天数着。
senses.why: Modern medicine gives the word a new home, where cure and suffering arrive together.
senses.whyCN: 现代医学给这个词一个新住处：治愈与痛苦一起来。

senses.title: The ordeal of waiting
senses.definition: the special strain of a time in which nothing can be done
senses.definitionCN: 一段什么也做不了的时间特有的紧绷
senses.example: The three days before the result were pure ordeal.
senses.exampleCN: 结果出来前那三天，纯粹是煎熬。
senses.why: Helplessness is the active ingredient; waiting is only its form.
senses.whyCN: 无助才是有效成分；等待只是它的形状。

senses.title: A rite one must pass
senses.definition: a hard passage that marks entry into a group or a new stage
senses.definitionCN: 标示进入某群体或新阶段的艰难通行
senses.example: The first winter served as the young doctor's ordeal.
senses.exampleCN: 第一个冬天成了这位年轻医生的过关磨难。
senses.why: The word can be almost neutral here: the pain is the price of belonging.
senses.whyCN: 这里的词近乎中性：痛苦是归属的价钱。

intro.en: Ordeal began as a word for judgement, then narrowed to one kind of judgement done to the body.
intro.cn: ordeal 起初是「判决」的词，后来收窄为对身体的某一种判决。

items.en: Ordælan meant 'to deal out, to allot', and also 'to judge' a case.
items.cn: ordælan 意为「分派、分配」，也意为「审判」一桩案件。

items.en: Ordæl meant 'a judgement, a verdict, a fate dealt out'.
items.cn: ordæl 意为「判决、裁决、分派给某人的命运」。

items.en: Medieval law used the word for tests by fire or water, which left the verdict to God.
items.cn: 中世纪法律用这个词指火判与水判，把裁决留给神。

items.en: By the seventeenth century any severe trial could be called an ordeal, with no court involved.
items.cn: 到十七世纪，任何严峻考验都可称为 ordeal，与法庭无关。

items.en: Today the word covers illness, waiting, grief and long processes of every kind.
items.cn: 今天这个词涵盖疾病、等待、悲伤与各种漫长的过程。

note.en: The look-alike group keeps the ord- sound; the near-meaning group separates testing, suffering and length.
note.cn: 形近组保留 ord- 的读音；近义组把「考验」「受苦」与「漫长」分开。

entries.definition: a test of strength or patience.

normalIntro.en: The hooks keep the picture of a dark room one has to walk all the way through.
normalIntro.cn: 以下联想留住「必须从头走穿的一间黑屋」的画面。

normal.en: Ordeal comes from an old word for a verdict: a fate dealt out, not chosen.
normal.cn: ordeal 来自一个意为「裁决」的古词：命运是被分派的，不是自己选的。

normal.en: Think of a corridor with no light at either end.
normal.cn: 想象一条两端都没有光的走廊。

normal.en: Or-deal: a bad deal handed to you by the day.
normal.cn: or-deal：日子分给你的一笔坏交易。

normal.en: Say aw-DEEL; the long vowel stretches like the hours inside it.
normal.cn: 读成 aw-DEEL，长元音像里面那些被拉长的小时。

normal.en: Pair it with survive: one survives an ordeal, one does not enjoy it.
normal.cn: 把它和 survive 配对：人熬过 ordeal，而不是享受它。

abstract.en: An ordeal is measured from the inside; from the outside it may look like an ordinary week.
abstract.cn: 磨难度量于内；从外面看，它可能只是一个普通的一周。

abstract.en: The old word for judgement survives in the modern sense: something is still deciding what you are.
abstract.cn: 古老「判决」义活在现代义里：仍有东西在裁定你是什么样的人。

abstract.en: What makes an ordeal is not the event but the absence of any way to hurry it.
abstract.cn: 造成煎熬的不是事件，而是没有任何办法催它快点。

examples.en: The operation lasted nine hours and was an ordeal for the family.
examples.cn: 手术持续九小时，对家人是一场煎熬。

examples.en: The three days before the result were pure ordeal.
examples.cn: 结果出来前那三天，纯粹是煎熬。

examples.en: In the old accounts, the accused walked over hot iron in an ordeal.
examples.cn: 在旧记载里，被控者要在神判中走过烧红的铁。

dict_mnemonic.text: or（古英语「裁决」）+ deal（分派）：命运分派给你的一份苦，就是「磨难」。

root: 古英语 ordǣl（判决、命运），源自动词 ordǣlan（分派、审判）

sensesIntro.en: The eight senses run from a court of God to a hospital corridor: a test, a pain, a length, a fire, a fear, a cure, a wait and a passage.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从神的法庭一路走到医院走廊：考验、疼痛、漫长、火、恐惧、治疗、等待与过关。

core.en: THE DARK ROOM ONE MUST WALK THROUGH

branches.en: A test of endurance and a fear that tests without a body.
branches.cn: 对承受力的考验，以及无需身体在场的恐惧考验。

branches.en: Pain endured and pain given by treatment.
branches.cn: 承受的痛苦与治疗带来的痛苦。

branches.en: Length as weight, and waiting as the purest form of it.
branches.cn: 以长为重，以及作为其最纯粹形态的等待。

branches.en: The historical judgement left to fire and water.
branches.cn: 留给火与水的历史裁决。

branches.en: A hard passage that admits a person into something.
branches.cn: 把人送入某处的艰难通行。

intro.en: The ord- family is about ordering and allotting: order arranges, ordain appoints, ordeal hands out a fate.
intro.cn: ord- 词族关乎排序与分派：order 安排，ordain 任命，ordeal 分派命运。

latinIntro.en: English kept its own word here; the Latin entries below are the neighbouring vocabulary of lot and judgement, not the source.
latinIntro.cn: 这里英语保留了自己的词；下面这些拉丁条目是「命运」与「审判」的邻近词汇，而不是它的来源。

definition_zh: 正统的；正宗的；传统的
definition_en: following the accepted or officially correct set of beliefs and methods
core_image: 一条被无数脚踩得发亮的旧路，所有脚印都朝着同一个方向
scene: 学校里只教这一种写法，别的写法一律算错。The school teaches only one way to write it, and every other way is marked wrong, so the method has become orthodox.
sceneCN: 这里 orthodox 指公认的正统做法（第 3 个义项：公认方法）；句意为学校只教这一种写法，别的都算错，这套方法已成正统。

senses.title: Correct in doctrine
senses.definition: holding the beliefs that a church has declared correct
senses.definitionCN: 持守教会宣告为正确的信仰
senses.example: The council ruled that his teaching was not orthodox.
senses.exampleCN: 会议裁定他的教导不合正统。
senses.why: The word was born in religious argument, where correct opinion had a single judge.
senses.whyCN: 这个词生于宗教争论，那里的「正确意见」只有一个裁判。

senses.title: Conventional in belief
senses.definition: believing what most people in one's circle believe
senses.definitionCN: 相信自己所处圈子里多数人所信的
senses.example: It was orthodox in that town to distrust the railway.
senses.exampleCN: 在那个镇上，不信任铁路是正统观念。
senses.why: Here the judge is no longer a church but a crowd.
senses.whyCN: 这里的裁判不再是教会，而是人群。

senses.title: The accepted method
senses.definition: the way of doing something that a profession treats as standard
senses.definitionCN: 某个行业视为标准的做法
senses.example: Surgery by keyhole is now orthodox for this operation.
senses.exampleCN: 这种手术如今以微创为正统做法。
senses.why: Practice, not doctrine, decides what is orthodox here.
senses.whyCN: 这里决定正统的是实践，而不是教义。

senses.title: Mainstream medicine
senses.definition: the medicine taught in universities and tested in trials, as against alternatives
senses.definitionCN: 大学所教、经试验检验的医学，与替代疗法相对
senses.example: She tried orthodox treatment before the herbal one.
senses.exampleCN: 她先试正统治疗，再试草药。
senses.why: The word draws a line, and the line is drawn by institutions.
senses.whyCN: 这个词画一条线，而线由机构来画。

senses.title: Traditional in art
senses.definition: following the established forms of a tradition rather than breaking them
senses.definitionCN: 沿袭传统的既定形式而不去打破
senses.example: His early work was orthodox, and only later did he loosen the line.
senses.exampleCN: 他早期作品很传统，后来才放松线条。
senses.why: In art the word can be faint praise: correct, and a little late.
senses.whyCN: 在艺术里，这个词可能是淡淡的贬意：正确，却晚了一步。

senses.title: Mainstream in policy
senses.definition: the economic or political thinking that the powerful currently accept
senses.definitionCN: 当权者目前接受的经济或政治思路
senses.example: Orthodox economics predicted a quick recovery.
senses.exampleCN: 主流经济学预测会迅速复苏。
senses.why: What is orthodox in one decade is often heterodox in the next.
senses.whyCN: 一个十年的正统，常常是下一个十年的异端。

senses.title: Conforming in behaviour
senses.definition: behaving in the way that is expected, without surprise
senses.definitionCN: 以别人期待的方式行事，不出意外
senses.example: He led an orthodox life and was never mentioned in the papers.
senses.exampleCN: 他过着循规蹈矩的生活，从未上过报纸。
senses.why: The word moves from ideas to habits, and loses most of its edge.
senses.whyCN: 这个词从观念移到习惯，也失去了大部分锋芒。

senses.title: Strictly by the book
senses.definition: keeping every detail of an established rule, even where it costs
senses.definitionCN: 连细节都守住既定规则，即使要付代价
senses.example: The monastery remained orthodox even about the hour of prayer.
senses.exampleCN: 那座修道院连祈祷的时辰都严守正统。
senses.why: Here correctness is exact and expensive, which is why the word can sound severe.
senses.whyCN: 这里的正确精确而昂贵，所以这个词听起来可以很严厉。

intro.en: Orthodox joins a Greek word for straight to a Greek word for opinion: right belief, judged by whoever holds the straight line.
intro.cn: orthodox 把一个意为「直」的希腊词与一个意为「意见」的希腊词接起来：正确信念，由握着那条直线的人来判定。

items.en: Orthos meant 'straight, upright, correct', the same idea that gives English orthodontics.
items.cn: orthos 意为「直的、正的、正确的」，与英语 orthodontics 里的概念相同。

items.en: Doxa meant 'opinion, what seems true', a weaker word than knowledge.
items.cn: doxa 意为「意见、看来如此」，比「知识」弱。

items.en: Orthodoxos meant 'of right opinion', first used of Christian teachers who held the accepted faith.
items.cn: orthodoxos 意为「意见正确的」，最初用于持守公认信仰的基督教教师。

items.en: English took the word in the sixteenth century, during arguments about the Reformation.
items.cn: 英语在十六世纪宗教改革争论中借入此词。

items.en: Modern English applies it to medicine, economics and art, wherever a profession has a standard.
items.cn: 现代英语把它用于医学、经济学与艺术，凡是行业有标准的地方。

note.en: The look-alike group keeps the ortho- prefix; the near-meaning group separates belief, custom, mainstream and doctrine.
note.cn: 形近组保留 ortho- 前缀；近义组把「信念」「习俗」「主流」与「教义」分开。

normalIntro.en: The hooks keep the picture of a worn path whose ruts all run one way.
normalIntro.cn: 以下联想留住「一条磨亮的旧路，车辙都朝同一方向」的画面。

normal.en: Ortho- means straight: orthodox is a straight opinion, the one that does not lean off the line.
normal.cn: ortho- 意为「直」：orthodox 是「直的意见」，不偏线的那一种。

normal.en: Think of a path worn bright by everyone walking the same way.
normal.cn: 想象一条被众人同向踩亮的路径。

normal.en: Ortho-dox: straight plus opinion, the two Greek pieces are both visible in the spelling.
normal.cn: ortho-dox：直加意见，两个希腊部件在拼写里都看得见。

normal.en: Say AW-thuh-doks; the first syllable carries the straight line.
normal.cn: 读成 AW-thuh-doks，第一个音节带着那条直线。

normal.en: Pair it with unorthodox: the prefix simply steps off the path.
normal.cn: 把它和 unorthodox 配对：前缀只是从路上迈开一步。

abstract.en: Orthodoxy is a choice that has forgotten it was a choice.
abstract.cn: 正统是一个忘了自己曾是选择的决定。

abstract.en: Every profession draws its own straight line, and calls the line correct.
abstract.cn: 每个行业都画出自己的直线，并把那条线叫作正确。

abstract.en: To be orthodox is safe and slightly late; to be unorthodox is to pay for the earlier step.
abstract.cn: 正统是安全而略晚；非正统是为早迈的那一步付账。

examples.en: The school teaches one way to write it, and the method has become orthodox.
examples.cn: 学校只教一种写法，这套方法已成正统。

examples.en: Surgery by keyhole is now orthodox for this operation.
examples.cn: 这种手术如今以微创为正统做法。

examples.en: Orthodox economics predicted a quick recovery.
examples.cn: 主流经济学预测会迅速复苏。

dict_mnemonic.text: ortho（正）+ dox（意见）：持有正确意见的，就是「正统的」。

root: 希腊语 orthodoxos（意见正确的），由 orthos（正）与 doxa（意见）构成

sensesIntro.en: The eight senses all place a straight line somewhere: in a creed, a town, a trade, a clinic, a studio, a ministry, a habit and a monastery.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都在某处画一条直线：信条里、小镇里、行业里、诊所里、画室里、部里、习惯里与修道院里。

core.en: THE WORN PATH EVERYONE FOLLOWS
core.cn: 所有人都在走的那条磨亮的旧路

chain: THE RULE FORGETS IT WAS A CHOICE

branches.en: A creed held exactly and a rule kept to the letter.
branches.cn: 严格持守的信条与守到字句的规则。

branches.en: A town's common belief and a life lived without surprise.
branches.cn: 小镇的共同信念与不出意外的人生。

branches.en: A trade's standard method and a clinic's approved cure.
branches.cn: 行业的标准做法与诊所认可的治疗。

branches.en: Tradition followed in art until it becomes faint praise.
branches.cn: 艺术中沿袭传统，直到它变成淡淡的褒贬。

branches.en: The thinking the powerful currently accept.
branches.cn: 当权者目前接受的思路。

intro.en: The ortho- family means straight: orthodox is a straight opinion, orthodontics straight teeth, orthography straight writing.
intro.cn: ortho- 词族意为「直」：orthodox 是直的意见，orthodontics 是直牙，orthography 是正写法。

latinIntro.en: Greek orthos supplies the line and doxa supplies the opinion; the opposite prefix hetero- supplies the other opinion.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊语 orthos 提供直线，doxa 提供意见；相反的前缀 hetero- 提供另一种意见。

definition_zh: 渗透；潜移默化；逐渐吸收
definition_en: the slow passing of something through a thin boundary, or the quiet way a person takes in what surrounds him
core_image: 水隔着薄薄一层膜慢慢渗过去，到最后两边一样咸
scene: 他在那间厨房待了三年，没学过菜谱，手艺却自己长了出来。He spent three years in that kitchen and never studied a recipe, yet the craft came to him by osmosis.
sceneCN: 这里 osmosis 指潜移默化的吸收（第 2 个义项：潜移默化的学习）；句意为他在厨房待了三年，没学菜谱，手艺却自己长了出来。

pos.zh: 渗透；潜移默化；逐渐吸收

senses.title: Physical osmosis
senses.definition: the movement of a liquid through a thin membrane toward the stronger solution
senses.definitionCN: 液体穿过薄膜、流向浓度更高一侧的运动
senses.example: Water crossed the membrane by osmosis until both sides matched.
senses.exampleCN: 水靠渗透穿过薄膜，直到两侧浓度相同。
senses.why: The core picture is a wall that water can pass but salt cannot.
senses.whyCN: 核心画面是一堵水能过、盐不能过的墙。

senses.title: Absorbing knowledge quietly
senses.definition: taking in a skill or body of knowledge by being near it rather than by study
senses.definitionCN: 靠身处其中而不是靠研习来吸收技能或知识
senses.example: He learned the kitchen by osmosis, watching and never asking.
senses.exampleCN: 他靠耳濡目染学会厨房里的活，只是看，从不问。
senses.why: The metaphor keeps the membrane: knowledge crosses a boundary without being poured.
senses.whyCN: 这个比喻保留了那层膜：知识穿过边界，而不是被灌进去。

senses.title: Passive uptake
senses.definition: receiving an attitude or habit without choosing to
senses.definitionCN: 未经选择地接收一种态度或习惯
senses.example: She absorbed the family's caution by osmosis and never noticed.
senses.exampleCN: 她不知不觉吸收了家里的谨慎，自己从未察觉。
senses.why: Here the word describes what happens when nobody is teaching.
senses.whyCN: 这里描述的是没有人在教时发生的事。

senses.title: Diffusion of ideas
senses.definition: the gradual spread of an idea through a group until it seems native there
senses.definitionCN: 观念在群体中逐渐扩散，直到像本来就长在那里
senses.example: The new vocabulary entered the office by osmosis, one meeting at a time.
senses.exampleCN: 新词汇靠渗透进入办公室，一次会议渗一点。
senses.why: Groups, like membranes, let some things through faster than others.
senses.whyCN: 群体像膜一样，让某些东西过得比别人快。

senses.title: Subtle influence
senses.definition: the slow permeation of a place or person by an outside influence
senses.definitionCN: 外来影响缓慢渗入一个地方或一个人
senses.example: The city changed by osmosis, street by street, without a single decree.
senses.exampleCN: 这座城市靠浸润改变，一条街一条街地变，没有一道法令。
senses.why: The word is useful when no cause can be pointed to, only a drift.
senses.whyCN: 当指不出原因、只看到漂移时，这个词就派上用场。

senses.title: Biological membrane exchange
senses.definition: the exchange of water and solutes across cell membranes in living tissue
senses.definitionCN: 活组织中水与溶质跨细胞膜的交换
senses.example: Roots depend on osmosis to pull water from the soil.
senses.exampleCN: 根靠渗透从土壤里吸水。
senses.why: Biology uses the word literally, and the metaphor borrows its patience.
senses.whyCN: 生物学按字面使用这个词，比喻借走的是它的耐心。

senses.title: Social assimilation
senses.definition: the process by which a newcomer slowly takes on a group's ways
senses.definitionCN: 新来者慢慢接受一个群体行事方式的过程
senses.example: The new clerk was assimilated by osmosis long before the training ended.
senses.exampleCN: 新职员在培训结束前很久就已经被同化了。
senses.why: People, too, are semi-permeable; the group enters by degrees.
senses.whyCN: 人也是半透的；群体是一点一点进来的。

senses.title: Doing something without knowing how
senses.definition: the casual phrase for knowing a thing one was never formally taught
senses.definitionCN: 对未曾正式学过却会做某事的一种随口说法
senses.example: Ask him the rule and he cannot tell you; he knows it by osmosis.
senses.exampleCN: 问他规则他说不出来；他是不知不觉学会的。
senses.why: Used loosely, the word admits that the learning had no syllabus.
senses.whyCN: 松散用法下，这个词承认这份学习没有教学大纲。

intro.en: Osmosis was coined by nineteenth-century science from a Greek word for a push: the liquid is not poured, it is pressed through.
intro.cn: osmosis 由十九世纪科学用一个意为「推」的希腊词造出：液体不是被倒过去，而是被推过去。

items.en: Osmos meant 'a push, an impulse', the pressure that starts the movement.
items.cn: osmos 意为「推、冲动」，是启动这一运动的压力。

items.en: The suffix -osis named a process or condition, as in osmosis or diagnosis.
items.cn: 后缀 -osis 命名一种过程或状态，如 osmosis 与 diagnosis。

items.en: Nineteenth-century chemists needed a word for water rising through a membrane, and built it from these pieces.
items.cn: 十九世纪化学家需要为水穿过薄膜上升的现象造词，便用了这两个部件。

items.en: The word stayed technical until teachers borrowed it for learning that happens without lessons.
items.cn: 这个词一直技术化，直到教师们借它来描述没有课程的学习。

items.en: Today 'by osmosis' is a common phrase for absorbing a culture, an accent or a habit.
items.cn: 今天 by osmosis 是常用说法，指吸收一种文化、口音或习惯。

note.en: The look-alike group is the osm- family; the near-meaning group separates diffusion, permeation and plain absorption.
