note.cn: 形近组是 osm- 词族；近义组把「扩散」「渗入」与「吸收」分开。

entries.definition: more than one instance of osmosis.
to pass or absorb by osmosis.
the spreading of particles or ideas.
a slow entry into a group or place.
entries.definitionCN: 缓慢进入某群体或场所。

normalIntro.en: The hooks keep the picture of water rising through a thin skin until both sides are the same.
normalIntro.cn: 以下联想留住「水穿过一层薄皮上升，直到两边一样」的画面。

normal.en: Osmosis starts with osmos, a push: nothing is poured, everything is pressed.
normal.cn: osmosis 起于 osmos（推）：没有被倒进去的东西，全是被推进去的。

normal.en: Think of a bladder of brine in fresh water, slowly swelling.
normal.cn: 想象一只装盐水的囊泡放在淡水里，慢慢胀起来。

normal.en: Oz-mosis: the first syllable sounds like 'oz', a slow drip through a wall.
normal.cn: oz-mosis：第一个音节像 oz，一滴一滴穿过墙。

normal.en: Say oz-MOH-sis; the long o is the slow part of the process.
normal.cn: 读成 oz-MOH-sis，那个长 o 就是过程中慢的那一段。

normal.en: Pair it with by: things learned by osmosis were never formally taught.
normal.cn: 把它和 by 配对：by osmosis 学到的东西从不曾被正式教授。

abstract.en: Osmosis is how a culture gets into a person without a lesson plan.
abstract.cn: 潜移默化是文化不经课程就进入一个人的方式。

abstract.en: The membrane matters: what passes is not everything, only what the wall allows.
abstract.cn: 膜是要紧的：过的不是全部，只是墙允许的那部分。

abstract.en: Slow is the point; anything fast enough to notice is called teaching.
abstract.cn: 慢是重点；快到能被注意到的，就叫教学。

examples.en: He spent three years in that kitchen and the craft came to him by osmosis.
examples.cn: 他在厨房待了三年，手艺不知不觉就长了出来。

examples.en: Water crossed the membrane by osmosis until both sides matched.
examples.cn: 水靠渗透穿过薄膜，直到两侧相同。

examples.en: The new vocabulary entered the office by osmosis, one meeting at a time.
examples.cn: 新词汇靠潜移默化进入办公室，一次会议渗一点。

dict_mnemonic.text: os（推）+ mosis（过程）：水被推着穿过薄膜，就是「渗透」。

root: 希腊语 ōsmos（推、推动），十九世纪科学加 -osis 造出 osmosis

sensesIntro.en: The eight senses all move something across a boundary: water through a membrane, a skill through a wall of habit, an idea through a group.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都把某物送过一道边界：水穿过膜、手艺穿过习惯的墙、观念穿过一个群体。

core.en: WATER CROSSING A THIN WALL

branches.en: The literal passage of water in a lab and in a cell.
branches.cn: 实验室与细胞里水的字面通过。

branches.en: A skill taken in by nearness and an attitude taken in without choice.
branches.cn: 靠近而得的技能与无从选择而得的态度。

branches.en: An idea spreading through a group and an influence entering a city.
branches.cn: 观念穿过群体与影响进入城市。

branches.en: A newcomer slowly becoming one of the group.
branches.cn: 新来者慢慢成为群体一员。

branches.en: The loose phrase for knowing without having been taught.
branches.cn: 未曾受教却知道的松散说法。

intro.en: The osm- family is about pushing through: osmosis passes, osmotic describes the passing, endosmosis pushes in and exosmosis pushes out.
intro.cn: osm- 词族关乎推过去：osmosis 是过程，osmotic 描述这个过程，endosmosis 推入，exosmosis 推出。

latinIntro.en: Greek osmos is the push and -osis is the process; the prefixes endo- and exo- decide which side the water enters from.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊语 osmos 是那一下推，-osis 是过程；前缀 endo- 与 exo- 决定水从哪一边进。

items.example: The syrup osmosed into the fruit.
He needs dialysis twice a week.

definition_zh: 排斥；放逐；孤立
definition_en: the act of shutting a person out of a group, so that no one will speak to or deal with him
core_image: 一圈人站成环，把一个人留在圈外，地上那道线谁也不肯跨过去
scene: 他因为说了真话，被整条街的人不再打招呼，连杂货店都懒得找零。Because he had told the truth, the whole street stopped greeting him, and even the grocer could not be bothered to give change, a quiet ostracism.
sceneCN: 这里 ostracism 指社会排斥（第 1 个义项：社会排斥）；句意为他说了真话后，整条街的人不再打招呼，连杂货店也懒得找零，这是一种无声的排斥。

senses.title: Social exclusion
senses.definition: the condition of being kept outside a group that once included you
senses.definitionCN: 被留在曾经接纳自己的群体之外的状态
senses.example: The ostracism began with silence at the school gate.
senses.exampleCN: 这种排斥从校门口的沉默开始。
senses.why: The word's force is collective: many people each do a little nothing.
senses.whyCN: 这个词的力量是集体的：许多人各自做了一点点「什么都不做」。

senses.title: Athenian ostracism
senses.definition: the ancient Athenian vote by which a citizen could be sent away for ten years
senses.definitionCN: 古雅典以投票把公民放逐十年的制度
senses.example: Under Athenian ostracism, a name scratched on a potshard could end a career.
senses.exampleCN: 在雅典的陶片放逐中，刻在陶片上一个名字就能终结一段仕途。
senses.why: The original is political and procedural, not merely social.
senses.whyCN: 原初义项是政治的、程序的，不只是社交的。

senses.title: Deliberate shunning
senses.definition: an organised refusal to speak to or deal with a person
senses.definitionCN: 有组织地拒绝与某人说话或往来
senses.example: The village practised ostracism against the family for a season.
senses.exampleCN: 村里人对那家人施行了一季的回避。
senses.why: Shunning is the everyday engine of ostracism; no law is needed.
senses.whyCN: 回避是排斥的日常引擎；不需要任何法律。

senses.title: Workplace exclusion
senses.definition: the quiet removal of a colleague from meetings, decisions and talk
senses.definitionCN: 把同事悄悄移出会议、决策与谈话
senses.example: His ostracism at the firm was never written down.
senses.exampleCN: 他在公司里被孤立，从未被写进任何文件。
senses.why: Modern institutions ostracize by omission rather than decree.
senses.whyCN: 现代机构靠遗漏而非命令来排斥。

senses.title: Political exclusion
senses.definition: the pushing of a rival out of influence while keeping the forms intact
senses.definitionCN: 在保留形式的同时把对手挤出影响力
senses.example: The party used ostracism instead of expulsion.
senses.exampleCN: 该党用排挤代替开除。
senses.why: Here the group keeps its rules and still removes the person.
senses.whyCN: 这里群体保留规则，却仍然移除了那个人。

senses.title: A child left out
senses.definition: the playground practice of excluding one child from every game
senses.definitionCN: 操场上把某个孩子排除在所有游戏之外的作法
senses.example: Teachers now treat ostracism as a form of harm.
senses.exampleCN: 教师如今把孤立视为一种伤害。
senses.why: Small groups rehearse the same politics with smaller stakes.
senses.whyCN: 小群体用更小的代价排练同样的政治。

senses.title: Cultural exclusion
senses.definition: the refusal of a community to count a person or practice as its own
senses.definitionCN: 一个社群拒绝把某人或某种做法算作自己的
senses.example: The ostracism of the dialect lasted two generations.
senses.exampleCN: 对方言的排斥持续了两代人。
senses.why: Cultures can ostracize a whole way of speaking, not only a speaker.
senses.whyCN: 文化可以排斥一整套说话方式，而不只是排斥某个人。

senses.title: Rejection of ideas
senses.definition: the refusal to admit a view into respectable discussion
senses.definitionCN: 拒绝让某种看法进入体面的讨论
senses.example: The ostracism of the theory was slow and complete.
senses.exampleCN: 对那个理论的排斥缓慢而彻底。
senses.why: Ideas are ostracized by the same silence that removes people.
senses.whyCN: 观念被排斥，靠的是移除人时那种同样的沉默。

intro.en: Ostracism is a word made of potsherds: the Athenians wrote a name on a broken piece of pottery and counted the pieces.
intro.cn: ostracism 是一个由陶片构成的词：雅典人把名字写在碎陶片上，然后数陶片。

items.en: Ostrakon meant 'a shell or a potsherd', the cheap material used for a vote.
items.cn: ostrakon 意为「贝壳或陶片」，是投票用的廉价材料。

items.en: Ostrakizein meant 'to vote by potsherd', hence 'to send a man out of the city'.
items.cn: ostrakizein 意为「用陶片投票」，因此意为「把一个人送出城」。

items.en: Ostrakismos named the institution itself, the ten-year exile decided by a majority of shards.
items.cn: ostrakismos 命名制度本身：由多数陶片决定的十年放逐。

items.en: English borrowed ostracism in the seventeenth century, first as a classical curiosity.
items.cn: 英语在十七世纪借入 ostracism，最初是作为古典典故。

items.en: Modern usage widened it from a vote to any group's refusal to keep a member.
items.cn: 现代用法把它从投票扩展到任何群体对成员的拒绝。

note.en: The look-alike group is the ostrakon family; the near-meaning group separates exclusion, shunning, exile and banishment.
note.cn: 形近组是 ostrakon 词族；近义组把「排斥」「回避」「流放」与「放逐」分开。

entries.definition: to shut a person out of a group.
entries.definitionCN: 把某人排斥在群体之外。

entries.definition: in the act of shutting out.
the act of keeping someone out.

normalIntro.en: The hooks keep the picture of a ring of people and one gap nobody will close.
normalIntro.cn: 以下联想留住「一圈人和一道谁都不肯补上的缺口」的画面。

normal.en: Ostracism holds ostrakon, a potsherd: the Athenians voted a man out with broken pottery.
normal.cn: ostracism 里藏着 ostrakon（陶片）：雅典人用碎陶片把一个人投出去。

normal.en: Think of a circle of chairs with one chair pushed outside the line.
normal.cn: 想象一圈椅子，其中一把被推到线外。

normal.en: Os-tra-cism: the middle sounds like 'trace', the line on the ground no one crosses.
normal.cn: os-tra-cism：中间听起来像 trace，地上那道没人越过的线。

normal.en: Say OS-truh-siz-um; the first syllable is the group, the rest is the pushing out.
normal.cn: 读成 OS-truh-siz-um，第一个音节是群体，其余是把人推出去。

normal.en: Pair it with silence: ostracism is mostly done by not speaking.
normal.cn: 把它和 silence 配对：排斥多半是靠不说话完成的。

abstract.en: Ostracism needs no enemy, only a majority that finds it easier to stay quiet.
abstract.cn: 排斥不需要敌人，只需要一个觉得沉默更省事的多数。

abstract.en: It is the punishment a group gives for the crime of making it uncomfortable.
abstract.cn: 这是群体对「让它不舒服」这一罪名的惩罚。

abstract.en: The old potsherd and the modern cold shoulder do the same work: they count the person out.
abstract.cn: 古老陶片与现代冷遇做的是同一件事：把人从数里减去。

examples.en: Because he had told the truth, the whole street stopped greeting him, a quiet ostracism.
examples.cn: 因为他说了真话，整条街的人不再打招呼，这是一种无声的排斥。

examples.en: Under Athenian ostracism, a name on a potsherd could end a career.
examples.cn: 在雅典的陶片放逐中，陶片上的一个名字就能终结一段仕途。

examples.en: The ostracism of the theory was slow and complete.
examples.cn: 对那个理论的排斥缓慢而彻底。

dict_mnemonic.text: ostracon（陶片）+ ism（制度）：雅典人用陶片投票把人放逐，就是「排斥」。

root: 希腊语 ostrakismos（陶片放逐），源自 ostrakon（陶片、贝壳）

sensesIntro.en: The eight senses all draw a line around a group: a city, a street, a firm, a party, a playground, a culture and a field of study.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都在群体周围画一道线：一座城、一条街、一家公司、一个政党、一片操场、一种文化与一个学科。

core.en: A RING OF PEOPLE WITH ONE GAP

branches.en: The condition of exclusion and the daily practice of shunning.
branches.cn: 被排斥的状态与日常回避的做法。

branches.en: The Athenian vote that started the word.
branches.cn: 开启这个词的雅典投票。

branches.en: A colleague removed quietly and a rival pushed aside.
branches.cn: 被悄悄移出的同事与被挤到一边的对手。

branches.en: A child left out and a dialect refused.
branches.cn: 被排除的孩子与被拒绝的方言。

branches.en: A view kept out of respectable talk.
branches.cn: 被挡在体面讨论之外的看法。

intro.en: The ostrakon family is about shells and shards: ostracism was a vote, ostracize the act, ostracon the material.
intro.cn: ostrakon 词族关乎贝壳与碎片：ostracism 是制度，ostracize 是行为，ostracon 是材料。

latinIntro.en: Greek ostrakon gives the material and ostrakizein gives the action; the suffix -ismos names the institution.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊语 ostrakon 提供材料，ostrakizein 提供动作，后缀 -ismos 命名制度。

items.example: Ostracism removed him for ten years.
items.exampleCN: 陶片放逐把他逐出十年。
每片陶片写着一个名字。

definition_zh: 他者性；异质感；与他人的差异
definition_en: the quality of being different from oneself or from the group, especially as something felt rather than measured
core_image: 镜子里的人和你几乎一模一样，却确定不是你
scene: 她在这条街上住了二十年，邻居仍用「外地人」三个字介绍她，那种异样感从未消失。She had lived on the street for twenty years, and the neighbours still introduced her as the outsider, a sense of otherness that never faded.
sceneCN: 这里 otherness 指被当作外人的异质感（第 4 个义项：被当作外人）；句意为她住了二十年，邻居仍称她外地人，那种异样感从未消失。

derivatives.zh: 他者化；把他人标记为异类

senses.title: The state of being different
senses.definition: the condition of not being the same as what is here
senses.definitionCN: 与眼前之物不同的状态
senses.example: The otherness of the dialect was audible in the first word.
senses.exampleCN: 那种方言的相异，从第一个词就听得出来。
senses.why: The word is abstract on purpose: it names the gap, not the thing across it.
senses.whyCN: 这个词有意抽象：它命名的是缺口，而不是缺口那边的东西。

senses.title: A felt strangeness
senses.definition: the impression that something is alien, before one can say why
senses.definitionCN: 说不出理由就觉得某物陌生的印象
senses.example: The house had an otherness that no cleaning removed.
senses.exampleCN: 那栋房子有一种洗不掉的异样。
senses.why: Feeling comes before analysis; the word often reports a sensation first.
senses.whyCN: 感受先于分析；这个词常常先报告一种感觉。

senses.title: Philosophical otherness
senses.definition: the condition of the other, which a self knows only by not being it
senses.definitionCN: 他者的处境：自我只能通过「不是它」来认识它
senses.example: Philosophy speaks of otherness as what a self cannot absorb.
senses.exampleCN: 哲学把他者性说成自我无法吸收的东西。
senses.why: Here the word is a problem rather than a description.
senses.whyCN: 这里的词是一个问题，而不是一段描写。

senses.title: Being treated as an outsider
senses.definition: the position of a person a group marks as not one of us
senses.definitionCN: 被群体标为「不是我们的人」的处境
senses.example: Her otherness was decided by her accent, not by her passport.
senses.exampleCN: 她的异类身份由口音决定，而不是护照。
senses.why: The quality is assigned by others; one does not choose to have it.
senses.whyCN: 这种性质是由别人指派的，不是自己选的。

senses.title: Cultural difference
senses.definition: the distance between two ways of living, felt by those who meet
senses.definitionCN: 两种生活方式之间的距离，由相遇的人感受到
senses.example: The exhibition was about otherness, and the labels kept apologising.
senses.exampleCN: 展览讲的是文化差异，说明牌却一直在道歉。
senses.why: The word can be respectful or uneasy, depending on who is looking.
senses.whyCN: 这个词可以是尊重的，也可以是不安的，取决于看的人。

senses.title: Distance within a relationship
senses.definition: the part of a close person that remains unreachable
senses.definitionCN: 亲近之人身上仍无法抵达的那一部分
senses.example: Marriage did not remove the otherness between them.
senses.exampleCN: 婚姻没有消除他们之间的那点距离。
senses.why: Even intimacy leaves a remainder; the word names it without blaming anyone.
senses.whyCN: 再亲密也会留下剩余；这个词命名它，却不怪罪谁。

senses.title: Nature as other
senses.definition: the sense that the natural world is indifferent and not ours
senses.definitionCN: 感到自然界冷漠、并不属于我们的那种感觉
senses.example: The storm gave the coast a sudden otherness.
senses.exampleCN: 风暴让海岸突然显得陌生而不可亲。
senses.why: Nature is the classic other: it does not answer in our words.
senses.whyCN: 自然是经典的他者：它不用我们的语言回答。

senses.title: Othering as exclusion
senses.definition: the process by which a group turns difference into a reason to exclude
senses.definitionCN: 群体把差异变成排斥理由的过程
senses.example: The report criticised the otherness built into the admission system.
senses.exampleCN: 报告批评招生制度里被制造出来的异己化。
senses.why: Here the word is a critique: difference was made, not found.
senses.whyCN: 这里的词是一种批评：差异是被制造出来的，不是被发现的。

intro.en: Otherness is a plain English compound that was later asked to carry a philosophical load.
intro.cn: otherness 本是一个朴素的英语复合词，后来被要求承担哲学的重量。

items.en: Oþer meant 'the second of two, the other one', the everyday word for what is not this.
items.cn: oþer 意为「两个中的另一个」，是对「非此」的日常说法。

items.en: The suffix -ness turned adjectives into nouns of quality, as in kindness and darkness.
items.cn: 后缀 -ness 把形容词变成表性质的名词，如 kindness 与 darkness。

items.en: Nineteenth-century writers used otherness to render German ideas about the other of the self.
items.cn: 十九世纪作家用 otherness 翻译德语中关于自我之他者的观念。

items.en: Twentieth-century critics added othering, the act of marking a person as alien.
items.cn: 二十世纪批评家加上 othering，指把人标记为异类的行为。

items.en: Today it covers a child's unease, a culture's distance and a theory's critique of both.
items.cn: 今天它涵盖孩子的不安、文化的距离，以及理论对两者的批评。

note.en: The look-alike group is the other family; the near-meaning group separates difference, strangeness and alienation.
note.cn: 形近组是 other 词族；近义组把「差异」「陌生」与「疏离」分开。

entries.definition: not this one, but a different one.
the act of marking someone as alien.
entries.definitionCN: 把某人标记为异类的行为。

entries.definition: in another way or in other respects.
entries.definitionCN: 以别的方式；在其他方面。

entries.definition: the state of not being the same.

entries.definitionCN: 哲学上指他者性的术语。

entries.definition: the feeling of being cut off.

normalIntro.en: The hooks keep the picture of a face in the mirror that is almost yours.
normalIntro.cn: 以下联想留住「镜子里那张几乎和你一样的脸」的画面。

normal.en: Otherness is other plus ness, the quality of being not this.
normal.cn: otherness 是 other 加 ness，即「不是这个」的性质。

normal.en: Think of a mirror that shows a face one shade different from yours.
normal.cn: 想象一面镜子，里面的脸和你差了一点点。

normal.en: Other-ness: say the two parts separately and you hear the gap.
normal.cn: other-ness：把两部分分开念，就听见了那道缺口。

normal.en: Stress the first syllable: UTH-er-ness, the difference at the front.
normal.cn: 重读第一个音节：UTH-er-ness，差异就在词首。

normal.en: Pair it with othering: otherness is the state, othering is the act that produces it.
normal.cn: 把它和 othering 配对：otherness 是状态，othering 是制造它的行为。

abstract.en: Otherness is usually assigned, not discovered; someone decides where the line runs.
abstract.cn: 他者性多半是指派的，不是发现的；总有人决定线画在哪里。

abstract.en: The word is useful because it prefers the gap to the label.
abstract.cn: 这个词有用，因为它宁可说缺口，也不说标签。

abstract.en: Every group needs an outside; the question is whether it needs a person out there.
abstract.cn: 每个群体都需要外部；问题在于它是否需要真的有个人在外面。

examples.en: She had lived there for twenty years, and the sense of otherness never faded.
examples.cn: 她在那里住了二十年，那种异样感从未消失。

examples.en: Marriage did not remove the otherness between them.
examples.cn: 婚姻没有消除他们之间的那点距离。

examples.en: The storm gave the coast a sudden otherness.
examples.cn: 风暴让海岸突然显得陌生而不可亲。

dict_mnemonic.text: other（另一个）+ ness（性质）：作为「另一个」的性质，就是「他者性、异质感」。

root: 古英语 ōþer（另一个）加后缀 -ness，十九世纪起用于哲学与社会理论

sensesIntro.en: The eight senses all mark a gap: between a word and a dialect, a house and its visitor, a self and an other, a group and its outsider.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都在标出一道缺口：词与方言之间、房子与来客之间、自我与他者之间、群体与外人之间。

core.en: A FACE THAT IS ALMOST YOURS

branches.en: A plain difference and the feeling of it.
branches.cn: 朴素的差异与对这份差异的感受。

branches.en: A philosophical problem and the distance inside intimacy.
branches.cn: 哲学问题与亲密关系里的距离。

branches.en: A label given by a group and the process that gives it.
branches.cn: 群体给出的标签与给出标签的过程。

branches.en: Two ways of living meeting and measuring each other.
branches.cn: 两种生活方式相遇并彼此丈量。

branches.en: A world that does not answer in our words.
branches.cn: 一个不用我们的语言回答的世界。

intro.en: The other family is small and old: other, otherness, othering, otherwise, another and otherworldly all come from one Germanic word.
intro.cn: other 词族小而古老：other、otherness、othering、otherwise、another 与 otherworldly 都来自同一个日耳曼词。

latinIntro.en: This word is Germanic, not Latin; the Latin entries below are its neighbours in meaning, especially alter and alienus.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词是日耳曼语而非拉丁语；下面这些拉丁条目是它在意义上的邻居，尤其是 alter 与 alienus。

items.exampleCN: 他者化从一个标签开始。

items.example: They felt othered by the joke.
items.exampleCN: 那个玩笑让他们觉得自己是异类。

definition_zh: 被抛弃者；被逐出的人；流浪者
definition_en: a person whom a group has thrown out and will not take back
core_image: 一个人被推到城门外面，门在身后关上，他手里只有一只包袱
scene: 村里把他赶了出去，从此没人提他的名字，只有孩子会在夜里讲他的故事。The village drove him out and no one spoke his name again, so he lived as an outcast whom only children mentioned after dark.
sceneCN: 这里 outcast 指被逐出的人（第 1 个义项：被逐出的人）；句意为村里把他赶出去，从此无人提他的名字，他成了只有孩子夜里会说的弃儿。

senses.title: A person expelled
senses.definition: someone a community has driven out and forbidden to return
senses.definitionCN: 被社群赶出并禁止回来的人
senses.example: The village drove him out, and he lived as an outcast.
senses.exampleCN: 村里把他赶出去，他成了被逐出的人。
senses.why: The past participle is built into the noun: the casting has already happened.
senses.whyCN: 过去分词就长在这个名词里：那一下「扔出去」已经发生过了。

senses.title: A social outsider
senses.definition: a person who is present but never counted as one of the group
senses.definitionCN: 人在场，却从不被算作群体一员
senses.example: He was an outcast in the club he had helped to found.
senses.exampleCN: 在他帮忙创办的俱乐部里，他是个边缘人。
senses.why: One need not leave to be outside; the group can keep you at its edge.
senses.whyCN: 不必离开也可以在外部；群体可以把你留在边上。

senses.title: Rejected as an adjective
senses.definition: of a person or thing, refused and left without support
senses.definitionCN: 人或物被拒绝、无人支持
senses.example: The outcast dog waited at the same gate every morning.
senses.exampleCN: 那条被抛弃的狗每天早上都在同一道门口等。
senses.why: As an adjective the word carries the same verdict with less history.
senses.whyCN: 作形容词时，它带着同样的判决，却少了过程。

senses.title: A wanderer
senses.definition: a person with no fixed place, moving because no place will hold him
senses.definitionCN: 没有固定处所、因无处收留而移动的人
senses.example: Outcasts gathered at the edge of the market after closing.
senses.exampleCN: 收市之后，流浪者聚在集市边上。
senses.why: Movement is the visible sign of the earlier verdict.
senses.whyCN: 移动是那场早先判决的可见迹象。

senses.title: Expelled from a faith
senses.definition: a person a religious body has cut off from its rites and company
senses.definitionCN: 被宗教团体断绝仪式与往来的人
senses.example: The heretic was declared an outcast and his books burned.
senses.exampleCN: 那个异端被宣布为教门之外的人，著作被烧。
senses.why: Sacred communities have their own gate, and it closes the same way.
senses.whyCN: 神圣社群也有自己的门，关起来的方式一样。

senses.title: Cast out of a family
senses.definition: a relative whom the family has formally stopped acknowledging
senses.definitionCN: 被家族正式不再承认的亲属
senses.example: He died an outcast, and the family sent no flowers.
senses.exampleCN: 他死时是家族的弃儿，家里没送花。
senses.why: The smallest group hurts most because it was the first home.
senses.whyCN: 最小的群体伤得最重，因为那是最初的家。

senses.title: A political castaway
senses.definition: a figure pushed out of a party or a cause and left without allies
senses.definitionCN: 被挤出政党或事业、失去盟友的人物
senses.example: After the vote he was a political outcast with a good memory.
senses.exampleCN: 投票之后，他成了记性很好的政治弃儿。
senses.why: Politics produces outcasts faster than it produces exiles.
senses.whyCN: 政治制造弃儿的速度快于制造流亡者。

senses.title: The outcast as a figure
senses.definition: the stock character whose exclusion lets a story examine its own rules
senses.definitionCN: 被排斥的典型人物，借他的位置审视故事自身的规则
senses.example: The novel's outcast sees more clearly than its judge.
senses.exampleCN: 小说里的弃儿比审判者看得更清楚。
senses.why: Literature keeps the word because the outside is a good place to look from.
senses.whyCN: 文学保留这个词，因为外部是个好视角。

intro.en: Outcast is English made of two English pieces: to cast is to throw, and out is where the throw sends you.
intro.cn: outcast 由两个英语部件组成：cast 是扔，out 是扔去的方向。

items.en: Casten meant 'to throw, to fling', from Old Norse and related to the modern cast.
items.cn: casten 意为「扔、掷」，来自古诺斯语，与现代 cast 相关。

items.en: Out- added direction: to outcaste was to throw someone beyond the boundary.
items.cn: out- 加上方向：outcaste 就是把某人扔到界限之外。

items.en: By the fourteenth century the past participle had become a noun for the person thrown out.
items.cn: 到十四世纪，过去分词已变成指「被扔出去的人」的名词。

items.en: Nineteenth-century writing fixed the word in its sympathy for the excluded poor.
items.cn: 十九世纪文字把这个词固定在对被排除的穷人的同情里。

items.en: Today it covers family, party and schoolyard, wherever a gate is closed behind someone.
items.cn: 今天它涵盖家庭、政党与校园，凡是在某人身后关上门的地方。

note.en: The look-alike group keeps the cast; the near-meaning group separates the expelled, the exile and the merely rejected.
note.cn: 形近组保留 cast；近义组把「被逐出者」「流亡者」与「被拒绝者」分开。

entries.definition: a person expelled from a caste.
a person cast away at sea.
a person forced to live abroad.
a person with no fixed home.

normalIntro.en: The hooks keep the picture of a bundle left outside a gate that has just shut.
normalIntro.cn: 以下联想留住「城门刚关上，门外只剩一只包袱」的画面。

normal.en: Outcast is out plus cast: someone was thrown out, and the throw is in the name.
normal.cn: outcast 是 out 加 cast：有人被扔出去，那一下扔就在名字里。

normal.en: Think of a bag on the road and a door closing behind it.
normal.cn: 想象路上一只包袱，身后一扇门正在关上。

normal.en: Out-cast: say the two words and you see the throw.
normal.cn: out-cast：把两个词念出来，就看见那一下扔。

normal.en: Stress the first syllable: OUT-cast, the direction comes before the act.
normal.cn: 重读第一个音节：OUT-cast，方向先于动作。

normal.en: Pair it with gate: every outcast was made at a boundary someone else controlled.
normal.cn: 把它和 gate 配对：每个弃儿都是在别人控制的边界上被造出的。

abstract.en: An outcast is not a stranger; a stranger was never inside.
abstract.cn: 弃儿不是陌生人；陌生人从来没在里面待过。

abstract.en: The word remembers the hand that threw, which is why it sounds like an accusation.
abstract.cn: 这个词记得那只扔人的手，所以听起来像一项指控。

abstract.en: Groups make outcasts to show themselves where the line is.
abstract.cn: 群体制造弃儿，是为了给自己看清线在哪里。

examples.en: The village drove him out, and he lived as an outcast.
examples.cn: 村里把他赶出去，他成了被逐出的人。

examples.en: He was an outcast in the club he had helped to found.
examples.cn: 在他帮忙创办的俱乐部里，他是个边缘人。

examples.en: The novel's outcast sees more clearly than its judge.
examples.cn: 小说里的弃儿比审判者看得更清楚。

dict_mnemonic.text: out（在外）+ cast（扔）：被扔到外面的人，就是「被抛弃者、弃儿」。

root: 中古英语 outcasten（扔出去），由 out 与 casten（扔）构成

sensesIntro.en: The eight senses all stand outside a different gate: a village, a club, a home, a road, a church, a family, a party and a story.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都站在不同的一道门外：村庄、俱乐部、家、道路、教会、家族、政党与一个故事。

core.en: A BUNDLE AT THE CITY GATE

branches.en: A person expelled and the adjective that follows him.
branches.cn: 被逐出的人与跟着他的那个形容词。

branches.en: An outsider kept at the edge and a relative no longer acknowledged.
branches.cn: 被留在边上的外人与不再被承认的亲属。

branches.en: The wanderer for whom no place will open.
branches.cn: 无处肯为他开门的流浪者。

branches.en: A faith's gate and a party's gate, closed the same way.
branches.cn: 教会的门与政党的门，以同样的方式关上。

branches.en: The literary figure whose outside view the story needs.
branches.cn: 故事需要其外部视角的文学形象。

intro.en: The cast family is about throwing: outcast is thrown out, broadcast is thrown wide, forecast is thrown ahead.
intro.cn: cast 词族关乎扔：outcast 被扔出去，broadcast 扔向四方，forecast 扔向前方。

latinIntro.en: The word is Germanic; the Latin entries below are neighbours in meaning, where ex- and pro- do the throwing.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词是日耳曼语；下面这些拉丁条目是意义上的邻居，由 ex- 与 pro- 完成那一下扔。

items.exampleCN: 被逐出种姓者在别处找到活。

definition_zh: 过时的；老式的；被淘汰的
definition_en: no longer accepted because a newer way has replaced it
core_image: 衣柜深处挂着的一件旧外套，肩线宽得不像现在人穿的
scene: 办公室还在用那套二十年前的报销流程，年轻同事每次都笑。The office still runs the expense system it bought twenty years ago, and the younger staff laugh at how outmoded it is.
sceneCN: 这里 outmoded 指方法陈旧（第 3 个义项：方法陈旧）；句意为办公室还在用二十年前的报销系统，年轻同事笑它过时。

pos.zh: 过时的；老式的；被淘汰的

senses.title: Out of fashion
senses.definition: of a style, no longer worn or admired by most people
senses.definitionCN: 某种样式不再被多数人穿戴或欣赏
senses.example: The wide lapel is outmoded, though it keeps returning.
senses.exampleCN: 宽翻领已不流行，尽管它总在回来。
senses.why: The word begins with fashion, where the change is visible and quick.
senses.whyCN: 这个词从时尚开始，那里的变化看得见、来得快。

senses.title: Outdated technology
senses.definition: of a machine or method, replaced by something faster or cheaper
senses.definitionCN: 机器或方法被更快或更便宜的东西取代
senses.example: The factory still runs outmoded looms.
senses.exampleCN: 工厂还在用过时的织机。
senses.why: Here the verdict is practical: the old thing still works, but the new one works better.
senses.whyCN: 这里的判决是实用的：旧的还能用，但新的更好用。

senses.title: An obsolete method
senses.definition: of a procedure, kept long after a better one exists
senses.definitionCN: 一种程序在更好的做法出现后仍被保留
senses.example: The expense system is outmoded and everyone knows it.
senses.exampleCN: 这套报销系统已过时，人人都知道。
senses.why: Institutions keep outmoded methods because changing them costs more than the waste.
senses.whyCN: 机构保留陈旧方法，因为改变它的代价高于浪费。

senses.title: Superseded ideas
senses.definition: of a belief, replaced by evidence or by another belief
senses.definitionCN: 信念被证据或另一种信念取代
senses.example: The theory of the four humours is outmoded.
senses.exampleCN: 四体液说已经过时。
senses.why: Ideas age too, and the word treats them like clothes.
senses.whyCN: 观念也会变老，这个词把它们当作衣服。

senses.title: Old-fashioned in person
senses.definition: of a person, still living by rules that others have dropped
senses.definitionCN: 人仍按别人已经放弃的规矩生活
senses.example: He was outmoded in his manners and beloved for it.
senses.exampleCN: 他的礼数老派，也因此受人喜爱。
senses.why: Applied to people the word can sting or praise, depending on the speaker.
senses.whyCN: 用在人身上，这个词可以刺人，也可以称赞，取决于说话者。

senses.title: Obsolete in law
senses.definition: of a rule, still on the books but no longer enforced
senses.definitionCN: 规则仍在册，却不再执行
senses.example: An outmoded bylaw still bans carts on Sundays.
senses.exampleCN: 一条过时条例仍禁止周日推车。
senses.why: Law keeps its own museum, and the word is the label on the case.
senses.whyCN: 法律有自己的博物馆，这个词就是展柜上的标签。

senses.title: Dated in style
senses.definition: of a design, recognisable as belonging to an earlier decade
senses.definitionCN: 设计可被认出属于更早的十年
senses.example: The lobby's brass and brown tile now look outmoded.
senses.exampleCN: 大堂的黄铜与棕砖如今显得过时。
senses.why: Style dates by its details, not by its age.
senses.whyCN: 风格按细节定年代，而不按年头。

senses.title: An abandoned custom
senses.definition: of a practice, given up by a community rather than forbidden
senses.definitionCN: 一种做法被社群自行放弃，而不是被禁止
senses.example: The custom of calling on neighbours is outmoded in the new blocks.
senses.exampleCN: 在新公寓楼里，拜访邻居的习俗已过时。
senses.why: Nothing was banned; people simply stopped, which is how customs end.
senses.whyCN: 没有被禁，人们只是停了，习俗正是这样结束的。

intro.en: Outmoded is a plain compound: out of mode, and mode once meant the measure of what is current.
intro.cn: outmoded 是个朴素复合词：out of mode，而 mode 曾经指「当下流行的尺度」。

items.en: Modus meant 'measure, manner, way', the root of mode, model and modern.
items.cn: modus 意为「尺度、方式、方法」，是 mode、model 与 modern 的词根。

items.en: French mode meant 'fashion, current custom', and English took it in that sense.
items.cn: 法语 mode 意为「时尚、当下习俗」，英语按此义借入。

items.en: English mode kept both the grammatical sense and the sense of prevailing fashion.
items.cn: 英语 mode 同时保留语法义与流行风尚义。

items.en: The verb outmode, 'to put out of fashion', produced the adjective outmoded in the nineteenth century.
items.cn: 动词 outmode（使不再流行）在十九世纪造出形容词 outmoded。

items.en: Modern English applies it to machines, laws, manners and ideas, not only to clothes.
items.cn: 现代英语把它用于机器、法律、礼数与观念，不只是衣服。

note.en: The look-alike group is the mode family; the near-meaning group separates outdated, obsolete, dated and archaic.
note.cn: 形近组是 mode 词族；近义组把「过时」「废弃」「有年代感」与「古旧」分开。

entries.definition: to make something no longer current.
the state of being out of date.
a way of doing or being.
marked by the style of a past period.
belonging to a much earlier age.

normalIntro.en: The hooks keep the picture of an old coat whose shoulders no longer match anyone.
normalIntro.cn: 以下联想留住「一件肩线已不合任何人的旧外套」的画面。

normal.en: Outmoded is out of mode: whatever was the measure has moved on.
normal.cn: outmoded 就是 out of mode：原来的尺度已经往前走了。

normal.en: Think of a coat in the closet whose shoulders are too wide.
normal.cn: 想象衣柜里一件肩线过宽的外套。

normal.en: Out-mode-ed: three pieces, and the middle one means fashion.
normal.cn: out-mode-ed：三个部件，中间那个意为时尚。

normal.en: Say owt-MOH-did; the long o is the old fashion stretching on.
normal.cn: 读成 owt-MOH-did，长 o 是旧时尚还在延续。

normal.en: Pair it with replaced: a thing is outmoded when a newer thing has taken its place, not when it is merely old.
normal.cn: 把它和 replaced 配对：当新东西取代了它，它才 outmoded，而不只是旧。

abstract.en: Outmoded is a judgement about fit, not about age; old things can still fit.
abstract.cn: outmoded 判断的是贴合，而不是年龄；旧东西也可以仍然合身。

abstract.en: Institutions keep outmoded methods because the cost of change is visible and the cost of waste is not.
abstract.cn: 机构保留陈旧方法，因为改变的代价看得见，浪费的代价看不见。

abstract.en: The word is kindest when applied to objects and coldest when applied to people.
abstract.cn: 这个词用于物件时最温和，用于人时最冷。

examples.en: The office still runs an outmoded expense system from twenty years ago.
examples.cn: 办公室还在用二十年前的过时报销系统。

examples.en: The factory still runs outmoded looms.
examples.cn: 工厂还在用过时的织机。

examples.en: The theory of the four humours is outmoded.
examples.cn: 四体液说已经过时。

dict_mnemonic.text: out（在外）+ mode（时尚）：被时尚留在外面的，就是「过时的」。

root: out 加 mode（源自拉丁语 modus，尺度、方式），十九世纪由动词 outmode 派生出形容词

sensesIntro.en: The eight senses all measure a fit that has failed: clothes, machines, procedures, beliefs, manners, laws, designs and customs.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都在衡量一种已经失效的贴合：衣服、机器、程序、信念、礼数、法律、设计与习俗。

core.en: A COAT WITH A FORGOTTEN SHOULDER LINE

chain: THE COAT STAYS IN THE CLOSET

branches.en: Fashion and design, where the change is easiest to see.
branches.cn: 时尚与设计，变化最容易看见的地方。

branches.en: A machine and a procedure that a better one has replaced.
branches.cn: 被更好的东西取代的机器与程序。

branches.en: A belief that evidence has left behind.
branches.cn: 被证据落在后面的信念。

branches.en: A person still living by rules others have dropped.
branches.cn: 仍按别人已放弃的规矩生活的人。

branches.en: A law kept on the books and a custom quietly stopped.
branches.cn: 仍留在册上的法律与悄悄停止的习俗。

intro.en: The mode family is about measure: mode is the measure, modern is what fits now, outmoded is what no longer does.
intro.cn: mode 词族关乎尺度：mode 是尺度，modern 是合于当下的，outmoded 是不再合的。

latinIntro.en: Latin modus gives the measure; the prefixes out- and modern- tell you which side of the measure a thing stands on.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 modus 提供尺度；前缀 out- 与现代用法说明一个东西站在尺度的哪一边。

definition_zh: 序曲；提议；友好的主动表示
definition_en: an opening move, whether a piece of music before the main work or a first offer made to another person
core_image: 幕布在第一声响起时缓缓升起，正戏还没开始
scene: 演出前乐队先奏了一段，观众在这几分钟里慢慢安静下来。Before the play the orchestra played a short piece, and the audience grew quiet during those few minutes of overture.
sceneCN: 这里 overture 指音乐序曲（第 1 个义项：序曲）；句意为演出前乐队先奏一段，观众在这几分钟的序曲里慢慢安静。

senses.title: A musical overture
senses.definition: a piece played before the main work to prepare the audience
senses.definitionCN: 正戏之前演奏、为观众作准备的一段音乐
senses.example: The overture ended and the curtain rose.
senses.exampleCN: 序曲结束，幕布升起。
senses.why: The word's core is simple: music whose job is to come first.
senses.whyCN: 这个词的核心很简单：任务就是「先来」的音乐。

senses.title: An opening move
senses.definition: the first action in a sequence, made to set up what follows
senses.definitionCN: 一连串动作中的第一步，为后面铺垫
senses.example: The first meeting was an overture, not the negotiation.
senses.exampleCN: 第一次会面是开场，不是谈判。
senses.why: Any beginning that is deliberately staged can borrow the word.
senses.whyCN: 任何刻意安排的开始都可以借这个词。

senses.title: A proposal
senses.definition: an offer put forward for another person to accept or refuse
senses.definitionCN: 一份供对方接受或拒绝的提议
senses.example: She made an overture about buying the shop.
senses.exampleCN: 她提出买下那家店的意向。
senses.why: The offer is explicit, but the outcome is still open.
senses.whyCN: 提议是明确的，结果却仍开着。

senses.title: A friendly approach
senses.definition: a first gesture of goodwill toward someone who may not expect it
senses.definitionCN: 对可能没有期待的人作出第一个善意姿态
senses.example: His overture of tea and gossip softened the room.
senses.exampleCN: 他递茶与闲聊的示好让屋里松了下来。
senses.why: Here the word is social: it risks being refused, and that risk is the point.
senses.whyCN: 这里的词是社交的：它冒着被拒的风险，而风险正是要点。

senses.title: A diplomatic overture
senses.definition: a cautious first contact between states that do not yet trust each other
senses.definitionCN: 彼此尚不信任的国家之间的谨慎首次接触
senses.example: The two governments exchanged overtures through a third party.
senses.exampleCN: 两国政府通过第三方交换试探。
senses.why: In diplomacy the word lets both sides deny that anything has begun.
senses.whyCN: 在外交里，这个词让双方都能否认已经开始过什么。

senses.title: A prelude to an event
senses.definition: a smaller happening that announces a larger one
senses.definitionCN: 预示更大事件的小型事件
senses.example: The small protest was an overture to a long summer.
senses.exampleCN: 那场小抗议是漫长夏天的前奏。
senses.why: The metaphor keeps the theatre: history also likes to warm up.
senses.whyCN: 这个比喻保留剧场感：历史也喜欢先热场。

senses.title: A first offer in bargaining
senses.definition: an initial bid meant to open a negotiation rather than to be accepted
senses.definitionCN: 意在开启谈判而非被接受的首次出价
senses.example: The first number was only an overture.
senses.exampleCN: 第一个数字只是开场价。
senses.why: Here the word warns the listener not to take the opening seriously.
senses.whyCN: 这里的词提醒听者不要把开场当真。

senses.title: An opening that is forgotten
senses.definition: a beginning whose only success is that the main thing could start
senses.definitionCN: 唯一的成功是让主要的东西得以开始的开场
senses.example: The overture is rarely played alone, and that is its fate.
senses.exampleCN: 序曲很少单独演奏，这就是它的命运。
senses.why: The word carries a quiet melancholy: first things are usually not the ones remembered.
senses.whyCN: 这个词带着一点静默的怅然：最先出现的东西，通常不是被记住的东西。

intro.en: Overture is French for an opening, and the same Latin verb that opens a door opens a piece of music.
intro.cn: overture 在法语里就是「打开」，打开一扇门的那个拉丁动词，也打开一段音乐。

items.en: Aperire meant 'to open, to uncover', the source of aperture and of the French word.
items.cn: aperire 意为「打开、揭开」，是 aperture 与那个法语词的来源。

items.en: Apertura meant 'an opening', both a gap and the act of opening.
items.cn: apertura 意为「开口」，既指缺口，也指打开的动作。

items.en: Old French ouverture kept the meaning 'an opening' and passed into English.
items.cn: 古法语 ouverture 保留「打开」之义，传入英语。

items.en: In the seventeenth century the word became the name for music played before an opera.
items.cn: 十七世纪，这个词成为歌剧前所奏音乐的名称。

items.en: Modern English extended it to first offers between people and states.
items.cn: 现代英语把它扩展到人与人、国与国之间的首个提议。

note.en: The look-alike group is the open family; the near-meaning group separates prelude, proposal, approach and bid.
note.cn: 形近组是「打开」词族；近义组把「前奏」「提议」「接近」与「出价」分开。

entries.definition: a short piece before the main one.
a first contact made to someone.

normalIntro.en: The hooks keep the picture of a curtain rising on the first note.
normalIntro.cn: 以下联想留住「第一声响起时幕布升起」的画面。

normal.en: Overture is French for opening; the same word sits in aperture, a hole that opens.
normal.cn: overture 在法语里是「打开」；同一个词根在 aperture（打开的孔）里。

normal.en: Think of a curtain lifting before anyone has entered.
normal.cn: 想象幕布在无人上场前先升起。

normal.en: O-ver-ture: the middle sounds like 'vert', a door turning open.
normal.cn: o-ver-ture：中间听起来像 vert，一扇门转开。

normal.en: Say oh-ver-CHOOR; the ending is the sound of a hinge.
normal.cn: 读成 oh-ver-CHOOR，尾音像铰链的声音。

normal.en: Pair it with offer: an overture is an offer made before you know the answer.
normal.cn: 把它和 offer 配对：overture 是在还不知道答复前递出的提议。

abstract.en: An overture asks to be judged by what it makes possible, not by itself.
abstract.cn: 序曲希望人按它促成了什么来评判它，而不是按它本身。

abstract.en: Diplomatic overtures are deniable by design, which is why they are useful.
abstract.cn: 外交试探天生可被否认，这正是它有用之处。

abstract.en: The first move is rarely the remembered one; beginnings are mostly scaffolding.
abstract.cn: 第一步很少是被记住的那一步；开头多半是脚手架。

examples.en: Before the play the orchestra played a short overture.
examples.cn: 演出前乐队先奏了一段序曲。

examples.en: She made an overture about buying the shop.
examples.cn: 她提出买下那家店的意向。

examples.en: The two governments exchanged overtures through a third party.
examples.cn: 两国政府通过第三方交换试探。

dict_mnemonic.text: overture 来自法语「打开」：先把门打开的那一段，就是「序曲、开场提议」。

root: 古法语 ouverture（打开），源自拉丁语 apertura，与 aperire（打开）同源

sensesIntro.en: The eight senses are all first moves: music, a staged beginning, an offer, a friendly gesture, a diplomatic probe, a prelude, an opening bid and a beginning that no one remembers.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都是第一步：音乐、刻意的开场、提议、善意姿态、外交试探、前奏、开场出价，以及无人记得的开头。

core.en: A CURTAIN LIFTING ON THE FIRST NOTE
core.cn: 第一声响起时升起的幕布

branches.en: Music that prepares and a small event that announces a large one.
branches.cn: 作准备的音乐与预示大事的小事件。

branches.en: A staged first step and the beginning nobody remembers.
branches.cn: 刻意的第一步与被忘记的开头。

branches.en: A proposal offered and an opening bid in a bargain.
branches.cn: 递出的提议与议价中的开场出价。

branches.en: A gesture of goodwill that risks refusal.
branches.cn: 冒着被拒风险的善意姿态。

branches.en: A first contact that both sides can deny.
branches.cn: 双方都可否认的首次接触。

intro.en: The open family is about apertures: overture is an opening, aperture a hole, overt what is uncovered.
intro.cn: 「打开」词族关乎开口：overture 是一次打开，aperture 是一个孔，overt 是未遮盖的。

latinIntro.en: Latin aperire supplies the opening, and its opposite operire supplies the covering behind covert.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 aperire 提供「打开」，它的反义词 operire 提供 covert 背后的「遮盖」。

definition_zh: 微不足道的；少得可怜的；可鄙的
definition_en: so small or mean that it invites contempt rather than respect
core_image: 桌上只有一小碟，里面三粒豆子，主人却说这是全部家当
scene: 他干了一整月，拿到的钱还不够付一半房租。He worked the whole month and was paid a sum that would not cover half the rent, a paltry reward for so much time.
sceneCN: 这里 paltry 指报酬菲薄（第 6 个义项：报酬菲薄）；句意为他干了一整月，报酬少得连一半房租都不够。

pos.zh: 微不足道的；少得可怜的；可鄙的

senses.title: Insignificantly small
senses.definition: of a quantity, below what the situation plainly deserves
senses.definitionCN: 数量低于情形明显应得的水平
senses.example: Three beans on a plate would be a paltry meal.
senses.exampleCN: 盘里三粒豆子，是少得可怜的一餐。
senses.why: The word measures by expectation: smallness alone is not enough.
senses.whyCN: 这个词按期待衡量：单是「小」还不足以构成它。

senses.title: A contemptible amount
senses.definition: of money, so little that it reads as an insult
senses.definitionCN: 钱少到读起来像侮辱
senses.example: They offered a paltry compensation and called it fair.
senses.exampleCN: 他们给出一笔微薄补偿，还称之为公平。
senses.why: Money is the word's most common home because prices can be compared.
senses.whyCN: 钱是这个词最常见的住处，因为价码可以比较。

senses.title: A feeble excuse
senses.definition: of an explanation, thin enough to show it was not meant
senses.definitionCN: 解释薄到一看就知道不是真话
senses.example: He gave a paltry excuse about the traffic.
senses.exampleCN: 他拿交通作了个拙劣借口。
senses.why: The word judges the effort behind the words, not their length.
senses.whyCN: 这个词评判话语背后的用心，而不是话语的长短。

senses.title: A token effort
senses.definition: of work, done just enough to be visible and no more
senses.definitionCN: 干活只干到能被看见的程度，一点不多
senses.example: The clean-up was a paltry effort and the street stayed dirty.
senses.exampleCN: 清扫只是敷衍了事，街道依旧脏。
senses.why: Here smallness is a choice, which makes it contemptible.
senses.whyCN: 这里的「小」是一种选择，因此可鄙。

senses.title: A sum that shames
senses.definition: of a payment, low enough to embarrass the payer and the paid
senses.definitionCN: 款项低到让付款者和收款者都难堪
senses.example: The prize was a paltry fifty pounds.
senses.exampleCN: 奖金只有寒酸的五十镑。
senses.why: The word often carries the speaker's flush of shame.
senses.whyCN: 这个词常带着说话者脸上一热的那种难堪。

senses.title: Meagre reward
senses.definition: of a return for labour, far below the time it took
senses.definitionCN: 劳动所得远低于所花的时间
senses.example: He worked the month for a paltry reward.
senses.exampleCN: 他干了一个月，报酬菲薄。
senses.why: Fairness enters here: the sum is judged against the hours.
senses.whyCN: 公平在这里进场：款子是跟小时数比的。

senses.title: A petty reason
senses.definition: of a motive, small in a way that lowers the person who holds it
senses.definitionCN: 动机小得让持有它的人显得低下
senses.example: Jealousy is a paltry reason to ruin a friendship.
senses.exampleCN: 因嫉妒毁掉友谊，是卑琐的理由。
senses.why: The word can turn from the thing to the mind that wants it.
senses.whyCN: 这个词可以从物转向想要它的那颗心。

senses.title: Beneath notice
senses.definition: of a thing, not worth the attention it asks for
senses.definitionCN: 不值得它所索取的注意
senses.example: The objection was paltry and the meeting moved on.
senses.exampleCN: 那点异议不值一提，会议继续往下走。
senses.why: Used this way the word dismisses rather than measures.
senses.whyCN: 这样用时，这个词是在驱散，而不是在衡量。

intro.en: Paltry is a word of uncertain origin, probably built from an old word for a rag or a scrap.
intro.cn: paltry 来源不确定，很可能由某个意为「破布、碎屑」的古词构成。

items.en: An English dialect word palt or pelt meant 'a rag, a worthless scrap'.
items.cn: 英语方言词 palt 或 pelt 意为「破布、没用的碎屑」。

items.en: The ending -ry made nouns of quality or collection, as in rivalry and jewellery.
items.cn: 词尾 -ry 构成表性质或集合的名词，如 rivalry 与 jewellery。

items.en: Paltry appears in sixteenth-century writing, already meaning 'worthless, contemptible'.
items.cn: paltry 见于十六世纪文字，当时已意为「无价值的、可鄙的」。

items.en: The nineteenth century fixed it to small sums of money and small wages.
items.cn: 十九世纪把它固定用于小额钱款与菲薄工资。

items.en: Today it judges excuses and efforts as readily as amounts.
items.cn: 今天它评判借口与作为，和评判数额一样顺手。

note.en: The look-alike group is the paltry family; the near-meaning group separates trifling, meagre, piddling and negligible.
note.cn: 形近组是 paltry 词族；近义组把「琐碎」「微薄」「小气」与「可忽略」分开。

normalIntro.en: The hooks keep the picture of three beans offered as a whole meal.
normalIntro.cn: 以下联想留住「三粒豆子被当作一顿饭」的画面。

normal.en: Paltry sounds like 'poultry' scraps: the bits nobody would buy.
normal.cn: paltry 听起来像 poultry（家禽）的碎屑：没人肯买的边角。

normal.en: Think of a plate with three beans and a proud host.
normal.cn: 想象一只盘子三粒豆子，主人还很得意。

normal.en: Pal-try: try with a 'pal', and even a friend would not call this enough.
normal.cn: pal-try：和 pal（朋友）一起 try，连朋友都不会说这够了。

normal.en: Say PAWL-tree; the long first syllable makes the thing sound emptier.
normal.cn: 读成 PAWL-tree，第一个音节拖长，东西听起来更空。

normal.en: Pair it with sum: a paltry sum is one that apologises for itself.
normal.cn: 把它和 sum 配对：paltry sum 是一笔自带歉意的款子。

abstract.en: Paltry is a comparison wearing the clothes of a description.
abstract.cn: paltry 是穿了描述外衣的比较。

abstract.en: The word is most damaging when applied to effort, because effort could have been more.
abstract.cn: 这个词用在「作为」上最伤人，因为作为本可以更多。

abstract.en: Small is neutral; paltry is small with a verdict attached.
abstract.cn: 小是中性的；paltry 是带着判决的小。

examples.en: He worked the whole month for a paltry reward.
examples.cn: 他干了一整月，报酬菲薄。

examples.en: They offered a paltry compensation and called it fair.
examples.cn: 他们给出一笔微薄补偿，还称之为公平。

examples.en: Jealousy is a paltry reason to ruin a friendship.
examples.cn: 因嫉妒毁掉友谊，是卑琐的理由。

dict_mnemonic.text: palt（古词「破布、碎屑」）+ ry（名词尾）：只值一块破布的东西，就是「微不足道的」。

root: 来源不确定，一般认为出自方言词 palt／pelt（破布、碎屑）加后缀 -ry

sensesIntro.en: The eight senses all shrink something and then judge it: a meal, a sum, an excuse, an effort, a prize, a wage, a motive and an objection.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都先把某物缩小，再作评判：一餐、一笔钱、一个借口、一番作为、一份奖、一份工资、一个动机与一点异议。

core.en: THREE BEANS CALLED A MEAL

branches.en: A small quantity and a small sum of money.
branches.cn: 少量的东西与微薄的款子。

branches.en: A thin excuse and an effort that stops at being seen.
branches.cn: 单薄的借口与只做到被看见的作为。

branches.en: A prize that shames and a wage that does not meet the hours.
branches.cn: 令人难堪的奖与不抵工时的工资。

branches.en: A motive small enough to lower its holder.
branches.cn: 小到让持有者显得低下的动机。

branches.en: A thing dismissed rather than measured.
branches.cn: 被驱散而不是被衡量的东西。

intro.en: The paltry family is thin: the adjective, its comparison and its noun, all built on the same scrap.
intro.cn: paltry 词族很单薄：形容词、比较级与名词，全都长在同一块碎屑上。

latinIntro.en: This word has no Latin source; the entries below are the neighbouring vocabulary of smallness and worthlessness.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有拉丁来源；下面这些条目是「小」与「无价值」的邻近词汇。

items.exampleCN: 接着来了一个更寒酸的提议。

definition_zh: 小册子作者；写小册子的人
definition_en: a person who writes and distributes short printed arguments, often to attack or defend a cause
core_image: 街角有人把几张纸钉在一起，塞给过路人，纸上满是对当权者的责骂
scene: 那几年他靠印几页纸谋生，骂财政大臣，也骂主教。For those years he lived by printing a few sheets at a time, attacking the chancellor and the bishops alike, a pamphleteer with ink on his cuffs.
sceneCN: 这里 pamphleteer 指写小册子的人（第 1 个义项：小册子作者）；句意为那几年他靠印几页纸谋生，骂财政大臣也骂主教，是个袖口沾墨的小册子作者。

collocations.zh: 言辞激烈的小册子作者
以小册子形式写诗讽世

senses.title: A writer of pamphlets
senses.definition: a person who writes short unbound booklets on a public question
senses.definitionCN: 就公共问题撰写短篇不装订册子的人
senses.example: He lived by printing a few sheets at a time, a pamphleteer with ink on his cuffs.
senses.exampleCN: 他靠一次印几页纸谋生，是个袖口沾墨的小册子作者。
senses.why: The suffix -eer names the person by the thing he makes, like auctioneer and engineer.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -eer 按所造之物来命名人，如 auctioneer 与 engineer。

senses.title: A political writer
senses.definition: a writer whose short works aim at a policy, a party or a minister
senses.definitionCN: 短篇作品针对某项政策、政党或大臣的作者
senses.example: The pamphleteer attacked the chancellor every month.
senses.exampleCN: 这位小册子作者每月攻击财政大臣。
senses.why: Politics gave the word most of its energy and most of its danger.
senses.whyCN: 政治给了这个词大部分能量，也给了它大部分危险。

senses.title: A controversialist
senses.definition: a person who argues in print and prefers a fight to a discussion
senses.definitionCN: 在印刷品中论战、宁可争吵不愿讨论的人
senses.example: He was a pamphleteer first and a thinker second.
senses.exampleCN: 他首先是论战者，其次才是思想家。
senses.why: The word can admire the courage or doubt the depth.
senses.whyCN: 这个词可以佩服勇气，也可以怀疑深度。

senses.title: A cheap hack writer
senses.definition: a writer paid by the sheet, with more speed than care
senses.definitionCN: 按页取酬、速度多于讲究的写作者
senses.example: The pamphleteer turned out six sheets a week and forgot them all.
senses.exampleCN: 这位写手一周出六页，转眼全忘。
senses.why: Here the trade is visible: pamphlets were cheap and quick.
senses.whyCN: 这里的行业属性露出来了：小册子便宜又快。

senses.title: To write pamphlets
senses.definition: to produce and circulate such sheets, usually for a cause
senses.definitionCN: 制作并散发这类纸页，通常为某项事业
senses.example: He pamphleteered for the cause until the money ran out.
senses.exampleCN: 他为这项事业写小册子，直到钱用完。
senses.why: As a verb the word stresses the activity rather than the person.
senses.whyCN: 作动词时，这个词强调活动，而不是人。

senses.title: A seventeenth-century figure
senses.titleCN: 十七世纪的小册子作者
senses.definition: the historical type who fought the civil war with ink and presses
senses.definitionCN: 用墨水与印刷机打内战的历史人物类型
senses.example: Seventeenth-century pamphleteers filled the city with argument.
senses.exampleCN: 十七世纪的小册子作者用论辩填满了这座城市。
senses.why: The word remembers an age when a few pages could change a street.
senses.whyCN: 这个词记得一个几页纸就能改变一条街的时代。

senses.title: A self-appointed campaigner
senses.definition: a person who takes up a public cause without being asked
senses.definitionCN: 未受邀请便承担公共事业的人
senses.example: The pamphleteer had no office and no mandate, only a press.
senses.exampleCN: 这位宣传者没有职位、没有授权，只有一台印刷机。
senses.why: The word is suspicious of self-appointment, even when it admires the result.
senses.whyCN: 这个词对自封总带着疑心，即使它佩服结果。

senses.title: A distributor of sheets
senses.definition: a person who hands the printed sheets to strangers
senses.definitionCN: 把印好的纸页递给陌生人的人
senses.example: The pamphleteer stood at the gate and gave away his argument.
senses.exampleCN: 他站在门口，把自己的论点免费送出。
senses.why: Distribution is half the word: an unread pamphlet changes nothing.
senses.whyCN: 散发是这个词的一半：没人读的小册子什么也改不了。

intro.en: Pamphlet began as the nickname of a short Latin poem, and the little book took the poem's name.
intro.cn: pamphlet 起初是一首拉丁小诗的昵称，这本小书后来继承了诗的名字。

items.en: Pamphilus was the title of a twelfth-century Latin love poem, short enough to fit in a few sheets.
items.cn: Pamphilus 是一首十二世纪拉丁爱情诗的名字，短到几页纸就能装下。

items.en: The poem circulated as a small unbound booklet, and English called any such booklet a pamphlet.
items.cn: 这首诗以小册子形式流传，英语便把任何这类小册子叫作 pamphlet。

items.en: Sixteenth-century religious conflict turned the pamphlet into a weapon of argument.
items.cn: 十六世纪宗教冲突把这种小册子变成论战武器。

items.en: The ending -eer, as in engineer and auctioneer, made pamphleteer a name for the writer.
items.cn: 后缀 -eer（如 engineer 与 auctioneer）把 pamphleteer 变成写作者的名号。

items.en: The word now covers political blogs in print and any short, sharp public argument.
items.cn: 今天这个词涵盖印刷形式的政治短论，以及任何短而锋利的公共论辩。

note.en: The look-alike group is the pamphlet family; the near-meaning group separates the essayist, the polemicist and the propagandist.
note.cn: 形近组是 pamphlet 词族；近义组把「随笔作者」「论战者」与「宣传者」分开。

entries.definition: a writer of short reflective pieces.
a writer who attacks a position.
a writer who spreads a cause's message.
entries.definitionCN: 传播某事业信息的作者。

normalIntro.en: The hooks keep the picture of a few sheets stapled together and pushed into a passing hand.
normalIntro.cn: 以下联想留住「几张纸钉在一起，被塞进路人手里」的画面。

normal.en: Pamphleteer is pamphlet plus -eer, the suffix of auctioneer and engineer.
normal.cn: pamphleteer 是 pamphlet 加 -eer，即 auctioneer 与 engineer 的那个后缀。

normal.en: Think of a stack of three sheets and a stranger refusing to take one.
normal.cn: 想象三张纸一叠，陌生人还不肯接。

normal.en: Pam-phlet-eer: three beats, like a hand pushing paper at you.
normal.cn: pam-phlet-eer：三拍，像一只手把纸推给你。

normal.en: Say pæm-fluh-TEER; the stress falls on the person, not the paper.
normal.cn: 读成 pæm-fluh-TEER，重音在人，不在纸。

normal.en: Pair it with press: the pamphleteer needs a press more than a publisher.
normal.cn: 把它和 press 配对：小册子作者需要的是一台印刷机，而不是出版社。

abstract.en: A pamphleteer is a person who believes an argument can fit on a few sheets.
abstract.cn: 小册子作者相信一个论点几页纸就能装下。

abstract.en: The word admires reach and suspects haste at the same time.
abstract.cn: 这个词同时佩服覆盖面，又怀疑仓促。

abstract.en: Cheap printing made the pamphleteer possible, much as the web made the blogger.
abstract.cn: 廉价印刷造就了小册子作者，正如网络造就了博主。

examples.en: For those years he lived by printing a few sheets, a pamphleteer with ink on his cuffs.
examples.cn: 那几年他靠印几页纸谋生，是个袖口沾墨的小册子作者。

examples.en: The pamphleteer attacked the chancellor every month.
examples.cn: 这位小册子作者每月攻击财政大臣。

examples.en: He pamphleteered for the cause until the money ran out.
examples.cn: 他为这项事业写小册子，直到钱用完。

dict_mnemonic.text: pamphlet（小册子）+ eer（做某事的人）：做小册子的人，就是「小册子作者」。

root: pamphlet 源自十二世纪拉丁小诗 Pamphilus 的书名，加后缀 -eer 构成指人的名词

sensesIntro.en: The eight senses all centre on a few printed sheets: the writer, the politician, the fighter, the hack, the activity, the historical type, the self-appointed voice and the hand at the gate.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都围着几张印好的纸：作者、政客、斗士、写手、活动、历史类型、自封的声音与门口的那只手。

core.en: FEW SHEETS IN A PASSING HAND
core.cn: 被塞进路人手里的几张纸

branches.en: The writer as a trade and as a hack.
branches.cn: 作为行业与作为廉价写手的作者。

branches.en: A political voice and a voice nobody appointed.
branches.cn: 政治声音与无人任命的声音。

branches.en: The controversialist and the seventeenth-century type.
branches.cn: 论战者与十七世纪类型。

branches.en: The activity rather than the person.
branches.cn: 活动，而不是人。

branches.en: The half of the work that happens at the gate.
branches.cn: 在门口完成的那一半工作。

intro.en: The pamphlet family is small: a booklet, the person who writes it, the activity and the verb.
intro.cn: pamphlet 词族不大：一本小册、写它的人、这项活动与那个动词。

latinIntro.en: The -eer suffix is French in origin and names a trade; the stem itself is a Latin poem's nickname.
latinIntro.cn: 后缀 -eer 源自法语，用来命名行业；词干本身是一首拉丁诗的昵称。

items.exampleCN: 一位激烈的小册子作者。
小册子作者们挤满广场。

definition_zh: 偏执；妄想症；多疑
definition_en: a state of mind in which a person reads every event as aimed at him, whether or not it is
core_image: 一个人把窗帘拉严，反复检查门锁，觉得每个声音都是冲他来的
scene: 他把窗帘拉上，又检查了三次门锁，说楼下那辆车从上周就跟着他。He drew the curtains, checked the lock three times and said the car downstairs had been following him since last week, a paranoia no argument could touch.
sceneCN: 这里 paranoia 指病理性的偏执（第 1 个义项：临床偏执）；句意为他拉上窗帘、三次检查门锁，说楼下的车从上周就跟着他，任何劝说都碰不到这种偏执。

senses.title: Clinical paranoia
senses.definition: a psychiatric condition in which the patient believes he is being watched or harmed
senses.definitionCN: 患者相信自己正被监视或加害的精神状况
senses.example: The diagnosis was paranoia, and the ward notes mentioned the neighbours.
senses.exampleCN: 诊断是偏执，病历里提到了邻居。
senses.why: The medical sense is strict: the belief is fixed and resistant to evidence.
senses.whyCN: 医学义是严格的：信念固定，且不受证据影响。

senses.title: Everyday suspicion
senses.definition: an ordinary habit of reading neutral events as hostile
senses.definitionCN: 把中性事件读成敌意的日常习惯
senses.example: A touch of paranoia made him reread every email twice.
senses.exampleCN: 一点多疑让他每封邮件都读两遍。
senses.why: Here the word is a mild diagnosis, often said with a smile.
senses.whyCN: 这里的词是轻诊断，常带笑说出口。

senses.title: Collective paranoia
senses.definition: a mood in which a whole group feels surrounded by enemies
senses.definitionCN: 整个群体觉得四面皆敌的气氛
senses.example: The town's paranoia grew until every stranger was a spy.
senses.exampleCN: 镇上的疑惧越来越重，最后每个陌生人都成了间谍。
senses.why: The word scales; a crowd can share one fixed idea.
senses.whyCN: 这个词可以放大：一群人能共享同一个固定念头。

senses.title: Political paranoia
senses.definition: a style of politics that explains every event as a plot
senses.definitionCN: 把每件事都解释为阴谋的政治风格
senses.example: The campaign ran on paranoia and a list of enemies.
senses.exampleCN: 那场竞选靠猜忌和一份敌人名单运转。
senses.why: Politics rewards the story that names a hidden hand.
senses.whyCN: 政治会奖励那种指出「幕后黑手」的故事。

senses.title: Suspicion of technology
senses.definition: the sense that devices are listening, even when they are not
senses.definitionCN: 觉得设备在偷听、即使并没有的那种感觉
senses.example: Her paranoia about the phone peaked after one strange advertisement.
senses.exampleCN: 一条奇怪的广告之后，她对手机的疑惧达到顶点。
senses.why: New tools give old fear a new object.
senses.whyCN: 新工具给旧恐惧换了一个新对象。

senses.title: A historical panic
senses.definition: a period in which a society sees a hidden enemy everywhere
senses.definitionCN: 社会到处看见隐藏敌人的一段时期
senses.example: Historians describe the hunt for witches as a paranoia with a legal form.
senses.exampleCN: 史学家把猎巫描述为一种有法律形式的集体偏执。
senses.why: The word lets historians judge a whole season, not just a patient.
senses.whyCN: 这个词让史学家评判一整个时代，而不只是评判病人。

senses.title: Paranoia in literature
senses.definition: a narrative mode in which the reader cannot tell plot from delusion
senses.definitionCN: 读者分不清情节与妄想的叙事方式
senses.example: The novel's paranoia is the reader's too, since no narrator is reliable.
senses.exampleCN: 小说的偏执也是读者的偏执，因为没有叙述者可靠。
senses.why: Fiction uses the condition as a lens, not a label.
senses.whyCN: 小说把这个状况当镜头，而不是当标签。

senses.title: Hypervigilance
senses.definition: a state of watching everything so closely that rest becomes impossible
senses.definitionCN: 把一切看得太紧，以至于无法休息的状态
senses.example: Years of paranoia had taught him to sleep with the light on.
senses.exampleCN: 多年过度警觉教会他开着灯睡觉。
senses.why: The word can describe the body's habit, not only the mind's belief.
senses.whyCN: 这个词可以描述身体的习惯，而不只是心的信念。

intro.en: Paranoia is Greek for 'beside the mind': the belief sits next to reason and will not move over.
intro.cn: paranoia 在希腊语里是「在心智旁边」：那个信念坐在理性的旁边，不肯挪过来。

items.en: Para meant 'beside, beyond', the prefix of parallel and paradox.
items.cn: para 意为「在旁边、超出」，是 parallel 与 paradox 的前缀。

items.en: Noos meant 'mind, thought', the noun behind nous and noetic.
items.cn: noos 意为「心智、思想」，是 nous 与 noetic 背后的名词。

items.en: Paranoia meant 'madness, derangement', literally a mind set beside itself.
items.cn: paranoia 意为「疯狂、错乱」，字面是「心放在自己旁边」。

items.en: Nineteenth-century psychiatry narrowed the word to fixed beliefs of persecution.
items.cn: 十九世纪精神病学把这个词收窄为固定的被害信念。

items.en: Modern English uses it for politics, technology and literature, often half in jest.
items.cn: 现代英语把它用于政治、技术与文学，常常半开玩笑。

note.en: The look-alike group is the paranoia family; the near-meaning group separates suspicion, delusion and vigilance.
note.cn: 形近组是 paranoia 词族；近义组把「怀疑」「妄想」与「警觉」分开。

entries.definition: a feeling that something is wrong.
a firm belief held despite evidence.
a refusal to rely on someone.
a thought that will not leave.

normalIntro.en: The hooks keep the picture of a locked door checked three times before sleep.
normalIntro.cn: 以下联想留住「睡前把门锁检查三次」的画面。

normal.en: Paranoia is para plus noos: a mind sitting beside itself.
normal.cn: paranoia 是 para 加 noos：一颗坐在自己旁边的心。

normal.en: Think of a curtain pulled shut and a car that is always there.
normal.cn: 想象窗帘拉严，而那辆车总在楼下。

normal.en: Para-noia: the first part means beside, the second means mind.
normal.cn: para-noia：前半是「旁边」，后半是「心」。

normal.en: Say pær-uh-NOY-uh; the last vowel sounds like a low hum of worry.
normal.cn: 读成 pær-uh-NOY-uh，最后的元音像担心的低鸣。

normal.en: Pair it with pattern: paranoia is a machine for finding patterns that are not there.
normal.cn: 把它和 pattern 配对：偏执是一台专门找出不存在的模式的机器。

abstract.en: Paranoia is not wrong about everything; it is wrong about the proportion.
abstract.cn: 偏执并非一切都错；它错在比例。

abstract.en: The condition is lonely because the evidence is private and cannot be shown.
abstract.cn: 这种状况是孤独的，因为证据是私人的，拿不出来。

abstract.en: A society can be paranoid in exactly the same way a person is: by counting enemies instead of facts.
abstract.cn: 社会与人一样会偏执：数敌人，而不数事实。

examples.en: He checked the lock three times, a paranoia no argument could touch.
examples.cn: 他三次检查门锁，任何劝说都碰不到这种偏执。

examples.en: A touch of paranoia made him reread every email twice.
examples.cn: 一点多疑让他每封邮件都读两遍。

examples.en: The town's paranoia grew until every stranger was a spy.
examples.cn: 镇上的疑惧越来越重，最后每个陌生人都成了间谍。

dict_mnemonic.text: para（旁边）+ noia（心智）：心智偏到一旁，就是「偏执、妄想」。

root: 希腊语 paranoia（疯狂、错乱），由 para（旁）与 noos（心智）构成

sensesIntro.en: The eight senses all place a fixed belief beside the facts: a patient, an email habit, a town, a campaign, a phone, a panic, a novel and a sleepless body.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都把同一个固定信念放在事实旁边：一个病人、一种读信习惯、一座镇、一场竞选、一部手机、一场恐慌、一部小说与一具失眠的身体。

core.en: A LOCK CHECKED THREE TIMES

branches.en: A clinical fixation and the body's watchfulness.
branches.cn: 临床的固定信念与身体的警觉。

branches.en: An everyday habit of doubt and a fear aimed at devices.
branches.cn: 日常的怀疑习惯与对准设备的恐惧。

branches.en: A town's mood and a season of panic.
branches.cn: 一座镇的气氛与一个恐慌的季节。

branches.en: A politics that explains everything as a plot.
branches.cn: 把一切解释为阴谋的政治。

branches.en: A story in which the reader shares the doubt.
branches.cn: 读者与人物共担疑虑的故事。

intro.en: The paranoia family turns on para-: parallel lines, paradoxes and paranoid minds all sit beside something.
intro.cn: paranoia 词族围绕 para- 展开：平行线、悖论与偏执的心，都坐在某物旁边。

latinIntro.en: Greek para supplies the beside and noos supplies the mind; psychiatry later added the clinical narrowing.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊语 para 提供「旁边」，noos 提供「心」；精神病学后来加上了临床上的收窄。

items.example: The paranoiac kept a diary of plots.

definition_zh: 家长式统治；家长作风；父权主义
definition_en: the habit of deciding for others on the grounds that one knows what is good for them
core_image: 一位家长替全家做了所有决定，还坚持说这是为每个人好
scene: 公司给员工安排了宿舍、食堂和作息表，说是替他们省心。The company provided housing, meals and a timetable for its workers, saying it was saving them trouble, a paternalism that came with a rent-free roof.
sceneCN: 这里 paternalism 指雇主的家长作风（第 1 个义项：雇主家长作风）；句意为公司给员工安排宿舍、食堂与作息表，说是替他们省心，这种家长作风还附赠一个免租房顶。

pos.zh: 家长式统治；家长作风；父权主义

senses.title: Employer paternalism
senses.definition: a firm that houses, feeds and supervises its workers as if they were children
senses.definitionCN: 像对待孩子一样给工人提供住处、饭食并加以监管的企业做法
senses.example: The mill's paternalism included a school and a chapel.
senses.exampleCN: 这家纺织厂的家长作风还包括一所学校和一座礼拜堂。
senses.why: Care and control arrive in the same van.
senses.whyCN: 照顾与控制是同一辆车送来的。

senses.title: State paternalism
senses.definition: a government that restricts choices because it claims to know better
senses.definitionCN: 以「更懂」为由限制选择空间的政府做法
senses.example: The smoking ban was defended as benevolent paternalism.
senses.exampleCN: 禁烟令被辩护为仁慈的家长式治理。
senses.why: The word names the trade: some freedom for some safety.
senses.whyCN: 这个词命名那笔交易：用一些自由换一些安全。

senses.title: Colonial paternalism
senses.definition: rule that treats a colonised people as wards in need of guidance
senses.definitionCN: 把被殖民民族当作需要指导的受监护人的统治
senses.example: The district officer's paternalism infuriated the new assembly.
senses.exampleCN: 地区官员的家长作风激怒了新议会。
senses.why: Here the word exposes the insult inside the kindness.
senses.whyCN: 这里的词揭开了善意里藏着的轻蔑。

senses.title: Medical paternalism
senses.definition: the tradition of deciding for a patient rather than with him
senses.definitionCN: 替病人决定而不是与病人共同决定的传统
senses.example: Medical paternalism once kept diagnoses from the sick.
senses.exampleCN: 医疗父权主义曾把诊断瞒着病人。
senses.why: The profession's authority was once thought to need no consent.
senses.whyCN: 这个行业的权威曾被认为无需同意。

senses.title: Legal paternalism
senses.definition: laws that protect people by limiting what they may choose
senses.definitionCN: 以限制选择来保护人的法律思路
senses.example: Helmet laws rest on a legal paternalism few drivers accept.
senses.exampleCN: 头盔法建立在一种少有司机接受的家长主义上。
senses.why: The argument is about who owns a life: the person or the state.
senses.whyCN: 争论在于一条命归谁：本人，还是国家。

senses.title: Family paternalism
senses.definition: a father's assumption that his judgement settles the household's questions
senses.definitionCN: 父亲认为自己的判断就能定下家中问题的假定
senses.example: The family ran on a quiet paternalism no one dared name.
senses.exampleCN: 这个家靠一种无人敢点名的安静父权运转。
senses.why: The word begins at home and then expands to institutions.
senses.whyCN: 这个词从家里开始，然后扩展到机构。

senses.title: Condescending benevolence
senses.definition: the manner of helping someone while making his own judgement look small
senses.definitionCN: 一边帮忙一边让对方的判断显得微不足道的态度
senses.example: She resented the paternalism of being told to rest.
senses.exampleCN: 被人叫去休息时，她厌恶那种居高临下的善意。
senses.why: Kindness can be a way of taking the pen out of another hand.
senses.whyCN: 善意可以是把笔从别人手里拿走的一种方式。

senses.title: Critique of paternalism
senses.definition: the argument that people should be allowed to make their own mistakes
senses.definitionCN: 主张人应当被允许自己犯错的论证
senses.example: The essay attacked paternalism in the name of dignity.
senses.exampleCN: 这篇文章以尊严之名抨击家长主义。
senses.why: The word is most often used by its opponents, which is why it rarely sounds neutral.
senses.whyCN: 这个词多由反对者使用，所以它很少听起来中性。

intro.en: Paternalism is made from the Latin word for father: the ruler is imagined as a parent, and the ruled as children.
intro.cn: paternalism 由拉丁语的「父亲」造出：统治者被想象为家长，被统治者被想象为孩子。

items.en: Pater meant 'father', the root of paternal, patron and patrician.
items.cn: pater 意为「父亲」，是 paternal、patron 与 patrician 的词根。

items.en: Paternal meant 'of a father', as opposed to maternal, of a mother.
items.cn: paternal 意为「父亲的」，与 maternal（母亲的）相对。

items.en: Nineteenth-century writers used paternalism for employers who governed their workers' whole lives.
items.cn: 十九世纪作家用 paternalism 指管理工人全部生活的雇主。

items.en: Twentieth-century politics made it a term of argument about the welfare state.
items.cn: 二十世纪政治把它变成关于福利国家的争论术语。

items.en: Today it is applied to medicine, law, colonial rule and ordinary condescension.
items.cn: 今天它被用于医学、法律、殖民统治与日常的居高临下。

note.en: The look-alike group is the pater family; the near-meaning group separates patriarchy, condescension and authoritarianism.
note.cn: 形近组是 pater 词族；近义组把「父权制」「居高临下」与「威权主义」分开。

entries.definition: one who governs like a father.
acting like a father toward others.
a social order ruled by fathers.
entries.definitionCN: 由父亲们统治的社会秩序。

normalIntro.en: The hooks keep the picture of a parent who has already decided for everyone.
normalIntro.cn: 以下联想留住「家长已经替所有人做完决定」的画面。

normal.en: Paternalism holds pater, Latin for father; the state is cast as a parent.
normal.cn: paternalism 里藏着 pater（拉丁语的父亲）；国家被安排成家长角色。

normal.en: Think of a timetable pinned to the fridge for grown adults.
normal.cn: 想象一张钉在冰箱上、却给成年人看的作息表。

normal.en: Pa-ter-nal-ism: four beats, each one a decision made for you.
normal.cn: pa-ter-nal-ism：四拍，每一拍都是一个替你做的决定。

normal.en: Say puh-TUR-nuh-li-zum; the stress is on the father, not the system.
normal.cn: 读成 puh-TUR-nuh-li-zum，重音在父亲，不在制度。

normal.en: Pair it with consent: paternalism is care that forgot to ask.
normal.cn: 把它和 consent 配对：家长主义是忘了问一声的照顾。

abstract.en: Paternalism is not cruelty; it is kindness that has stopped listening.
abstract.cn: 家长主义不是残酷；它是停止了倾听的善意。

abstract.en: The test is simple: who gets to decide, and who is told afterwards.
abstract.cn: 检验很简单：谁来决定，谁事后被告知。

abstract.en: A welfare state and a mill town can share the same shape, one with forms and one with houses.
abstract.cn: 福利国家与纺织镇可以共享同一个形状，一个用表格，一个用宿舍。

examples.en: The company provided housing and a timetable, a paternalism that came with a roof.
examples.cn: 公司提供宿舍和作息表，这种家长作风还附赠一个房顶。

examples.en: The smoking ban was defended as benevolent paternalism.
examples.cn: 禁烟令被辩护为仁慈的家长式治理。

examples.en: She resented the paternalism of being told to rest.
examples.cn: 被人叫去休息时，她厌恶那种居高临下的善意。

dict_mnemonic.text: pater（父亲）+ nal + ism（主义）：像父亲一样替别人决定，就是「家长主义」。

root: 拉丁语 pater（父亲）加形容词词尾 -nal 与名词词尾 -ism

sensesIntro.en: The eight senses all put one person in the parent's chair: an employer, a state, a colony, a doctor, a law, a father, a helper and a critic.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都把一个人放上家长的位子：雇主、国家、殖民地、医生、法律、父亲、帮忙的人与批评者。

core.en: A PARENT WHO HAS ALREADY DECIDED
core.cn: 已经替所有人做完决定的家长

branches.en: A firm and a state acting as parent.
branches.cn: 像家长一样行事的公司与国家。

branches.en: A colony and a clinic, where authority is older than consent.
branches.cn: 权威早于同意的殖民地与诊所。

branches.en: A law that protects by limiting and a father who settles matters.
branches.cn: 以限制保护人的法律与替家中定事的父亲。

branches.en: Kindness delivered from above.
branches.cn: 从上面递下来的善意。

branches.en: The argument made against all of it.
branches.cn: 针对这一切提出的论证。

intro.en: The pater family is about fathers and patrons: paternal care, patronage, and a patriarchy that runs on the same root.
intro.cn: pater 词族关乎父亲与庇护者：paternal 的照顾、patronage 的庇护，以及同根运转的 patriarchy。

latinIntro.en: Latin pater supplies the father; the endings -nal and -ism turn him into a manner and then a system.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 pater 提供父亲；词尾 -nal 与 -ism 先把他变成一种态度，再变成一套制度。

items.meaning: one who acts as a father

definition_zh: 病理的；病态的；反常到近乎病态的
definition_en: of a disease, or of behaviour that seems to obey a disease rather than a will
core_image: 一片组织放到显微镜下，被放大到能看见病变的那一层
scene: 病理科把切片放到镜下，那层变化不因谁的看法而改变。The slide showed a pathological change that no argument could wish away.
sceneCN: 这里 pathological 指病理上的改变（第 1 个义项：病理学的）；句意为镜下切片显出病理性的变化，任何争辩都无法把它抹去。

pos.zh: 病理的；病态的；反常到近乎病态的

senses.title: Of disease
senses.definition: belonging to the study of disease or to a disease itself
senses.definitionCN: 属于疾病研究，或属于某种疾病本身
senses.example: The report described a pathological lesion in the lung.
senses.exampleCN: 报告描述了肺部的一处病理病变。
senses.why: This is the technical sense doctors use every day.
senses.whyCN: 这是医生每天在用的技术义。

senses.title: Pathological liar
senses.definition: of a person who lies so often that lying no longer looks like a choice
senses.definitionCN: 形容一个人说谎频繁到说谎已不像一种选择
senses.example: Her brother was a pathological liar who could not stop at the truth.
senses.exampleCN: 她弟弟是个病态说谎者，讲到真话也停不下来。
senses.why: Here the word moves from tissue to habit and still sounds clinical.
senses.whyCN: 这里词从组织移向习惯，却仍带着临床口吻。

senses.title: Pathological fear
senses.definition: of a fear far beyond the danger that caused it
senses.definitionCN: 形容恐惧远远超过引起它的危险
senses.example: He had a pathological fear of lifts and took the stairs for years.
senses.exampleCN: 他对电梯有病理性的恐惧，多年都走楼梯。
senses.why: The fear is real, but its size has no proportion to its cause.
senses.whyCN: 恐惧是真的，但它的规模与原因完全不成比例。

senses.title: Pathological gambling
senses.definition: of an impulse to gamble that overruns money, family and sleep
senses.definitionCN: 形容赌博冲动压过金钱、家庭与睡眠
senses.example: The clinic treated pathological gambling as an addiction, not a vice.
senses.exampleCN: 诊所把病态赌博当作成瘾，而不是恶习。
senses.why: The word moves the blame from character to condition.
senses.whyCN: 这个词把责备从人品移到病症。

senses.title: Pathological jealousy
senses.definition: of a suspicion that feeds on itself and needs no evidence
senses.definitionCN: 形容自我滋养、不需要证据的猜疑
senses.example: Pathological jealousy turned every late train into proof.
senses.exampleCN: 病态的嫉妒把每一班晚点列车都变成证据。
senses.why: Nothing can disprove it, which is exactly what makes it pathological.
senses.whyCN: 什么都无法反驳它，而这正是它病态之处。

senses.title: Of tissue
senses.definition: of a specimen examined for signs of disease rather than for normal structure
senses.definitionCN: 形容标本检查的是疾病迹象，而非正常结构
senses.example: The pathological specimen was kept in the teaching collection.
senses.exampleCN: 那份病理标本被保存在教学收藏里。
senses.why: Medical schools name a thing by what it shows, and this specimen shows illness.
senses.whyCN: 医学院按它显示的东西命名，而这份标本显示的是病。

senses.title: Beyond reason
senses.definition: of behaviour so fixed that argument cannot move it
senses.definitionCN: 形容行为僵硬到争论无法撼动
senses.example: His pathological punctuality made every delay feel like an insult.
senses.exampleCN: 他那近乎病态的守时，让每一次延误都像侮辱。
senses.why: The joke works because the word exaggerates a virtue into a symptom.
senses.whyCN: 这个玩笑成立，因为这个词把一种美德夸张成了症状。

senses.title: As a metaphor
senses.definition: of any habit described as if it were a disease, usually with disapproval
senses.definitionCN: 形容任何被当作疾病来描述的习惯，通常带着不赞许
senses.example: Critics called the party's pathological optimism a refusal to read the polls.
senses.exampleCN: 批评者把该党病态的乐观称为拒绝看民调。
senses.why: The metaphor borrows a doctor's authority to win an argument.
senses.whyCN: 这个比喻借来医生的权威，用来赢下一场争论。

intro.en: Pathological began at the bedside: pathos is Greek for what a body suffers, and -logia is the study of it.
intro.cn: pathological 从病床边开始：pathos 在希腊语里指身体所受的苦，-logia 是对它的研究。

items.en: Pathos meant 'suffering, disease, feeling', a word that always points at something endured.
items.cn: pathos 意为「痛苦、疾病、情感」，这个词总是指向某种被承受的东西。

items.en: -Logia meant 'study, account', the ending behind biology and theology.
items.cn: -logia 意为「研究、论述」，是 biology 与 theology 背后的词尾。

items.en: The compound pathologia named the study of disease in learned Latin.
items.cn: 复合词 pathologia 在学术拉丁语里指对疾病的研究。

items.en: English took pathology in the seventeenth century, and the adjective pathological followed it.
items.cn: 英语在十七世纪借入 pathology，形容词 pathological 随之而来。

items.en: Later centuries extended the word from tissue to habits and feelings judged beyond reason.
items.cn: 后来的世纪把这个词从组织扩展到被判为超出理性的习惯与情绪。

note.en: The look-alike group is the pathos family; the near-meaning group separates disease, compulsion and mere strangeness.
note.cn: 形近组是 pathos 词族；近义组把「疾病」「强迫」与「只是古怪」分开。

entries.definition: a doctor who reads tissue for disease.
entries.definitionCN: 通过组织判读疾病的医生。

entries.definition: in a way that belongs to disease.
driven by an urge one cannot resist.
entries.definitionCN: 被无法抵抗的冲动驱使的。

normalIntro.en: The hooks keep the picture of a slide under a lens, where what the body hid becomes visible.
normalIntro.cn: 以下联想留住「切片放到镜下、身体藏起的东西显形」的画面。

normal.en: Pathological holds pathos, Greek for suffering; the word always points at something a body or mind endures.
normal.cn: pathological 里藏着 pathos（希腊语的受苦）；这个词总指向身体或心智所承受的东西。

normal.en: Think of a slide under a microscope: the trouble is at the level of tissue, not opinion.
normal.cn: 想象镜下的一张切片：问题在组织那一层，不在看法那一层。

normal.en: Pa-tho-LO-gi-cal: put the stress on LO, where the study of disease sits.
normal.cn: pa-tho-LO-gi-cal：重音落在 LO，正是疾病研究所在。

normal.en: Say path-uh-LOJ-i-kl; the ending -logical names a field, not a patient.
normal.cn: 读成 path-uh-LOJ-i-kl，词尾 -logical 命名的是一个领域，不是病人。

normal.en: Pair it with liar and gambler: the word turns a habit into a diagnosis.
normal.cn: 把它和 liar、gambler 配对：这个词把习惯变成了诊断。

abstract.en: A word that began in the morgue ends up in arguments about habits, because both involve something that will not answer reason.
abstract.cn: 一个从停尸房开始的词，最后进了关于习惯的争论，因为两者都涉及某种不回应理性的东西。

abstract.en: Calling a behaviour pathological is a polite way of saying it has stopped being a choice.
abstract.cn: 把一种行为称为病态，是「它已不再是选择」的礼貌说法。

abstract.en: The word's authority is medical; its most common work is moral.
abstract.cn: 这个词的权威来自医学，它最常干的活却是道德评判。

examples.en: The slide showed a pathological change that no argument could wish away.
examples.cn: 镜下显出病理性的变化，任何争辩都无法把它抹去。

examples.en: The clinic treated pathological gambling as an addiction, not a vice.
examples.cn: 诊所把病态赌博当作成瘾，而不是恶习。

examples.en: His pathological punctuality made every delay feel like an insult.
examples.cn: 他那近乎病态的守时，让每一次延误都像侮辱。

dict_mnemonic.text: patho（病）+ logical（逻辑）：按病灶的逻辑行事，就是「病态的」。

root: 希腊语 pathos（痛苦、疾病）与 -logia（学说），经拉丁语 pathologia 进入英语

sensesIntro.en: The eight senses begin at the microscope and end at the dinner table: tissue, lying, fear, gambling, jealousy, a specimen, punctuality and a party's optimism.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从显微镜下开始，到餐桌上结束：组织、说谎、恐惧、赌博、嫉妒、标本、守时与一个政党的乐观。

core.en: A SLIDE THAT SHOWS WHAT THE BODY HIDES
core.cn: 镜下显出身体藏起来的那一层

branches.en: The clinic and the specimen.
branches.cn: 诊所与标本。

branches.en: Lying and fear, habits wearing a symptom's shape.
branches.cn: 说谎与恐惧，带着症状形状的习惯。

branches.en: Gambling and jealousy, appetites that feed themselves.
branches.cn: 赌博与嫉妒，自我喂养的欲望。

branches.en: Punctuality pushed past the edge of virtue.
branches.cn: 被推过美德边界的守时。

branches.en: The metaphor borrowed for an argument.
branches.cn: 为一场争论借来的比喻。

intro.en: The pathos family is about what is suffered: pathology studies it, a pathogen causes it, sympathy feels it with another person.
intro.cn: pathos 词族关乎被承受的苦：pathology 研究它，pathogen 引起它，sympathy 与另一个人一同感受它。

latinIntro.en: Greek pathos supplies the suffering and -logia supplies the study; the prefixes syn- and a- only decide whether the feeling is shared or absent.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊语 pathos 提供苦，-logia 提供研究；前缀 syn- 与 a- 只决定这份感受是被分担还是缺席。

definition_zh: 必然地；不得已地；被迫地
definition_en: by necessity, because no other course of action is open
core_image: 一扇门后面所有的岔路都已封死，只剩一条路可以走
scene: 合同时限一到，两边都知道再拖也没用，只能在纸上落笔。The deadline closed every other route, and perforce both sides signed the same settlement.
sceneCN: 这里 perforce 指迫不得已地（第 1 个义项：不得不然）；句意为截止期限封死了别的路，双方只好签下同一份和解。

pos.zh: 必然地；不得已地；被迫地

senses.title: By necessity
senses.definition: because no alternative exists, so the step must be taken
senses.definitionCN: 因为不存在别的选项，所以这一步非走不可
senses.example: The bridge was gone, and the travellers perforce waited for the boat.
senses.exampleCN: 桥断了，旅人只得等船。
senses.why: This is the plainest sense: the road itself has closed.
senses.whyCN: 这是最朴素的义项：路本身已经封了。

senses.title: Under compulsion
senses.definition: because someone or something has taken the choice away
senses.definitionCN: 因为某人或某物已经把选择拿走
senses.example: The village perforce gave up its well to the new road.
senses.exampleCN: 村子被迫把水井让给了新修的路。
senses.why: Here the pressure has an author, even if the author is never named.
senses.whyCN: 这里压力有个施加者，哪怕施加者从未被点名。

senses.title: Logical consequence
senses.definition: because the premises leave no other conclusion standing
senses.definitionCN: 因为前提不给别的结论留下位置
senses.example: If every witness is lying, the alibi perforce fails.
senses.exampleCN: 如果每个证人都说谎，那不在场证明就必然站不住。
senses.why: In argument the word marks a step that cannot be avoided, not a person who is forced.
senses.whyCN: 在论证里，这个词标记一个绕不开的步骤，而不是一个被强迫的人。

senses.title: Legal compulsion
senses.definition: because a statute or a court requires the act
senses.definitionCN: 因为法令或法院要求这样做
senses.example: The tenant perforce vacated the flat within the month.
senses.exampleCN: 租客只得在一个月内腾出公寓。
senses.why: The force behind it is a document that can be enforced.
senses.whyCN: 它背后的力量是一份可以强制执行的文书。

senses.title: Diplomatic necessity
senses.definition: because the balance of power allows nothing else
senses.definitionCN: 因为力量对比不允许别的做法
senses.example: The small state perforce followed its larger neighbour's line.
senses.exampleCN: 这个小国只得跟随较大邻国的路线。
senses.why: Here nobody is ordered, and yet the choice is already narrow.
senses.whyCN: 这里没人下命令，选择却已经很窄。

senses.title: By armed force
senses.definition: the older sense: by physical force, with weapons behind it
senses.definitionCN: 较古老的义项：凭体力与武力，背后有兵器
senses.example: The gate was perforce opened, and the town taken before dawn.
senses.exampleCN: 城门被强行打开，天没亮镇子就失守了。
senses.why: This is the oldest layer of the phrase, where force meant soldiers.
senses.whyCN: 这是这个短语最古老的一层，force 那时指兵。

senses.title: Reluctant consent
senses.definition: agreement given because refusing would cost more
senses.definitionCN: 因为拒绝代价更高而给出的同意
senses.example: She perforce agreed to the plan her partners had already sold.
senses.exampleCN: 她勉强同意了合伙人早已卖出去的计划。
senses.why: The signature is real, which is what makes the word bitter.
senses.whyCN: 签名是真的，而这正是这个词苦涩的地方。

senses.title: Narrative inevitability
senses.definition: the sense in stories, where events could not have gone otherwise
senses.definitionCN: 故事里的那种意味：事情不可能有别的走向
senses.example: The letters perforce crossed at sea, and each blamed the other for silence.
senses.exampleCN: 那些信必然在海上交错而过，两人都为沉默责怪对方。
senses.why: A storyteller uses the word to make accident look like structure.
senses.whyCN: 讲故事的人用这个词，让偶然看起来像结构。

intro.en: Perforce is two words welded into one adverb: through, and force.
intro.cn: perforce 是两个词焊成一个副词：凭借，与力量。

items.en: Fortis meant 'strong', the root behind force, fort and effort.
