items.cn: fortis 意为「强壮」，是 force、fort 与 effort 的词根。

items.en: Old French force carried both 'strength' and 'a body of troops'.
items.cn: 古法语 force 既指「力量」，也指「一队兵」。

items.en: The phrase par force meant 'by force', and English took it over as one word.
items.cn: 短语 par force 意为「凭武力」，英语把它整个接过来，写成了一词。

items.en: Perforce appears in Middle English as an adverb of necessity.
items.cn: perforce 在中古英语里作为表必然的副词出现。

items.en: Today it survives in formal and literary prose, where it sounds slightly archaic.
items.cn: 今天它多半活在正式与文学性的文字里，听起来略嫌古旧。

note.en: The look-alike group is the force family; the near-meaning group keeps necessity, compulsion and inevitability apart.
note.cn: 形近组是 force 词族；近义组把「必然」「强制」与「不可避免」分开。

entries.definition: strength or power used on someone.
entries.definitionCN: 施加于人的力量或强力。

entries.definition: in a way that cannot be avoided.
in a way that cannot be prevented.

normalIntro.en: The hooks keep the picture of a corridor with every other door sealed.
normalIntro.cn: 以下联想留住「走廊上别的门都被封住」的画面。

normal.en: Perforce is par force in Old French: by force, and therefore by necessity.
normal.cn: perforce 就是古法语的 par force：凭力量，于是也就凭必然。

normal.en: Per- means through; force means strength; the road is forced through.
normal.cn: per- 意为穿过，force 意为力量：路是被力量推着穿过去的。

normal.en: Per-FORCE: the stress sits on force, exactly where the pressure is.
normal.cn: per-FORCE：重音落在 force 上，正是压力所在。

normal.en: Say per-FORSS, two syllables with no pause between them.
normal.cn: 读成 per-FORSS，两个音节中不容停顿。

normal.en: Pair it with had to: perforce is had to compressed into one word.
normal.cn: 把它和 had to 配对：perforce 就是把 had to 压成一个词。

abstract.en: The word always describes a choice that has already closed.
abstract.cn: 这个词总是描述一个已经关上了的选择。

abstract.en: It sounds archaic because modern prose prefers had to or was forced to.
abstract.cn: 它听起来古旧，因为现代文章更喜欢说 had to 或 was forced to。

abstract.en: Perforce is the quiet admission that freedom was smaller than it looked.
abstract.cn: perforce 是一句安静的承认：自由比它看起来的要小。

examples.en: The deadline closed every other route, and perforce both sides signed the same settlement.
examples.cn: 截止期限封死了别的路，双方只好签下同一份和解。

examples.en: The bridge was gone, and the travellers perforce waited for the boat.
examples.cn: 桥断了，旅人只得等船。

examples.en: She perforce agreed to the plan her partners had already sold.
examples.cn: 她勉强同意了合伙人早已卖出去的计划。

dict_mnemonic.text: per（凭借）+ force（力量）：被力量推着走，就是「不得已」。

root: 古法语 par force（凭武力），源出拉丁语 per（通过）与 fortis（强壮的）

sensesIntro.en: The eight senses all describe a door that has closed: a road, a village, an argument, a statute, a balance of power, an army, a signature and a story.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都在描述一扇已经关上的门：一条路、一个村子、一个论证、一条法令、一份力量对比、一支军队、一个签名与一个故事。

core.en: A DOOR THAT ONLY OPENS ONE WAY

branches.en: Necessity in fact and necessity in argument.
branches.cn: 事实上的必然与论证上的必然。

branches.en: Compulsion from outside and consent that costs less.
branches.cn: 来自外部的强制与代价更小的同意。

branches.en: A statute and a balance of power.
branches.cn: 一条法令与一份力量对比。

branches.en: The oldest layer: by armed force.
branches.cn: 最古老的一层：以武力。

branches.en: The storyteller's sense that it could not be otherwise.
branches.cn: 叙事者那种「不可能有别的结果」的意味。

intro.en: The force family is about strength applied: enforce puts it behind a rule, reinforce puts it behind a wall, forcible describes the result.
intro.cn: force 词族关乎被施加的力量：enforce 把它放在规则背后，reinforce 把它放在墙背后，forcible 描述结果。

latinIntro.en: Latin fortis supplies the strength, and per- supplies the direction through which the strength travels.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 fortis 提供力量，per- 提供力量穿行而过的方向。

items.meaning: to put force behind a rule

definition_zh: 悲观主义者；总是预期最坏结果的人
definition_en: a person who expects the worst outcome, either as a philosophy or as a habit
core_image: 一桌人正在吃饭，有人已经先在心里把菜算成了不够
scene: 每回开新项目，他先数会出问题的地方，大家干脆叫他悲观主义者。At every new project he counted what could go wrong, and the team called him a pessimist before the first week ended.
sceneCN: 这里 pessimist 指团队里的悲观者（第 2 个义项：惯于悲观的性格）；句意为每个新项目他都先数会出问题的地方，第一周还没过团队就这样叫他。

pos.zh: 悲观主义者；总是预期最坏结果的人

senses.title: Philosophical pessimist
senses.definition: one who holds that life holds more pain than good and that this cannot be repaired
senses.definitionCN: 认为生命中的苦多于好、且无法修补的人
senses.example: Schopenhauer is usually read as the philosophical pessimist.
senses.exampleCN: 叔本华通常被读作哲学上的悲观主义者。
senses.why: This sense is a position argued in books, not a mood on a given morning.
senses.whyCN: 这个义项是书里论证的立场，不是某个早晨的心情。

senses.title: Habitual pessimist
senses.definition: a person whose first guess about any outcome is the bad one
senses.definitionCN: 对任何结果的第一猜测都是坏结果的人
senses.example: He is the office pessimist, and he is usually right.
senses.exampleCN: 他是办公室里的悲观者，而且通常猜对。
senses.why: Here the word describes a reflex, not a theory.
senses.whyCN: 这里描述的是条件反射，不是理论。

senses.title: Economic pessimist
senses.definition: one who expects markets to fall and hard times to last
senses.definitionCN: 预期市场下跌、艰难时期持续的人
senses.example: The economist was a pessimist about the housing market.
senses.exampleCN: 这位经济学家对住房市场持悲观看法。
senses.why: Forecasts make the word public: a view with dates and numbers attached.
senses.whyCN: 预测让这个词变得公开：一个带日期与数字的看法。

senses.title: Pessimist as realist
senses.definition: a person who calls his gloom a clear look at the facts
senses.definitionCN: 把自己的阴郁称为对事实的清醒审视的人
senses.example: Every pessimist claims he is simply a realist.
senses.exampleCN: 每个悲观者都说自己只是个现实主义者。
senses.why: The word is often a label the speaker rejects while using it.
senses.whyCN: 这个词常是说话者一边用、一边拒绝的标签。

senses.title: Team pessimist
senses.definition: the member who lists the risks before anyone has chosen a name
senses.definitionCN: 在别人还没定名之前就先列出风险的那个人
senses.example: The team pessimist saved them from a costly launch.
senses.exampleCN: 团队里那个泼冷水的人让他们避免了一次代价高昂的上市。
senses.why: In groups the word can be a criticism or a quiet compliment.
senses.whyCN: 在群体里，这个词可以是批评，也可以是一句安静的称赞。

senses.title: Temperamental pessimist
senses.definition: a mood that expects loss before any evidence has arrived
senses.definitionCN: 证据还没出现就先预期损失的心情
senses.example: Her pessimist's mood lifted only on the last day.
senses.exampleCN: 她那悲观的心情直到最后一天才松开。
senses.why: The noun reaches for a temperament, which is older than any argument.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词指向一种性情，它比任何论证都更早存在。

senses.title: Pessimist about people
senses.definition: one who doubts that people will act well without pressure
senses.definitionCN: 怀疑人在没有压力时就会好好行事的人
senses.example: The old judge was a pessimist about human nature.
senses.exampleCN: 这位老法官对人性的看法很悲观。
senses.why: This sense is about other people, not about one's own fortune.
senses.whyCN: 这个义项关乎别人，而非自己的运气。

senses.title: Stock figure
senses.definition: the cartoon figure imagined to enjoy bad news
senses.definitionCN: 卡通里那个被想象成爱听坏消息的形象
senses.example: The pessimist of the cartoons is never invited to the party.
senses.exampleCN: 卡通里的悲观的家伙从来不在被邀请之列。
senses.why: The stereotype is a joke about the word, not a description of it.
senses.whyCN: 这个刻板印象是关于这个词的笑话，不是对它的描述。

intro.en: Pessimist comes from the Latin superlative for 'worst': the mind has already gone to the bottom of the scale.
intro.cn: pessimist 来自拉丁语表示「最坏」的最高级：心已经先走到了刻度最底。

items.en: Pessimus meant 'worst', the superlative of malus, 'bad'.
items.cn: pessimus 意为「最坏」，是 malus（坏）的最高级。

items.en: Malus supplied a whole family: malice, malign, malady.
items.cn: malus 提供了一整族词：malice、malign、malady。

items.en: Pessimism was coined in the eighteenth century as the opposite of optimism.
items.cn: pessimism 在十八世纪被造出，作为 optimism 的反面。

items.en: The word grew out of the argument over whether this is the best of all possible worlds.
items.cn: 这个词从「这是否是可能世界中最好的一个」的争论里长出来。

items.en: Schopenhauer and others turned the label into a system, and the person into a pessimist.
items.cn: 叔本华等人把这个标签变成体系，也把人变成 pessimist。

note.en: The look-alike group is the pessimism family; the near-meaning group separates the cynic, the defeatist and the doomsayer.
note.cn: 形近组是 pessimism 词族；近义组把「愤世者」「失败主义者」与「末日预言者」分开。

entries.definition: the belief that the bad outweighs the good.
in a way that expects the worst.
one who trusts no one's motives.
entries.definitionCN: 不信任任何人动机的人。

entries.definition: one who expects to lose and acts on it.
entries.definitionCN: 预期失败并据此行事的人。

normalIntro.en: The hooks keep the picture of a person who has already counted the plates and found them short.
normalIntro.cn: 以下联想留住「有人已经数过盘子、先算出不够」的画面。

normal.en: Pessimist holds pessimus, Latin for worst: the mind starts at the bottom of the scale.
normal.cn: pessimist 里藏着 pessimus（拉丁语的「最坏」）：心从刻度最底开始。

normal.en: Think of a dinner guest who counts the plates before the food arrives.
normal.cn: 想象一位客人，菜还没上就先数盘子。

normal.en: Pes-si-MIST: the stress sits on mis, and the mist is already closing in.
normal.cn: pes-si-MIST：重音落在 mis 上，雾也已经合拢。

normal.en: Say PESS-uh-mist; the first syllable already sounds like a sigh.
normal.cn: 读成 PESS-uh-mist，第一个音节已经像一声叹气。

normal.en: Pair it with optimist: the two words are the same machine, running in opposite directions.
normal.cn: 把它和 optimist 配对：两个词是同一台机器，朝相反方向转。

abstract.en: A pessimist is not always wrong; he is a person whose guesses are graded on a steeper curve.
abstract.cn: 悲观者不总是错的；他只是把猜测放在一条更陡的曲线上评分。

abstract.en: The word can name a philosophy, a temperament or an office role, and only the first one has arguments.
abstract.cn: 这个词可以命名一种哲学、一种性情或一个办公室角色，其中只有第一种带论证。

abstract.en: Every pessimist keeps a small hope somewhere, which is why the word is never quite stable.
abstract.cn: 每个悲观者心里都留着一点希望，所以这个词从不十分稳定。

examples.en: The team called him a pessimist before the first week ended.
examples.cn: 第一周还没过，团队就叫他悲观主义者。

examples.en: The economist was a pessimist about the housing market.
examples.cn: 这位经济学家对住房市场持悲观看法。

examples.en: Every pessimist claims he is simply a realist.
examples.cn: 每个悲观者都说自己只是个现实主义者。

dict_mnemonic.text: pessim（最坏）+ ist（人）：总把结果往最坏处算的人，就是「悲观主义者」。

root: 拉丁语 pessimus（最坏的），malus（坏）的最高级，加 -ist（表人后缀）

sensesIntro.en: The eight senses move from a system in a book to a face at a party: a philosophy, a habit, a forecast, a claim, a team role, a temperament, a view of people and a cartoon.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从书里的体系走到聚会上的那张脸：哲学、习惯、预测、自我辩解、团队角色、性情、对人性的看法与一个卡通形象。

core.en: A SCALE THAT STARTS AT THE BOTTOM

chain: THE MIND GOES TO THE WORST

branches.en: A position argued in books.
branches.cn: 书里论证过的立场。

branches.en: A reflex and a temperament, both older than argument.
branches.cn: 条件反射与性情，都比论证更早。

branches.en: A forecast with dates and a role inside a team.
branches.cn: 带日期的预测与团队里的角色。

branches.en: The claim to realism and the verdict on other people.
branches.cn: 自称现实与对他人的判断。

branches.en: The cartoon figure that the word now drags behind it.
branches.cn: 这个词如今拖在身后的卡通形象。

intro.en: The pessimism family is a small seesaw: pessimism at one end, optimism at the other, and the same -ism and -ist endings on both.
intro.cn: pessimism 词族是一副小跷跷板：一端是 pessimism，一端是 optimism，两边用的都是 -ism 与 -ist。

latinIntro.en: Latin pessimus supplies 'worst' and malus supplies 'bad'; the endings -ism and -ist turn a judgement into a system and a person.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 pessimus 提供「最坏」，malus 提供「坏」；词尾 -ism 与 -ist 把一个判断变成体系与人。

items.exampleCN: 一个固执的乐观主义者。

items.meaning: a bad condition of the body

definition_zh: 使石化；使吓呆；使僵化
definition_en: to turn into stone, or to make a person or an institution unable to move
core_image: 一滴含矿物的水长年滴在木头上，木头慢慢变成了石头
scene: 他站在门口，看见母亲的脸色，整个人像被浇成了石头。He stood in the doorway, saw his mother's face, and felt the news petrify him where he stood.
sceneCN: 这里 petrify 指吓得整个人僵住（第 3 个义项：使吓呆）；句意为他在门口看见母亲的脸色，那条消息把他吓得当场僵住。

senses.title: Turn to stone
senses.definition: to change organic matter into stone over a long period
senses.definitionCN: 在漫长岁月里把有机物变成石头
senses.example: The wood had petrified under layers of ash.
senses.exampleCN: 那木头在层层火山灰下已经石化。
senses.why: This is the mineral sense, slow and geological.
senses.whyCN: 这是矿物义，缓慢而地质性。

senses.title: Fossilize
senses.definition: to preserve a living shape by replacing its substance with stone
senses.definitionCN: 用石头替换原有物质，把生命的形状保存下来
senses.example: The fallen forest was petrified by mineral water.
senses.exampleCN: 倒下的森林被含矿物的水化成了石头。
senses.why: Preservation and loss happen in the same motion.
senses.whyCN: 保存与失去在同一次动作里发生。

senses.title: Terrify
senses.definition: to frighten someone so badly that the body will not obey
senses.definitionCN: 把某人吓到身体不听使唤
senses.example: The sound from the cellar petrified the child.
senses.exampleCN: 地窖里传来的声音把那孩子吓呆了。
senses.why: The figurative sense borrows the literal one: fear turns a person to stone.
senses.whyCN: 比喻义借用了字面义：恐惧把人变成石头。

senses.title: Freeze in place
senses.definition: to leave a person standing still, as if the limbs had hardened
senses.definitionCN: 让人站在原地不动，好像四肢已经变硬
senses.example: She was petrified at the top of the stairs.
senses.exampleCN: 她在楼梯顶端僵住了。
senses.why: The body's stillness is the whole point of the metaphor.
senses.whyCN: 身体的静止正是这个比喻的全部要点。

senses.title: Institutional paralysis
senses.definition: to make an organisation unable to change or to act
senses.definitionCN: 让一个机构无法改变或行动
senses.example: Fear of blame had petrified the department.
senses.exampleCN: 对追责的恐惧让这个部门僵化了。
senses.why: Institutions can be petrified too, and they last longer than people.
senses.whyCN: 机构也会被石化，而且比人持续得更久。

senses.title: Hardening of feeling
senses.definition: to make a feeling or a heart stiff and unyielding
senses.definitionCN: 让一种情感或一颗心变得僵硬、不肯弯折
senses.example: Grief had petrified what was left of their kindness.
senses.exampleCN: 悲伤把他们剩下的善意也硬化了。
senses.why: The word can describe a defence that has outlived its use.
senses.whyCN: 这个词可以描述一种已经超出用途的防御。

senses.title: Shock into silence
senses.definition: to leave a room or a person unable to speak
senses.definitionCN: 让一个房间或一个人说不出话
senses.example: The verdict petrified the courtroom.
senses.exampleCN: 判决让整个法庭惊呆了。
senses.why: Silence after shock is the social form of standing still.
senses.whyCN: 震惊后的沉默，是僵立的社交版本。

senses.title: Petrifying spring
senses.definition: to encrust objects with stone, as mineral water does
senses.definitionCN: 像含矿物的水那样给物体裹上一层石壳
senses.example: The spring petrified the branches that fell into it.
senses.exampleCN: 那眼泉水把落进去的枝条裹成了石头。
senses.why: Water here does the work that time does elsewhere, only faster.
senses.whyCN: 这里水做的是别处时间做的事，只是快得多。

intro.en: Petrify is rock plus making: the word simply says 'to make stone'.
intro.cn: petrify 是「岩石」加「使成为」：这个词说的就是「使变成石头」。

items.en: Petra meant 'rock or stone', the word behind petrous and petroleum.
items.cn: petra 意为「岩石」，是 petrous 与 petroleum 背后的词。

items.en: Latin kept petra unchanged, and the church built a whole name on it.
items.cn: 拉丁语原样保留 petra，教会还在它上面造出了一整个名号。

items.en: The ending -fy comes from facere, 'to make', as in simplify and solidify.
items.cn: 词尾 -fy 来自 facere（使成为），如 simplify 与 solidify。

items.en: English formed petrify in the sixteenth century for the mineral process.
items.cn: 英语在十六世纪造出 petrify，指矿化过程。

items.en: The sense of fright came later: a frightened body behaves like hardened stone.
items.cn: 受惊的义项出现得更晚：受惊的身体像硬了的石头。

note.en: The look-alike group is the petra family; the near-meaning group separates terror, fossilisation and literal hardening.
note.cn: 形近组是 petra 词族；近义组把「恐惧」「化石化」与字面意义上的变硬分开。

entries.definition: turned to stone, or frozen by fear.
entries.definitionCN: 石化的，或被恐惧冻住的。

entries.definition: the process of turning to stone.
turns to stone or freezes another.
to turn into bone or become rigid.

normalIntro.en: The hooks keep the picture of mineral water slowly turning a branch into stone.
normalIntro.cn: 以下联想留住「含矿物的水把枝条慢慢变成石头」的画面。

normal.en: Petrify holds petra, Greek for rock, and -fy, to make: to make rock.
normal.cn: petrify 里藏着 petra（希腊语的岩石）与 -fy（使成为）：使变成岩石。

normal.en: Think of a branch in a mineral spring: it keeps its shape and loses its wood.
normal.cn: 想象矿物泉里的一根枝条：形状还在，木头没了。

normal.en: Pet-ri-FY: the stress sits on pet, and the rest is the making.
normal.cn: pet-ri-FY：重音落在 pet，其余部分是「使成为」。

normal.en: Say PET-ruh-fye; the first syllable is short, like a tap on stone.
normal.cn: 读成 PET-ruh-fye，第一音节短促，像敲一下石头。

normal.en: Pair it with fear: a frightened witness is a person who has been petrified.
normal.cn: 把它和 fear 配对：被吓住的证人，就是一个被石化的人。

abstract.en: The literal and the figurative senses share one idea: something alive stops moving.
abstract.cn: 字面义与比喻义共享一个想法：活着的东西停止移动。

abstract.en: Stone is what remains when the soft part leaves, which is why the word suits both fossils and fear.
abstract.cn: 石头是柔软部分离开后留下的东西，所以这个词既适合化石也适合恐惧。

abstract.en: An institution can be petrified without any rock at all; it simply stops answering new questions.
abstract.cn: 机构可以没有一点石头也被石化，它只是不再回答新问题。

examples.en: He felt the news petrify him where he stood.
examples.cn: 那条消息把他吓得当场僵住。

examples.en: The fallen forest was petrified by mineral water.
examples.cn: 倒下的森林被含矿物的水化成了石头。

examples.en: Fear of blame had petrified the department.
examples.cn: 对追责的恐惧让这个部门僵化了。

dict_mnemonic.text: petri（岩石）+ fy（使成为）：使变成石头，人被吓到也会「僵成石头」。

root: 希腊语 petra（岩石）经拉丁语 petra 进入英语，加 -fy（使成为，源自 facere）

sensesIntro.en: The eight senses all end in stillness: mineral replacement, a fossil, a frightened body, a frozen posture, a stuck institution, a hardened heart, a silent court and a spring that coats whatever falls in.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都以静止收尾：矿物替换、化石、受惊的身体、僵住的姿势、卡住的机构、硬化的心、无声的法庭与一眼给落物裹壳的泉。

core.en: A BRANCH THAT KEEPS ITS SHAPE AND LOSES ITS WOOD
core.cn: 保住形状、失去木质的枝条

branches.en: Stone replacing wood, slowly.
branches.cn: 石头缓慢地替换木头。

branches.en: A frightened body that will not obey.
branches.cn: 不听使唤的受惊身体。

branches.en: A stuck institution and a hardened heart.
branches.cn: 卡住的机构与硬化的心。

branches.en: A room that has gone silent.
branches.cn: 一个静下来的房间。

branches.en: Water doing in a year what time does in an age.
branches.cn: 水在一年里做时间在一个纪元里做的事。

intro.en: The petra family is about rock: petrous describes the hard bone at the base of the skull, petroleum is rock oil, and petrify is rock-making.
intro.cn: petra 词族关乎岩石：petrous 描述颅底的硬骨，petroleum 是岩中之油，petrify 是造石。

latinIntro.en: Greek petra passes into Latin unchanged, and the suffix -ficare, from facere, supplies the 'making' in every -fy verb.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊语 petra 原样进入拉丁语，而来自 facere 的后缀 -ficare 为每个 -fy 动词提供「使成为」。

definition_zh: 尖顶；顶峰；极点；浪尖
definition_en: the highest point of a building, a rock, a career or a wave
core_image: 一座石塔最上面那个细尖，风只能从它旁边绕过去
scene: 他四十五岁那年坐上公司最高一层，别人说这就是顶峰。At forty-five he took the top floor of the firm, and everyone said he had reached the pinnacle.
sceneCN: 这里 pinnacle 指事业的顶峰（第 3 个义项：事业顶峰）；句意为他在四十五岁那年坐上公司最高一层，人人都说他已到顶峰。

senses.title: Architectural pinnacle
senses.definition: a small pointed ornament on a roof, a tower or a buttress
senses.definitionCN: 屋顶、塔身或扶壁上的小尖状装饰
senses.example: Each pinnacle of the chapel carried a carved saint.
senses.exampleCN: 礼拜堂的每个尖顶上都雕着一位圣人。
senses.why: This is the oldest sense, and it is still the most exact.
senses.whyCN: 这是最古老的义项，也仍是最精确的一个。

senses.title: Rocky point
senses.definition: a sharp point of rock standing above a ridge
senses.definitionCN: 山脊之上凸起的一块尖锐岩石
senses.example: The last pinnacle could be climbed only on a rope.
senses.exampleCN: 最后那座岩峰只能靠绳索攀上去。
senses.why: Stone and stone ornament share a shape, so the word carried over easily.
senses.whyCN: 岩石与石饰共享同一个形状，词就这样轻易地移了过去。

senses.title: Career peak
senses.definition: the highest point that a working life reaches
senses.definitionCN: 职业生涯所达到的最高处
senses.example: She reached the pinnacle of her profession at fifty.
senses.exampleCN: 她在五十岁到达本行的顶峰。
senses.why: Careers are imagined as mountains, which is why the word fits.
senses.whyCN: 事业被想象成山，所以这个词合用。

senses.title: Peak of achievement
senses.definition: the best result a skill or an art has produced so far
senses.definitionCN: 一门技艺或艺术迄今产生的最好结果
senses.example: That quartet remains the pinnacle of his chamber music.
senses.exampleCN: 那首四重奏至今仍是他室内乐的顶点。
senses.why: The word ranks works, not only people.
senses.whyCN: 这个词给作品排名，不只给人排名。

senses.title: Pinnacle of fashion
senses.definition: the moment when a style is most admired
senses.definitionCN: 一种风格最受推崇的那一刻
senses.example: The narrow silhouette was the pinnacle of fashion that year.
senses.exampleCN: 那一年窄身廓形正是时尚之巅。
senses.why: Taste also builds peaks, and it moves them every season.
senses.whyCN: 品味也会堆出山峰，而且每季挪动一次。

senses.title: Social pinnacle
senses.definition: the top of a social order, seen as a place where one stands
senses.definitionCN: 社会秩序的最高处，被看作可以站上去的位置
senses.example: The family had climbed to the pinnacle of local society.
senses.exampleCN: 这家人已爬到本地社会的顶层。
senses.why: Here the height is a rank, not a rock.
senses.whyCN: 这里的「高」是等级，不是岩石。

senses.title: Final point
senses.definition: the last and highest point of a rise, after which comes the descent
senses.definitionCN: 上升过程中最后也是最高的一点，之后就是下降
senses.example: The road reached its pinnacle above the tree line.
senses.exampleCN: 路在树线以上到达最高点。
senses.why: The word names a turning point as well as a height.
senses.whyCN: 这个词既命名高度，也命名转折点。

senses.title: Wave crest
senses.definition: the top of a wave, where a surfer tries to stand
senses.definitionCN: 波浪的最高处，冲浪者想站上去的地方
senses.example: He held the board on the pinnacle for a full second.
senses.exampleCN: 他在浪尖上把板稳住了整整一秒。
senses.why: Water makes a temporary pinnacle, and the word grants it the same honour.
senses.whyCN: 水造出临时的峰顶，词也给它同样的尊称。

intro.en: Pinnacle began as a little feather: Latin pinna meant 'wing', and its diminutive named a small point.
intro.cn: pinnacle 起初是一根小羽毛：拉丁语 pinna 指「翼」，它的指小形式命名了一个小尖。

items.en: Pinna meant 'feather or wing', and also named the feather-shaped parts of a building.
items.cn: pinna 意为「羽毛或翼」，也用来称建筑上羽状的部件。

items.en: The diminutive pinnaculum meant 'a small point or peak'.
items.cn: 指小形式 pinnaculum 意为「小尖、小峰」。

items.en: Old French took the word as pinacle and kept the architectural sense.
items.cn: 古法语把它接作 pinacle，保留了建筑义。

items.en: English borrowed pinacle for the ornament on a roof or a buttress.
items.cn: 英语借入 pinacle，指屋顶或扶壁上的装饰尖。

items.en: Later the word climbed: careers, styles and even waves acquired pinnacles.
items.cn: 后来这个词往上爬：事业、风格甚至波浪都有了 pinnacle。

note.en: The look-alike group is the pinna family; the near-meaning group separates summit, apex, zenith and peak.
note.cn: 形近组是 pinna 词族；近义组把「山顶」「顶点」「天顶」与「高峰」分开。

entries.definition: a feather, or the outer ear.
the highest point of a shape.
a pointed top or a highest value.

normalIntro.en: The hooks keep the picture of the thin stone point that the wind has to go around.
normalIntro.cn: 以下联想留住「风只能绕着走的那根细石尖」的画面。

normal.en: Pinnacle holds pinna, Latin for feather: a small pointed thing, light and sharp.
normal.cn: pinnacle 里藏着 pinna（拉丁语的羽毛）：一个小小的尖物，轻而尖。

normal.en: Think of a chapel roof: every corner finishes in a carved point.
normal.cn: 想象礼拜堂的屋顶：每个转角都收成一个雕花尖。

normal.en: Pin-na-CLE: the last syllable is the little peak itself.
normal.cn: pin-na-CLE：最后一个音节就是那个小峰。

normal.en: Say PIN-uh-kl; the first syllable is as short as the point is thin.
normal.cn: 读成 PIN-uh-kl，第一音节短得像那个尖一样细。

normal.en: Pair it with career: a career is a mountain that the word lets you climb.
normal.cn: 把它和 career 配对：事业是一座由这个词允许你攀爬的山。

abstract.en: A pinnacle is always relative: remove the mountain and the point is only a stone.
abstract.cn: 顶点总是相对的：抽掉那座山，尖也只是一块石头。

abstract.en: The word suits both buildings and lives because both are judged by their highest part.
abstract.cn: 这个词同时适合建筑与人生，因为两者都按最高处被评判。

abstract.en: Every pinnacle implies a slope behind it, which is why the word often carries a warning.
abstract.cn: 每个顶点都暗示身后有一段坡，所以这个词常带警告。

examples.en: Everyone said he had reached the pinnacle of the firm.
examples.cn: 人人都说他已经到了公司的顶峰。

examples.en: That quartet remains the pinnacle of his chamber music.
examples.cn: 那首四重奏至今仍是他室内乐的顶点。

examples.en: He held the board on the pinnacle for a full second.
examples.cn: 他在浪尖上把板稳住了整整一秒。

dict_mnemonic.text: pin（针）+ nacle：像针一样细尖的顶，就是「尖顶」，也引申为「顶峰」。

root: 拉丁语 pinna（羽毛、翼）的指小形式 pinnaculum（小尖），经古法语 pinacle 进入英语

sensesIntro.en: The eight senses climb one shape: an ornament on a roof, a rock, a career, a work of art, a style, a social rank, the top of a road and the crest of a wave.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都在攀爬同一个形状：屋顶上的饰物、岩石、事业、艺术作品、风格、社会等级、路的最高处与浪尖。

core.en: A THIN POINT ABOVE EVERYTHING ELSE

chain: THE POINT IS SEEN FROM BELOW

branches.en: Carved stone and living rock.
branches.cn: 雕过的石头与活着的岩石。

branches.en: A working life and a work of art.
branches.cn: 一段职业生涯与一件艺术作品。

branches.en: A season's taste and a town's ladder.
branches.cn: 一季的品味与一座城的阶梯。

branches.en: The point after which the road descends.
branches.cn: 路在此之后开始下降的那一点。

branches.en: A peak that lasts one second.
branches.cn: 只存在一秒的峰。

intro.en: The pinna family is about feathers and points: a pinnate leaf is feather-shaped, and a pinnacle is the point a feather makes in stone.
intro.cn: pinna 词族关乎羽毛与尖：pinnate 的叶子是羽状的，而 pinnacle 是羽毛在石头里留下的那个尖。

latinIntro.en: Latin pinna gives the feather, pinnaculum gives the small point, and English keeps both the roof sense and the height sense.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 pinna 给出羽毛，pinnaculum 给出小尖；英语把屋顶义与高度义都留了下来。

items.example: A pinniped such as a seal.

definition_zh: 论战文章；激烈争论；论战
definition_en: a strong written or spoken attack on a position, made to win rather than to understand
core_image: 一篇小册子，页边写满批注，每个句子都像在挥拳
scene: 那本小册子没有数据，只有火气，读起来是一篇论战。The pamphlet carried no figures, only heat, and read like a polemic from its first page.
sceneCN: 这里 polemic 指论战文章（第 1 个义项：论战文章）；句意为那本小册子没有数据，只有火气，从第一页起就像一篇论战。

pos.zh: 论战文章；激烈争论；论战

senses.title: Written attack
senses.definition: a piece of writing that argues hard against a position
senses.definitionCN: 针对某一立场强硬地展开攻击的文字
senses.example: His polemic against the new tax ran to forty pages.
senses.exampleCN: 他反对新税的那篇论战写了四十页。
senses.why: The word names the piece itself, not the person who wrote it.
senses.whyCN: 这个词命名文章本身，而不是写文章的人。

senses.title: Spoken attack
senses.definition: a speech or a broadcast that fights a case in public
senses.definitionCN: 在公开场合为某一立场开火的演讲或广播
senses.example: The radio polemic ended with three names read aloud.
senses.exampleCN: 那场广播论战以念出三个名字收尾。
senses.why: The mouth can carry a polemic as well as a page.
senses.whyCN: 嘴也能承载论战，不只是纸面。

senses.title: Genre
senses.definition: a style that puts argument before evidence
senses.definitionCN: 把论证放在证据之前的文体
senses.example: The essay is a polemic in form, whatever its footnotes say.
senses.exampleCN: 无论注释怎么写，这篇文章在形式上都是论战。
senses.why: The genre is recognised by its posture, not by its topic.
senses.whyCN: 这个文体靠姿态被认出，不靠题目。

senses.title: Religious polemic
senses.definition: controversy over doctrine conducted in pamphlets and sermons
senses.definitionCN: 用小册子与布道进行的教义争论
senses.example: Seventeenth-century religious polemic was a blood sport.
senses.exampleCN: 十七世纪的宗教论战是一场见血的运动。
senses.why: The oldest home of the word is the pamphlet war.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最古老的家是小册子之战。

senses.title: Political polemic
senses.definition: argument aimed at a party or a policy rather than at a person
senses.definitionCN: 指向一个政党或一项政策、而非某个人的争论
senses.example: The editorial was political polemic dressed as analysis.
senses.exampleCN: 那篇社论是披着分析外衣的政治论战。
senses.why: Politics gave the word its modern audience.
senses.whyCN: 政治给了这个词现代的听众。

senses.title: Against criticism
senses.definition: attack that seeks victory rather than understanding
senses.definitionCN: 追求胜负而非理解的攻击
senses.example: A review asks what a book is; a polemic asks who is right.
senses.exampleCN: 书评问这本书是什么，论战问谁是对的。
senses.why: The difference is the goal, not the temperature.
senses.whyCN: 差别在目的，不在温度。

senses.title: Polemicist's stance
senses.definition: the posture of a writer who treats an opponent as an enemy
senses.definitionCN: 写作者把对手当作敌人的那种姿态
senses.example: The polemicist never lets the other side finish a sentence.
senses.exampleCN: 论战者从不让对方说完一句话。
senses.why: Here the noun describes a role as much as a text.
senses.whyCN: 这里名词既描述文本，也描述角色。

senses.title: Argument as noise
senses.definition: heat without substance, argument performed for an audience
senses.definitionCN: 没有实质的火气，演给观众看的争论
senses.example: The panel dissolved into polemic before the first question.
senses.exampleCN: 第一个问题还没问完，讨论组就沦为一团攻讦。
senses.why: The word can dismiss as easily as it can praise.
senses.whyCN: 这个词既能称赞，也一样能打发。

intro.en: Polemic comes from the Greek word for war: an argument imagined as a campaign with a front line.
intro.cn: polemic 来自希腊语的「战争」：争论被想象成一场有前线的战役。

items.en: Polemos meant 'war', the plain noun behind the whole family.
items.cn: polemos 意为「战争」，是整族词背后那个朴素的名称。

items.en: Polemikos meant 'of war, warlike', an adjective for things that fight.
items.cn: polemikos 意为「战争的、好战的」，是形容交战之物的形容词。

items.en: Latin took polemicus for controversial writing, especially in theology.
items.cn: 拉丁语用 polemicus 指争论性的文字，尤其在神学里。

items.en: English borrowed polemic during the pamphlet wars of the seventeenth century.
items.cn: 英语在十七世纪的小册子之战中借入了 polemic。

items.en: Newspapers and parties later moved the word from doctrine to policy.
items.cn: 报纸与政党后来把这个词从教义移向政策。

note.en: The look-alike group is the polemos family; the near-meaning group separates diatribe, invective, tirade and critique.
note.cn: 形近组是 polemos 词族；近义组把「谩骂」「恶语」「长篇指责」与「评论」分开。

entries.definition: a careful judgement of a work.

normalIntro.en: The hooks keep the picture of a pamphlet whose margins are all fists.
normalIntro.cn: 以下联想留住「一本页边全是拳头的册子」的画面。

normal.en: Polemic holds polemos, Greek for war: the page is a front line.
normal.cn: polemic 里藏着 polemos（希腊语的战争）：纸面就是前线。

normal.en: Think of a pamphlet with no numbers in it, only heat.
normal.cn: 想象一本没有数字、只有火气的小册子。

normal.en: Po-LE-mic: the stress sits on le, and the word leans forward.
normal.cn: po-LE-mic：重音落在 le，整个词向前倾。

normal.en: Say POH-luh-mik; the flat first syllable is the calm before the attack.
normal.cn: 读成 POH-luh-mik，平的第一音节是攻击前的安静。

normal.en: Pair it with critique: a critique wants to understand, a polemic wants to win.
normal.cn: 把它和 critique 配对：critique 想理解，polemic 想赢。

abstract.en: A polemic is an argument that has decided the answer before the evidence arrives.
abstract.cn: 论战是一个在证据到齐前就已经定了答案的论证。

abstract.en: The word is borrowed from war, which is why it never sounds like a seminar.
abstract.cn: 这个词借自战争，所以它从不像研讨会。

abstract.en: Polemic can be brave or cheap; the word records the fighting, not the worth of it.
abstract.cn: 论战可以是勇敢的，也可以是廉价的；这个词记录战斗，不记录价值。

examples.en: The pamphlet read like a polemic from its first page.
examples.cn: 那本小册子从第一页起就像一篇论战。

examples.en: His polemic against the new tax ran to forty pages.
examples.cn: 他反对新税的那篇论战写了四十页。

examples.en: A review asks what a book is; a polemic asks who is right.
examples.cn: 书评问这本书是什么，论战问谁是对的。

dict_mnemonic.text: pole（杆）+ mic（麦克风）：举着杆子对着麦克风开火，就是「论战」。

root: 希腊语 polemos（战争）与 -ikos（形容词词尾），经拉丁语 polemicus 进入英语

sensesIntro.en: The eight senses are one fight in different rooms: a page, a microphone, a genre, a church, a parliament, a review, a writer's posture and a panel that has stopped listening.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项是同一场战斗换在不同的房间：纸面、麦克风、文体、教会、议会、书评、写作者的姿态，以及一个已经不再倾听的讨论组。

core.en: A PAMPHLET WITH FISTS IN THE MARGINS

chain: THE ARGUMENT ENDS IN A SCORE

branches.en: A page and a microphone.
branches.cn: 纸面与麦克风。

branches.en: A style that puts argument first.
branches.cn: 把论证放在最前的文体。

branches.en: A church and a parliament.
branches.cn: 教会与议会。

branches.en: The difference from criticism and the writer's stance.
branches.cn: 与批评的差别，以及写作者的姿态。

branches.en: Heat with nothing behind it.
branches.cn: 背后空空的火气。

intro.en: The polemos family is small and warlike: polemic is the fight, polemics is the practice, a polemicist is the fighter.
intro.cn: polemos 词族小而好战：polemic 是那场战斗，polemics 是作战的做法，polemicist 是作战的人。

latinIntro.en: Greek polemos supplies the war, and the ending -ikos, Latin -icus, turns it into an adjective of controversy.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊语 polemos 提供战争，词尾 -ikos（拉丁语 -icus）把它变成争论的形容词。

items.example: The two editors polemicized in public.
items.exampleCN: 两位主编曾在公开场合论战。

definition_zh: 浮夸；自负的做派；铺张的排场
definition_en: the quality of being self-important in speech, manner or display
core_image: 一个人把嗓门和姿势都放大一号，好让整个房间都看见他
scene: 主席台上的人清了三次嗓子才开口，那份排场让整个礼堂都发闷。The speaker cleared his throat three times before beginning, and the pomposity of the ceremony made the hall feel airless.
sceneCN: 这里 pomposity 指仪式上的铺张排场（第 4 个义项：仪式铺张）；句意为台上的人清了三次嗓子才开口，那种排场让整个礼堂都发闷。

pos.zh: 浮夸；自负的做派；铺张的排场

senses.title: Inflated speech
senses.definition: language made larger than the thought behind it
senses.definitionCN: 语言被放得比它背后的想法更大
senses.example: The minister's pomposity turned a short answer into ten minutes.
senses.exampleCN: 部长那套浮夸把一个简短回答拖成了十分钟。
senses.why: The vice here is proportion: words outrunning meaning.
senses.whyCN: 这里的毛病是比例：言辞跑到了意义前面。

senses.title: Self-important manner
senses.definition: a bearing that asks to be taken seriously before anything has been said
senses.definitionCN: 还没开口就先要求被认真对待的姿态
senses.example: He entered every room with a pomposity that no joke could dent.
senses.exampleCN: 他进每个房间都带着一种玩笑撼不动的自负。
senses.why: The body performs the claim even when the mouth is silent.
senses.whyCN: 即使嘴不出声，身体也在表演那个主张。

senses.title: Institutional display
senses.definition: the ceremony an organisation stages to make its power visible
senses.definitionCN: 机构为让权力可见而搭起的仪式
senses.example: The bank's pomposity showed in its marble and its waiting times.
senses.exampleCN: 这家银行的排场体现在大理石和等待时间上。
senses.why: Institutions borrow the word from people and make it architecture.
senses.whyCN: 机构从人那里借来这个词，然后把它变成建筑。

senses.title: Ceremonial display
senses.definition: the swell of robes, titles and announcements at a formal event
senses.definitionCN: 正式场合里袍服、头衔与宣告的层层堆叠
senses.example: The pomposity of the ceremony made the hall feel airless.
senses.exampleCN: 仪式的铺张让整个礼堂都发闷。
senses.why: This sense is about staging, not about any one speaker.
senses.whyCN: 这个义项关乎舞台布置，不关乎某一位说话者。

senses.title: Ornate prose
senses.definition: writing that prefers the long word and the balanced clause
senses.definitionCN: 偏爱长词与对仗句子的写作
senses.example: The essay's pomposity hides a very simple argument.
senses.exampleCN: 这篇文章的夸饰掩着一个非常简单的论点。
senses.why: Style can be a way of making a small idea look furnished.
senses.whyCN: 文风可以让一个小想法看起来陈设齐全。

senses.title: Self-importance
senses.definition: a settled belief that one's own rank deserves attention
senses.definitionCN: 一种稳定的信念：自己的地位理应得到关注
senses.example: Her pomposity was not an act; she had believed it for years.
senses.exampleCN: 她的自命不凡不是表演；她已经信了很多年。
senses.why: Here the word names a belief rather than a performance.
senses.whyCN: 这里这个词命名一种信念，而不是一场表演。

senses.title: Pomposity as mask
senses.definition: display used to cover uncertainty or a lack of substance
senses.definitionCN: 用来遮住不确定或内容不足的排场
senses.example: The pomposity of the new director was a shield for his fear.
senses.exampleCN: 新主管的浮夸是他恐惧的一面盾。
senses.why: The word can be read backwards, as a confession.
senses.whyCN: 这个词可以反过来读，当成一句自白。

senses.title: Comic pomposity
senses.definition: the lovable version, where the speaker is undone by his own dignity
senses.definitionCN: 可爱的那一面：说话者被自己的尊严绊倒
senses.example: The chairman's pomposity was the best part of the annual dinner.
senses.exampleCN: 主席那份端架子是年度晚宴上最好看的部分。
senses.why: Comedy often needs the word to be dear rather than cruel.
senses.whyCN: 喜剧常需要这个词显得可亲，而不是刻薄。

intro.en: Pomposity is the noun of a procession: pomp was the show that walked through a city, and the word kept the swagger.
intro.cn: pomposity 是一场游行的名词：pomp 曾是穿过城市的展示，这个词留下了那份招摇。

items.en: Pompe meant 'a sending, a procession', the escort that walked a god or a ruler through a city.
items.cn: pompe 意为「送出、游行」，指护送神祇或统治者穿过城市的队列。

items.en: Latin pompa kept the sense of a public show with music and robes.
items.cn: 拉丁语 pompa 保留了那种带音乐与袍服的公开展示。

items.en: Late Latin pomposus meant 'full of display', and it carried a hint of excess from the start.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语 pomposus 意为「充满排场」，从一开始就带着过度的暗示。

items.en: English took pompous, and pomposity followed as its noun.
items.cn: 英语借入 pompous，pomposity 作为其名词随后出现。

items.en: By the eighteenth century the noun was chiefly a criticism, as it still is.
items.cn: 到十八世纪，这个名词主要是一种批评，至今仍是。

note.en: The look-alike group is the pomp family; the near-meaning group separates pretension, grandiosity, bombast and mere pride.
note.cn: 形近组是 pomp 词族；近义组把「做作」「夸大」「浮词」与「单纯的自豪」分开。

entries.definition: a claim to importance one lacks.
entries.definitionCN: 对并不具备的重要性的声称。

entries.definition: a swollen sense of one's own scale.
an exaggerated sense of one's worth.
entries.definitionCN: 对自身价值的夸大的感觉。

normalIntro.en: The hooks keep the picture of a man who has turned his voice and his chin up one size.
normalIntro.cn: 以下联想留住「一个人把嗓门和下巴都放大一号」的画面。

normal.en: Pomposity holds pomp, the old word for a procession: the show is still walking.
normal.cn: pomposity 里藏着 pomp（古语里的游行）：那场展示还在走。

normal.en: Think of a speaker clearing his throat three times before a short sentence.
normal.cn: 想象一位说话者，短短一句话前清了三次嗓子。

normal.en: Pom-POS-i-ty: the stress sits on pos, and the word puffs itself up.
normal.cn: pom-POS-i-ty：重音落在 pos，整个词把自己吹了起来。

normal.en: Say pom-PAH-si-ti; the middle vowel opens wide like a held note.
normal.cn: 读成 pom-PAH-si-ti，中间那个元音张开得像一个拖长的音符。

normal.en: Pair it with airless: pomposity makes a room feel short of oxygen.
normal.cn: 把它和 airless 配对：浮夸让房间显得缺氧。

abstract.en: Pomposity is a matter of proportion: it is not size, but size without content.
abstract.cn: 浮夸是比例问题：不是大，而是没有内容的大。

abstract.en: The word began as the name of a parade and ended as a name for a bore.
abstract.cn: 这个词起初是一场游行的名字，最后成了无聊之人的名字。

abstract.en: Every pomposity contains a small fear that the audience will notice the gap.
abstract.cn: 每一份浮夸里都藏着一点恐惧：怕观众发现那个空隙。

examples.en: The speaker cleared his throat three times, and the pomposity made the hall feel airless.
examples.cn: 说话的人清了三次嗓子，那份浮夸让礼堂发闷。

examples.en: The essay's pomposity hides a very simple argument.
examples.cn: 这篇文章的夸饰掩着一个非常简单的论点。

examples.en: The chairman's pomposity was the best part of the annual dinner.
examples.cn: 主席那份端架子是年度晚宴上最好看的部分。

dict_mnemonic.text: pomp（排场）+ osity：把排场做到过分，就是「浮夸、自负」。

root: 希腊语 pompe（游行、送出）经拉丁语 pompa 与 pomposus 进入英语

sensesIntro.en: The eight senses are one inflated thing seen from eight angles: words, bearing, an institution, a ceremony, a prose style, a belief, a mask and a joke.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项是同一个被吹大的东西的八个侧面：言辞、姿态、机构、仪式、文风、信念、面具与笑话。

core.en: A VOICE AND A CHIN TURNED UP ONE SIZE
core.cn: 被放大一号的嗓门与下巴

branches.en: Words and written style, both larger than the thought.
branches.cn: 言辞与文风，都比想法更大。

branches.en: A bearing and a belief.
branches.cn: 一种姿态与一种信念。

branches.en: An institution and a ceremony.
branches.cn: 机构与仪式。

branches.en: Display used as a shield.
branches.cn: 当作盾牌用的排场。

branches.en: The version an audience can love.
branches.cn: 观众能喜欢的那一面。

intro.en: The pomp family is about display: pomp is the show, pompous is the person who carries it, pomposity is the quality left in the air afterwards.
intro.cn: pomp 词族关乎展示：pomp 是那场展示，pompous 是端着它的人，pomposity 是散场后留在空气里的那种性质。

latinIntro.en: Greek pompe gives the procession, Latin pompa gives the show, and the ending -ositas turns all of it into a quality to be judged.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊语 pompe 给出游行，拉丁语 pompa 给出展示，词尾 -ositas 把这一切变成一种可被评判的性质。

definition_zh: 合成词；旅行皮箱；合成的
definition_en: a word made by packing two words into one, or an old travelling case with two compartments
core_image: 一只旧皮箱，中间一道隔板，两边各自装得满满的
scene: 行李架上那只旧皮箱一边装衣服，一边装书，是地道的两格式。On the rack the old portmanteau held clothes on one side and books on the other, exactly as its name promises.
sceneCN: 这里 portmanteau 指两格式旅行皮箱（第 1 个义项：旅行皮箱）；句意为行李架上那只旧皮箱一边装衣服、一边装书，正合它名字的许诺。

senses.title: Travelling case
senses.definition: an old leather case that opens into two equal halves
senses.definitionCN: 一种打开后分成两个相等半边的旧皮箱
senses.example: The porter set the portmanteau down at the foot of the stairs.
senses.exampleCN: 搬运工把那只旅行皮箱放在楼梯脚下。
senses.why: This is the literal object, and it explains the metaphor.
senses.whyCN: 这是字面的物件，而它解释了那个比喻。

senses.title: Packed word
senses.definition: a word made by joining two words and keeping sounds from both
senses.definitionCN: 把两个词拼合、两边各留一部分读音造出的词
senses.example: Smog is a portmanteau of smoke and fog.
senses.exampleCN: smog 是 smoke 与 fog 的合成词。
senses.why: Two things are packed into one case, exactly like clothes and books.
senses.whyCN: 两样东西被装进一只箱子，正像衣服与书。

senses.title: Linguistic blend
senses.definition: the technical name for a blend that cuts each source word in the middle
senses.definitionCN: 对各自从源词中段截取的混合词的技术称呼
senses.example: The class collected portmanteaus and sorted them by seam.
senses.exampleCN: 课上收集了一批混合词，按接缝分类。
senses.why: Linguists use the term for the seam, not for the joke.
senses.whyCN: 语言学家用这个词指那道接缝，不是指那个笑话。

senses.title: Portmanteau adjective
senses.definition: an adjective that carries two ideas at once, as in a portmanteau role
senses.definitionCN: 同时承载两个意思的形容词，如 a portmanteau role
senses.example: Critics called the part a portmanteau adjective: mother and manager in one.
senses.exampleCN: 评论者把这角色称为复合修饰语：母亲与经理合一。
senses.why: Grammar borrowed the trunk and packed two labels into it.
senses.whyCN: 语法借来这只箱子，往里装了两个标签。

senses.title: Political coinage
senses.definition: a campaign word built by welding two policies together
senses.definitionCN: 把两项政策焊在一起造出的竞选词
senses.example: The slogan was a portmanteau designed to offend nobody.
senses.exampleCN: 那句口号是一个谁也不得罪的合成词。
senses.why: Politics loves the form because a blend can promise twice.
senses.whyCN: 政治喜欢这种形式，因为混合词可以许诺两遍。

senses.title: Brand name
senses.definition: a product name made from two familiar words so it feels new and known
senses.definitionCN: 用两个熟悉的词造出的产品名，既新又已知
senses.example: The company's name was a portmanteau of its two founders' towns.
senses.exampleCN: 公司的名字是两位创始人故乡地名的合成。
senses.why: Commerce uses the form to make a strange thing sound familiar.
senses.whyCN: 商业用这种形式让陌生的东西听起来熟悉。

senses.title: Compression
senses.definition: any phrase that folds two ideas into one word to save space
senses.definitionCN: 任何为省空间把两个想法折进一个词的表达
senses.example: His style is all portmanteau: every noun doing two jobs.
senses.exampleCN: 他的文风全是压缩：每个名词都在干两份活。
senses.why: The word can describe a habit of speech, not a single coinage.
senses.whyCN: 这个词可以描述一种说话习惯，而不只是一个新造词。

senses.title: Old travelling gear
senses.definition: the baggage of an earlier century, now mostly a word in novels
senses.definitionCN: 上一个世纪的行李，如今多半只是小说里的一个词
senses.example: The novel's heroine travelled with one portmanteau and no maid.
senses.exampleCN: 小说女主人公只带一只皮箱，没带侍女。
senses.why: Objects outlive their usefulness and survive as images.
senses.whyCN: 物件熬过自己的用途，作为形象活下来。

intro.en: Portmanteau is French for 'carry the cloak': a case built to hold a coat in one half and everything else in the other.
intro.cn: portmanteau 在法语里意为「携带斗篷」：这只箱子一半放外套，一半放别的东西。

items.en: Porter meant 'to carry', from Latin portare.
items.cn: porter 意为「携带」，源自拉丁语 portare。

items.en: Manteau meant 'cloak or coat', from Latin mantellus.
items.cn: manteau 意为「斗篷、外套」，源自拉丁语 mantellus。

items.en: The compound portemanteau named the officer who carried a prince's cloak, and then the case itself.
items.cn: 复合词 portemanteau 先指替君主携斗篷的官员，后指那只箱子本身。

items.en: English borrowed the case in the sixteenth century and kept the French spelling.
items.cn: 英语在十六世纪借入这只箱子，并保留了法语拼法。

items.en: In 1871 Carroll called smog-like coinages 'portmanteau words', and the second life began.
items.cn: 一八七一年卡罗尔把 smog 这类新造词称为「合成词」，这个词的第二条命就此开始。

note.en: The look-alike group is the portare family; the near-meaning group separates blend, coinage, neologism and compound.
note.cn: 形近组是 portare 词族；近义组把「混合词」「新造词」「新语」与「复合词」分开。

entries.definition: cases, or blended words, in the plural.
the carrying of goods between waters.
a word made from parts of two others.
entries.definitionCN: 由两个词的部分构成的词。

entries.definition: a word made of two whole words.
entries.definitionCN: 由两个完整词构成的词。

normalIntro.en: The hooks keep the picture of one case with a divider down the middle and both halves full.
normalIntro.cn: 以下联想留住「一只中间有隔板、两半都装满的箱子」的画面。

normal.en: Portmanteau is porter plus manteau: carry the coat.
normal.cn: portmanteau 是 porter 加 manteau：携带外套。

normal.en: Think of a suitcase split in two, clothes on one side and books on the other.
normal.cn: 想象一只分成两半的手提箱，一边衣服，一边书。

normal.en: Port-man-TOW: the stress sits on tow, where the carrying happens.
normal.cn: port-man-TOW：重音落在 tow，正是搬运发生处。

normal.en: Say port-MAN-toh; the middle syllable is the handle you hold.
normal.cn: 读成 port-MAN-toh，中间那个音节就是你握的把手。

normal.en: Pair it with smog: the case and the word work the same way.
normal.cn: 把它和 smog 配对：箱子和词用的是同一种办法。

abstract.en: A portmanteau word is a suitcase for meaning: two things packed so tightly that the seam shows.
abstract.cn: 合成词是意义的行李箱：两样东西塞得太紧，接缝都露了出来。

abstract.en: The object disappeared from travel and survived in grammar, which is a strange kind of promotion.
abstract.cn: 这只物件从旅行里消失了，却在语法里活下来，这是一种奇怪的升迁。

abstract.en: The word asks a simple question of any blend: can you still see both halves?
abstract.cn: 这个词对任何混合词只问一句：两半你还看得见吗？

examples.en: Smog is a portmanteau of smoke and fog.
examples.cn: smog 是 smoke 与 fog 的合成词。

examples.en: The porter set the portmanteau down at the foot of the stairs.
examples.cn: 搬运工把那只旅行皮箱放在楼梯脚下。

examples.en: The slogan was a portmanteau designed to offend nobody.
examples.cn: 那句口号是一个谁也不得罪的合成词。

dict_mnemonic.text: porter（携带）+ manteau（外套）：装外套的箱子，后来也指「把两词装进一个」的合成词。

root: 法语 porter（携带）与 manteau（外套）合成的 portemanteau，源自拉丁语 portare 与 mantellus

sensesIntro.en: The eight senses are one case with two compartments: a travel object, a packed word, a linguistic seam, a double adjective, a campaign slogan, a brand name, a compressed style and a novel's luggage.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项是同一只有两个隔层的箱子：旅行物件、被塞满的词、语言学接缝、双义形容词、竞选口号、品牌名、压缩文风与小说里的行装。

core.en: ONE CASE WITH TWO COMPARTMENTS
core.cn: 一只有两个隔层的箱子

branches.en: The object, real and remembered.
branches.cn: 真实的物件与被记住的物件。

branches.en: The word and the linguistic name for it.
branches.cn: 词本身与对它的语言学称呼。

branches.en: Two ideas in one modifier.
branches.cn: 一个修饰语里的两个想法。

branches.en: A slogan and a brand.
branches.cn: 一句口号与一个品牌。

branches.en: A whole style that packs two jobs into one word.
branches.cn: 把两份活压进一个词的整套文风。

intro.en: The portare family is about carrying: a porter carries bags, a portfolio carries leaves, and a portmanteau carries a coat.
intro.cn: portare 词族关乎携带：porter 搬行李，portfolio 携纸页，portmanteau 携外套。

latinIntro.en: Latin portare supplies the carrying and Latin mantellus supplies the cloak; French welded them into one object and English borrowed it twice.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 portare 提供携带，mantellus 提供斗篷；法语把它们焊成一件物，英语借了两次。

definition_zh: 君主；统治者；有权势的人
definition_en: a ruler who holds power in his own right, especially one who rules without limits
core_image: 一个人坐在高背椅上，整片土地的地契都压在他脚边
scene: 那一带的土地都在他名下，连警察也要先向他问好。In that district every field was in his name, and even the police greeted the potentate before asking anything.
sceneCN: 这里 potentate 指地方上的权势者（第 4 个义项：地方土皇帝）；句意为那一带的土地全在他名下，连警察也要先向这位权势者问好才开口。

pos.zh: 君主；统治者；有权势的人

senses.title: Absolute ruler
senses.definition: a ruler whose power has no constitution above it
senses.definitionCN: 权力之上没有宪法的统治者
senses.example: The potentate answered to no assembly and no court.
senses.exampleCN: 这位专制君主不对任何议会与法庭负责。
senses.why: The word marks the absence of a higher authority.
senses.whyCN: 这个词标记更高权威的缺席。

senses.title: Feudal lord
senses.definition: a lord who holds land and people as personal property
senses.definitionCN: 把土地与人当作私产的领主
senses.example: The potentate of the valley taxed every cart that crossed.
senses.exampleCN: 谷地的领主对每辆过路车征税。
senses.why: Power here is measured in acres and in men who owe labour.
senses.whyCN: 这里的力量以亩数与欠工的人来计算。

senses.title: Modern strongman
senses.definition: a leader who keeps the forms of a state and the habits of a throne
senses.definitionCN: 保留国家形式、却带着王座习惯的领导人
senses.example: The general became a potentate in all but the title.
senses.exampleCN: 这位将军除头衔之外，已经成了君主。
senses.why: Modern politics keeps the word for the gap between form and fact.
senses.whyCN: 现代政治保留这个词，用来指形式与事实之间的缝隙。

senses.title: Local boss
senses.definition: a person whose power over one district is total and personal
senses.definitionCN: 在一区内拥有完全而私人的权力的人
senses.example: Even the police greeted the potentate before asking anything.
senses.exampleCN: 连警察也要先向这位地方权势者问好才开口。
senses.why: The word scales down well: a district can hold a small throne.
senses.whyCN: 这个词缩小尺寸也很好用：一个区就能容下一张小王座。

senses.title: Corporate potentate
senses.definition: an owner or executive who runs a company like a private domain
senses.definitionCN: 把公司当作私人领地来经营的老板或高管
senses.example: The founder was a potentate of his own factory town.
senses.exampleCN: 这位创始人就是他工厂镇的君主。
senses.why: Money can build a court even where there is no crown.
senses.whyCN: 即使没有王冠，钱也能造出一座宫廷。

senses.title: As a title
senses.definition: the formal word used in treaties for a sovereign who signs
senses.definitionCN: 条约里用来称呼签约君主的正式用词
senses.example: The treaty named each potentate and each heir.
senses.exampleCN: 这份条约逐一列出每位君主与每位继承人。
senses.why: Diplomacy needs a neutral word that does not rank its signers.
senses.whyCN: 外交需要一个不替签字者排座次的中性称呼。

senses.title: Petty potentate
senses.definition: a ruler of very little territory who behaves as if it were an empire
senses.definitionCN: 领地极小却按帝国排场行事的统治者
senses.example: The petty potentate built a palace with three gates.
senses.exampleCN: 这位小国之君造了一座有三道门的宫殿。
senses.why: The word often carries irony when the domain is small.
senses.whyCN: 当领地很小时，这个词常带反讽。

senses.title: Figure of satire
senses.definition: the stock powerful man whom satirists dress in robes
senses.definitionCN: 讽刺作家给穿上袍子的那种权势人物
senses.example: The cartoon potentate wore a crown made of share certificates.
senses.exampleCN: 漫画里的权势者戴着一顶由股票凭证做的王冠。
senses.why: Satire borrows the word because it already sounds oversized.
senses.whyCN: 讽刺借来这个词，因为它本来就显得尺码过大。

intro.en: Potentate comes from the Latin verb 'to be able': the word begins as a statement about capacity and ends as a claim about right.
intro.cn: potentate 来自拉丁语「能够」的动词：这个词从关于能力的陈述开始，以关于权利的宣称收尾。

items.en: Posse meant 'to be able, to have power', the verb behind potent, possible and power.
items.cn: posse 意为「能够、有力量」，是 potent、possible 与 power 背后的动词。

items.en: The participle potens meant 'powerful', used of gods, kings and medicines alike.
items.cn: 分词 potens 意为「强有力的」，神、王与药都用它。

items.en: Potentatus meant 'power, dominion, the rank of a ruler'.
items.cn: potentatus 意为「权力、统治、统治者的位阶」。

items.en: English borrowed potentate for a sovereign who rules in his own name.
items.cn: 英语借入 potentate，指以自己名义统治的君主。

items.en: Today the word is mostly historical or ironic, kept for rulers who look out of date.
items.cn: 今天这个词多半是历史性或反讽的，留给那些显得过时的统治者。

note.en: The look-alike group is the posse family; the near-meaning group separates monarch, autocrat, despot and magnate.
note.cn: 形近组是 posse 词族；近义组把「君主」「独裁者」「暴君」与「巨头」分开。

entries.definition: power that is not yet used.

entries.definitionCN: 权力不受限制的统治者。

entries.definition: a ruler who governs by will alone.

normalIntro.en: The hooks keep the picture of a high-backed chair with the district's deeds piled at its feet.
normalIntro.cn: 以下联想留住「一张高背椅，脚边堆着全区的地契」的画面。

normal.en: Potentate holds potens, Latin for powerful: the word is potency wearing a crown.
normal.cn: potentate 里藏着 potens（拉丁语的强有力的）：这个词就是戴上王冠的效力。

normal.en: Think of a chair taller than the table, so everyone must look up.
normal.cn: 想象一张比桌子还高的椅子，所有人都得抬头。

normal.en: Po-ten-TATE: the stress sits on tate, and the word ends like a title.
normal.cn: po-ten-TATE：重音落在 tate，词尾听起来像一个头衔。

normal.en: Say POH-tuhn-tayt; the middle syllable is swallowed, as servants are.
normal.cn: 读成 POH-tuhn-tayt，中间音节被吞掉，就像仆人一样。

normal.en: Pair it with petty: the smaller the domain, the funnier the word.
normal.cn: 把它和 petty 配对：领地越小，这个词越好笑。

abstract.en: Potentate is power with no one above it, which is why the word rarely survives a constitution.
abstract.cn: potentate 是上方无人的权力，所以这个词很少活得过一部宪法。

abstract.en: The word began as a fact about strength and ended as a complaint about rights.
abstract.cn: 这个词起初是关于力量的事实，最后成了关于权利的抱怨。

abstract.en: Every potentate needs a court, because power without an audience is only capacity.
abstract.cn: 每位君主都需要一座宫廷，因为没有观众的权力只是能力。

examples.en: Even the police greeted the potentate before asking anything.
examples.cn: 连警察也要先向这位权势者问好才开口。

examples.en: The potentate answered to no assembly and no court.
examples.cn: 这位专制君主不对任何议会与法庭负责。

examples.en: The petty potentate built a palace with three gates.
examples.cn: 这位小国之君造了一座有三道门的宫殿。

dict_mnemonic.text: potent（有力量的）+ ate：手里握着全部力量的人，就是「君主、权势者」。

root: 拉丁语 potens（强有力的，源自 posse「能够」）的派生名词 potentatus

sensesIntro.en: The eight senses are one chair in different rooms: a throne, a valley, a modern state, a district, a company, a treaty, a tiny palace and a cartoon.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项是同一把椅子摆在不同房间：王座、谷地、现代国家、一个区、一家公司、一份条约、一座小宫殿与一幅漫画。

core.en: A CHAIR WITH NO ONE ABOVE IT

branches.en: The ruler in law and in treaty.
branches.cn: 法律中的统治者与条约中的统治者。

branches.en: Land held as a person's own.
branches.cn: 被当作私产持有的土地。

branches.en: A modern state and a company town.
branches.cn: 现代国家与公司镇。

branches.en: A district boss and a tiny empire.
branches.cn: 一个区的地头蛇与一个小帝国。

branches.en: The figure satire dresses in robes.
branches.cn: 讽刺给它穿上袍子的形象。

intro.en: The posse family is about capacity: potent is strong, potential is strength not yet spent, omnipotent is strength with no limit.
intro.cn: posse 词族关乎能力：potent 是强，potential 是尚未花掉的力量，omnipotent 是没有上限的力量。

latinIntro.en: Latin posse supplies the ability, potens supplies the strength, and -atus turns it into an office a man can hold.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 posse 提供能力，potens 提供力量，-atus 把它变成一个人可以坐上的位子。

definition_zh: 序言；前言；开场白；铺垫
definition_en: the part that comes before the main text or the main point
core_image: 一队人走在前面开路，真正的队伍还没出现
scene: 他没寒暄，也没铺垫，直接说出结论。He offered no greeting and no preamble, and gave the conclusion first.
sceneCN: 这里 preamble 指讲话前的开场铺垫（第 3 个义项：讲话开场）；句意为他没有寒暄、也没有铺垫，开口就是结论。

senses.title: Constitutional preamble
senses.definition: the opening paragraph that states why a constitution exists
senses.definitionCN: 说明宪法为何存在的开篇段落
senses.example: The preamble begins with the words 'We the people'.
senses.exampleCN: 序言以「我们人民」这几个字开头。
senses.why: Here the opening carries legal weight and is quoted in court.
senses.whyCN: 这里开篇承载法律效力，会在法庭上被引用。

senses.title: Treaty preamble
senses.definition: the section that names the parties and the purpose before the articles
senses.definitionCN: 在条款之前点明各方与目的的段落
senses.example: The treaty's preamble listed three reasons and no promises.
senses.exampleCN: 条约序言列了三条理由，没有一条承诺。
senses.why: Diplomacy puts its intentions first so that the rules can follow.
senses.whyCN: 外交把意图放在前面，好让规则随后跟上。

senses.title: Speech opening
senses.definition: the remarks made before the point is reached
senses.definitionCN: 在进入正题之前的几句交代
senses.example: He offered no greeting and no preamble, and gave the conclusion first.
senses.exampleCN: 他没有寒暄也没有铺垫，开口就是结论。
senses.why: In speech the word measures patience rather than law.
senses.whyCN: 在讲话里，这个词衡量的是耐心，不是法律。

senses.title: Legal recital
senses.definition: the statement of facts a document must recite before its operative clauses
senses.definitionCN: 文件在生效条款之前必须陈述的事实
senses.example: The deed's preamble recited the old boundary twice.
senses.exampleCN: 这份契据的前提陈述把旧边界写了两遍。
senses.why: Law requires the story before the command.
senses.whyCN: 法律要求先讲故事，再下命令。

senses.title: Warning prologue
senses.definition: words that prepare a listener for bad news
senses.definitionCN: 为坏消息作准备的几句话
senses.example: His preamble about 'difficult decisions' told the room what was coming.
senses.exampleCN: 他关于「艰难决定」的铺垫让全屋人都知道要出什么。
senses.why: A preamble can soften a blow or announce it.
senses.whyCN: 铺垫可以减轻打击，也可以预告它。

senses.title: Book preface
senses.definition: the few pages in which an author explains the book's aim
senses.definitionCN: 作者用几页说明本书目的的篇幅
senses.example: The preamble thanks four libraries and no readers.
senses.exampleCN: 绪言感谢了四家图书馆，一个读者也没提。
senses.why: Publishing kept the word for the author's own voice.
senses.whyCN: 出版业保留这个词，指作者自己的声音。

senses.title: Empty preamble
senses.definition: a formal opening with nothing behind it
senses.definitionCN: 背后空空的程式化开场
senses.example: The report buried its one fact under a long preamble.
senses.exampleCN: 这份报告把唯一的事实埋在一段冗长开场下面。
senses.why: The word turns critical when the opening outgrows the text.
senses.whyCN: 当开场长得超过正文，这个词就变得带批评意味。

senses.title: Any preparation
senses.definition: whatever is said or done to set up what follows
senses.definitionCN: 为使后文成立而先说的话或先做的事
senses.example: The apology was only a preamble to the request.
senses.exampleCN: 那句道歉只是请求之前的铺垫。
senses.why: This is the loosest sense, and the most common in speech.
senses.whyCN: 这是最宽松的义项，也是口语里最常见的。

intro.en: Preamble is a walking word: prae- means before, and ambulare means to walk, so the preamble walks in front.
intro.cn: preamble 是一个「走路」的词：prae- 意为在前，ambulare 意为行走，所以序言是在前面走的那部分。

items.en: Ambulare meant 'to walk', the verb behind amble and ambulance.
items.cn: ambulare 意为「行走」，是 amble 与 ambulance 背后的动词。

items.en: Prae- meant 'before, in front', giving the walking a direction.
items.cn: prae- 意为「在前、在面前」，给行走一个方向。

items.en: Late Latin praeambulum named 'that which goes before', a thing that walks ahead.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语 praeambulum 指「走在前面之物」。

items.en: English borrowed preamble first for legal and church documents.
items.cn: 英语最初在法律与教会文书里借入 preamble。

items.en: Later the word escaped the law and came to mean any opening remarks.
items.cn: 后来这个词走出法律，泛指任何开场的话。

note.en: The look-alike group is the walking family; the near-meaning group separates preface, prologue, introduction and foreword.
note.cn: 形近组是「行走」词族；近义组把「前言」「序幕」「引言」与「序文」分开。

entries.definition: to walk at an easy pace.
able to walk, or moving about.
a section that brings the reader in.
a short opening by someone other than the author.
entries.definitionCN: 由作者之外的人写的短序。

normalIntro.en: The hooks keep the picture of a small escort walking ahead of the real procession.
normalIntro.cn: 以下联想留住「一小队人走在真正队伍前面开路」的画面。

normal.en: Preamble holds prae (before) and ambulare (to walk): the part that walks in front.
normal.cn: preamble 里藏着 prae（在前）与 ambulare（行走）：走在前面那部分。

normal.en: Think of a speaker clearing his throat before the one sentence that matters.
normal.cn: 想象一位说话者在关键那句之前先清了清嗓子。

normal.en: Pre-AM-ble: the stress sits on am, the middle of the walk.
normal.cn: pre-AM-ble：重音落在 am，正是行走的中段。

normal.en: Say PREE-am-bl; the first syllable is already ahead of the rest.
normal.cn: 读成 PREE-am-bl，第一音节已经走在其余部分前面。

normal.en: Pair it with without: 'without preamble' is the phrase people use when they want the point.
normal.cn: 把它和 without 配对：说 without preamble，就是想要直接说重点。

abstract.en: A preamble is a promise about what kind of text follows, made before the text exists.
abstract.cn: 序言是在正文出现之前，对「接下来是哪种文本」作出的承诺。

abstract.en: The word is at its best when short and at its worst when it outgrows the thing it introduces.
abstract.cn: 这个词短的时候最好，长得超过它所引的东西时最糟。

abstract.en: Law, diplomacy and apology all use preambles because all three need to prepare a listener.
abstract.cn: 法律、外交与道歉都用铺垫，因为三者都需要先安顿听者。

examples.en: He offered no greeting and no preamble, and gave the conclusion first.
examples.cn: 他没有寒暄也没有铺垫，开口就是结论。

examples.en: Smog is not treated here; the preamble explains why the book is short.
examples.cn: 这里不谈雾霾，序言解释了这本书为何写得短。

examples.en: The apology was only a preamble to the request.
examples.cn: 那句道歉只是请求之前的铺垫。

dict_mnemonic.text: pre（在前）+ amble（走）：走在正文前面的一段，就是「序言、铺垫」。

root: 拉丁语 prae（在前）与 ambulare（行走）合成的晚期拉丁语 praeambulum

sensesIntro.en: The eight senses all walk ahead of something: a constitution, a treaty, a remark, a deed, a warning, a book, an empty formality and an apology.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都在某样东西前面行走：宪法、条约、一句话、一份契据、一个警告、一本书、一道空洞程序和一句道歉。

core.en: AN ESCORT WALKING AHEAD OF THE PROCESSION
core.cn: 走在队伍前面的那队人

branches.en: A constitution and a treaty.
branches.cn: 宪法与条约。

branches.en: A speech and a warning before bad news.
branches.cn: 一段讲话与坏消息前的警告。

branches.en: A deed reciting its facts.
branches.cn: 一份陈述事实的契据。

branches.en: A book's own note, and the version that outgrows the book.
branches.cn: 书自己的说明，以及那个长得超过正文的版本。

branches.en: The loosest sense: any preparation at all.
branches.cn: 最宽松的义项：任何事前准备。

intro.en: The ambulare family is about walking: amble is an easy walk, ambulance was a moving hospital, and a preamble walks in front of a text.
intro.cn: ambulare 词族关乎行走：amble 是轻松的走，ambulance 曾是会走的医院，preamble 走在文本前面。

latinIntro.en: Latin prae- gives the direction and ambulare gives the gait; praeambulum is simply 'the thing that walks before'.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 prae- 给出方向，ambulare 给出步态；praeambulum 就是「走在前面之物」。

definition_zh: 有先见之明的；能预知的
definition_en: knowing or acting as if one already knows what is going to happen
core_image: 一个人提前站在明天的位置上，回头看今天的人群
scene: 他在会上说这栋楼迟早会出问题，两年后果然塌了。He said at the meeting that the building would fail, and two years later the remark proved prescient.
sceneCN: 这里 prescient 指有先见之明（第 1 个义项：预见未来）；句意为他在会上说这栋楼迟早会出问题，两年后这句话果然应验，显出先见。

pos.zh: 有先见之明的；能预知的

senses.title: Foreseeing events
senses.definition: of a person, knowing what will happen before it happens
senses.definitionCN: 形容人在事情发生之前就知道它会来
senses.example: The chairman was prescient about the collapse of the market.
senses.exampleCN: 主席对市场的崩盘早有预见。
senses.why: The word attributes knowledge of the future, which no one quite has.
senses.whyCN: 这个词把对未来的知识归给某个人，而没人真能拥有它。

senses.title: Prescient warning
senses.definition: of a warning that names the danger before anyone else does
senses.definitionCN: 在别人之前就点出危险的警告
senses.example: Her prescient warning was filed and forgotten.
senses.exampleCN: 她那句有先见的警告被归档，然后被遗忘。
senses.why: The word judges the timing of a sentence, not the person who said it.
senses.whyCN: 这个词评判一句话的时机，而非说话的人。

senses.title: Prescient analysis
senses.definition: of reasoning that reaches tomorrow's conclusion from today's facts
senses.definitionCN: 从今天的事实推出明天结论的推理
senses.example: The report's prescient analysis read the trade figures correctly.
senses.exampleCN: 那份报告有预见性的分析把贸易数字读对了。
senses.why: Analysis earns the word by being right early, not by being loud.
senses.whyCN: 分析靠早而正确赢得这个词，不靠声量。

senses.title: Prescient writer
senses.definition: of an author whose work describes a future that later arrives
senses.definitionCN: 作品描述了后来真的到来的未来的作者
senses.example: The novel was prescient about how people would talk to machines.
senses.exampleCN: 这部小说预见了人们将如何与机器交谈。
senses.why: Art can be called prescient without having made a single forecast.
senses.whyCN: 艺术可以被称作有先见，却一次预测也没做过。

senses.title: Market call
senses.definition: of a financial judgement that turns out right before the crowd agrees
senses.definitionCN: 在众人认同之前就被证明正确的金融判断
senses.example: His prescient call on the currency made him briefly famous.
senses.exampleCN: 他对货币的先见判断让他短暂成名。
senses.why: Money gives the word a scoreboard.
senses.whyCN: 钱给这个词一块记分牌。

senses.title: Prescient policy
senses.definition: of a rule made for a problem that has not yet fully appeared
senses.definitionCN: 为尚未完全出现的难题制定的规则
senses.example: The ban looked fussy then and prescient now.
senses.exampleCN: 那项禁令当时显得多事，如今显得有先见。
senses.why: Institutions are praised for this sense only after the fact.
senses.whyCN: 机构只会在事后因这个义项受到称赞。

senses.title: Prescient dream
senses.definition: of a dream or a feeling that seems to have announced an event
senses.definitionCN: 似乎提前宣告了某件事的梦或感觉
senses.example: She had a prescient dream the night before the accident.
senses.exampleCN: 事故前一晚，她做了一个预知般的梦。
senses.why: The word admits the uncanny without quite believing it.
senses.whyCN: 这个词容许诡异之事，却不完全相信它。

senses.title: Retrospective prescience
senses.definition: the label given afterwards to a remark that happened to be right
senses.definitionCN: 事后给一句碰巧说对的话贴上的标签
senses.example: Every lucky guess is called prescient once the results are in.
senses.exampleCN: 结果一出来，每个走运的猜测都被叫作先见。
senses.why: This sense exposes the trick: the word is often awarded backwards.
senses.whyCN: 这个义项揭穿了把戏：这个词常是倒着颁发的。

intro.en: Prescient is 'knowing before': prae- is before, and scire is to know.
intro.cn: prescient 就是「先知道」：prae- 为在前，scire 为知道。

items.en: Scire meant 'to know', the verb behind science and conscience.
items.cn: scire 意为「知道」，是 science 与 conscience 背后的动词。

items.en: Scientia meant 'knowledge', and English made it science.
items.cn: scientia 意为「知识」，英语把它变成 science。

items.en: Praescire meant 'to know beforehand', a plain compound of prae- and scire.
items.cn: praescire 意为「预先知道」，是 prae- 与 scire 的朴素复合。

items.en: English formed prescient from the Latin participle in the seventeenth century.
items.cn: 英语在十七世纪由拉丁语分词造出 prescient。

items.en: Modern usage applies it to warnings, analyses, novels and lucky guesses alike.
items.cn: 现代用法把它同时用于警告、分析、小说与走运的猜测。

note.en: The look-alike group is the scire family; the near-meaning group separates prophetic, foresighted, clairvoyant and far-sighted.
note.cn: 形近组是 scire 词族；近义组把「预言的」「有远见的」「千里眼的」与「目光长远的」分开。

entries.definition: with knowledge of what is coming.
entries.definitionCN: 带着对将至之事的了解。

entries.definition: the inner sense of right and wrong.

entries.definitionCN: 为可能到来之事作打算的。

normalIntro.en: The hooks keep the picture of a man standing in tomorrow and looking back at today.
normalIntro.cn: 以下联想留住「一个人站在明天，回头看今天」的画面。

normal.en: Prescient is prae plus scire: to know before.
normal.cn: prescient 是 prae 加 scire：先知道。

normal.en: Think of a warning filed two years before the collapse.
normal.cn: 想象一条在崩塌前两年就被归档的警告。

normal.en: Pre-SCI-ent: the stress sits on sci, where the knowing lives.
normal.cn: pre-SCI-ent：重音落在 sci，正是「知道」所在。

normal.en: Say PRESH-uhnt in American speech; the s softens like a whisper.
normal.cn: 美式读成 PRESH-uhnt，那个 s 软得像耳语。

normal.en: Pair it with hindsight: prescient is hindsight awarded in advance.
normal.cn: 把它和 hindsight 配对：prescient 是提前颁发的后见之明。

abstract.en: The word is always awarded after the event, which is why it tells us more about winners than about vision.
abstract.cn: 这个词总在事件之后颁发，所以它更多地告诉我们谁赢了，而不是谁有远见。

abstract.en: A prescient remark needs only to be right early; it does not need to be wise.
abstract.cn: 一句有先见的话只需要早而正确，不需要有智慧。

abstract.en: Every field keeps a small shelf of prescient warnings that nobody read in time.
abstract.cn: 每个领域都有一小架没人及时读的先见警告。

examples.en: The remark proved prescient two years later.
examples.cn: 两年后这句话被证明有先见。

examples.en: The chairman was prescient about the collapse of the market.
examples.cn: 主席对市场的崩盘早有预见。

examples.en: The novel was prescient about how people would talk to machines.
examples.cn: 这部小说预见了人们将如何与机器交谈。

dict_mnemonic.text: pre（在前）+ scient（知道）：提前就知道，就是「有先见之明的」。

root: 拉丁语 prae（在前）与 scire（知道）构成的 praesciens

sensesIntro.en: The eight senses all arrive early: a person, a warning, an analysis, a writer, a market call, a policy, a dream and a label given out after the fact.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都提前到达：一个人、一个警告、一份分析、一位作家、一次市场判断、一项政策、一个梦，以及事后颁发的标签。

core.en: STANDING IN TOMORROW, LOOKING BACK

branches.en: A person and a dream, both credited with the future.
branches.cn: 被归功于未来的人与梦。

branches.en: A warning and an analysis, judged by timing.
branches.cn: 按时机被评判的警告与分析。

branches.en: A writer whose fiction arrives before the fact.
branches.cn: 小说先于事实到达的作家。

branches.en: A market call and a policy.
branches.cn: 一次市场判断与一项政策。

branches.en: The prize handed out afterwards.
branches.cn: 事后颁发的那份奖。

intro.en: The scire family is about knowing: science is organised knowledge, conscience is knowledge shared with oneself, prescient is knowledge that arrives early.
intro.cn: scire 词族关乎知道：science 是有组织的知识，conscience 是与自己共享的知识，prescient 是提前到达的知识。

latinIntro.en: Latin prae- supplies the 'before' and scire supplies the 'know'; the participle praesciens simply joins them.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 prae- 提供「在前」，scire 提供「知道」；分词 praesciens 只是把它们接起来。

definition_zh: 神童；奇才；奇迹；奇观
definition_en: a young person with extraordinary talent, or something so unusual that it seems a wonder or an omen
core_image: 一个孩子在台上完成大人一生才练成的曲子
scene: 他七岁就能拉完整首协奏曲，报纸称他为神童。At seven he could play a whole concerto, and the newspapers called him a prodigy.
sceneCN: 这里 prodigy 指音乐上的神童（第 1 个义项：神童）；句意为他七岁就能拉完整首协奏曲，报纸把他称作神童。

senses.title: Child prodigy
senses.definition: a young person who performs far beyond his years
senses.definitionCN: 表现远超年龄的年轻人
senses.example: At seven he could play a whole concerto, and the newspapers called him a prodigy.
senses.exampleCN: 他七岁就能拉完整首协奏曲，报纸称他为神童。
senses.why: The word measures the gap between age and ability.
senses.whyCN: 这个词衡量年龄与能力之间的落差。

senses.title: Wonder of nature
senses.definition: a natural thing so unusual that it seems a sign
senses.definitionCN: 异常到像是一种征兆的自然之物
senses.example: The double rainbow over the valley was called a prodigy.
senses.exampleCN: 谷地上空的双彩虹被称作奇观。
senses.why: This is the oldest sense: nature speaking out of turn.
senses.whyCN: 这是最古老的义项：自然越出常轨地开口。

senses.title: Portent
senses.definition: an event read as a warning from the gods
senses.definitionCN: 被解读为神祇警告的事件
senses.example: A calf with two heads was a prodigy to the old farmers.
senses.exampleCN: 双头牛犊对老农来说是一种异象。
senses.why: Here the wonder is also a message, and it must be interpreted.
senses.whyCN: 这里奇观同时是消息，而且必须被解读。

senses.title: Prodigy of learning
senses.definition: a person of any age whose command of one field or faculty seems beyond ordinary human reach
senses.definitionCN: 任何年龄在某一领域或某种能力上超出常人的人
senses.example: The scholar was a prodigy of memory and read six languages.
senses.exampleCN: 这位学者是记忆上的奇才，能读六种语言。
senses.why: Age drops out of the definition here, and the word measures mastery alone.
senses.whyCN: 这里年龄退出了定义，这个词只衡量造诣。

intro.en: Prodigy began as an omen: a thing that pointed beyond itself, and only later became a gifted child.
intro.cn: prodigy 起初是一种征兆：一样指向自身之外的东西，后来才变成有天赋的孩子。

items.en: Prodigium meant 'a portent, a sign, a monstrous event'.
items.cn: prodigium 意为「征兆、迹象、异常之事」。

items.en: Roman priests kept lists of prodigia and argued over what they warned of.
items.cn: 罗马祭司记录异象清单，争论它们预示着什么。

items.en: English borrowed prodigy first for omens and wonders.
items.cn: 英语最初借入 prodigy，指征兆与奇观。

items.en: By the seventeenth century the word was being used for a person of extraordinary early talent.
items.cn: 到十七世纪，这个词开始指早慧的人。

items.en: Today the child sense dominates, and the omen sense survives only in old texts.
items.cn: 今天孩子的义项占主导，征兆义只活在旧文本里。

note.en: The look-alike group is the prodigium family; the near-meaning group separates wunderkind, genius, phenomenon and marvel.
note.cn: 形近组是 prodigium 词族；近义组把「神童」「天才」「现象」与「奇物」分开。

entries.definition: wonders, or gifted children, in the plural.
a child who succeeds remarkably early.
entries.definitionCN: 很早便惊人成功的孩子。

normalIntro.en: The hooks keep the picture of a small figure on a big stage, playing something written for grown hands.
normalIntro.cn: 以下联想留住「小个子站在大舞台上，弹着为大人的手写的曲子」的画面。

normal.en: Prodigy holds prodigium, an omen: something that points beyond itself.
normal.cn: prodigy 里藏着 prodigium（征兆）：指向自身之外的东西。

normal.en: Think of a child playing a concerto written for adult hands.
normal.cn: 想象一个孩子弹着为成人之手写的协奏曲。

normal.en: Pro-di-GY: the stress sits on the last syllable, where the surprise lands.
normal.cn: pro-di-GY：重音落在最后，惊讶正落在那里。

normal.en: Say PROD-uh-jee; the first syllable is short, like a small person.
normal.cn: 读成 PROD-uh-jee，第一音节短促，像一个小个子。

normal.en: Pair it with clock: one sense measures a child against time, another measures mastery alone.
normal.cn: 把它和 clock 配对：一个义项用时间量孩子，另一个只量造诣。

abstract.en: A prodigy is a wonder measured against a clock, not against a scale.
abstract.cn: 神童是按时钟衡量的奇观，不是按尺子衡量的。

abstract.en: The word began with signs in the sky and ended with a child at a piano, which is a long way to travel.
abstract.cn: 这个词从天上的迹象开始，最后停在钢琴前的孩子身上，走了很长的路。

abstract.en: Being called a prodigy is a gift with a bill attached, because the clock never stops.
abstract.cn: 被称作神童是一份附了账单的礼物，因为时钟从不停止。

examples.en: At seven he could play a whole concerto, and the newspapers called him a prodigy.
examples.cn: 他七岁就能拉完整首协奏曲，报纸称他为神童。

examples.en: Mozart is the prodigy every later case is measured against.
examples.cn: 莫扎特是后来每一个案例都被拿来对照的神童。

examples.en: The scholar was a prodigy of memory and read six languages.
examples.cn: 这位学者是记忆上的奇才，能读六种语言。

dict_mnemonic.text: pro（向前）+ digy（指出）：指出未来之事的异象，后来指「神童、奇才」。

root: 拉丁语 prodigium（征兆、异象），由 pro-（向前）与提示性的词根构成

sensesIntro.en: The four senses run from a wonder in the sky to a mastery that has no age: a child, a marvel of nature, an omen and a prodigy of learning.
sensesIntro.cn: 四个义项从天上的奇观一路走到不问年龄的造诣：一个孩子、一桩自然奇观、一种征兆，以及一位学问上的奇才。

core.en: A THING OUT OF SCALE, THEN A PERSON OUT OF SCALE
core.cn: 先是超出尺度之物，后是超出尺度之人

chain: IT IS READ AS A SIGN
THE SIGN IS TAKEN AS WONDER
THE WONDER IS FOUND IN A PERSON

branches.en: The child measured against the clock.
branches.cn: 按时钟衡量的孩子。

branches.en: Nature making something out of scale.
branches.cn: 自然造出超尺度之物。

branches.en: The same wonder read as a warning.
branches.cn: 同一奇观被读成警告。

branches.en: Mastery that needs no birthday.
branches.cn: 不需要生日的造诣。

branches.en: Two gifted people, one early and one deep.
branches.cn: 两个有天赋的人，一个早，一个深。

intro.en: The prodigium family is about things out of scale: prodigious means enormous, prodigality means waste on a grand scale, and a prodigy is a wonder before it is a child.
intro.cn: prodigium 词族关乎超出尺度之物：prodigious 意为巨大，prodigality 意为大规模挥霍，而 prodigy 先是奇观，后才是孩子。

latinIntro.en: Latin prodigium supplies the sign; the endings -ious and -ality stretch it towards size and spending, while the bare noun keeps the wonder.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 prodigium 提供迹象；词尾 -ious 与 -ality 把它伸向规模与花费，而光秃的名词保留那份惊奇。

items.meaning: a sign of what is to come

definition_zh: 预言；预测；预示
definition_en: to say what will happen, usually on the basis of signs or a trained reading
core_image: 一个人摊开一封写着未来的信，逐行念给旁边的人听
scene: 医生不愿给出时间表，只说不能凭一张片子预言结局。The doctor would not give a timetable and said no single scan could prognosticate the outcome.
sceneCN: 这里 prognosticate 指预言结局（第 1 个义项：预测病情）；句意为医生不愿给出时间表，只说不能凭一张片子就预言结局。

senses.title: Forecast illness
senses.definition: to say how a disease is likely to develop
senses.definitionCN: 判断一种病大致会往哪里走
senses.example: The doctor could prognosticate a slow recovery but not a date.
senses.exampleCN: 医生能预测康复会很慢，却给不出日期。
senses.why: This is the word's most careful home, where the claim is hedged.
senses.whyCN: 这是这个词最谨慎的家，主张在这里都带着保留。

senses.title: Forecast weather
senses.definition: to read the sky and say what it will do
senses.definitionCN: 读天色并说出它接下来会怎样
senses.example: Sailors used to prognosticate storms from the colour of dawn.
senses.exampleCN: 水手曾凭黎明的颜色预测风暴。
senses.why: Old weather lore is a method, even when it is wrong.
senses.whyCN: 古老的天气经验是一种方法，即使它错了也是。

senses.title: Foretell by signs
senses.definition: to read an omen and announce what it points to
senses.definitionCN: 读出一个征兆，并宣告它指向什么
senses.example: The priest prognosticated a long war from a single eclipse.
senses.exampleCN: 祭司从一次日食预言了一场漫长的战争。
senses.why: Here the word belongs to divination rather than to data.
senses.whyCN: 这里这个词属于占卜，而不属于数据。

senses.title: Political forecast
senses.definition: to say how an election or a movement will end
senses.definitionCN: 说出选举或运动将如何收场
senses.example: The columnist prognosticated a coalition within a month.
senses.exampleCN: 这位专栏作者预测一个月内会组成联合政府。
senses.why: Commentary borrows the word to sound more scientific than it is.
senses.whyCN: 评论借来这个词，好显得比实际更科学。

senses.title: Economic forecast
senses.definition: to estimate the direction of prices, output or jobs
senses.definitionCN: 估计价格、产出或就业的走向
senses.example: The bank prognosticated two quarters of falling demand.
senses.exampleCN: 这家银行预测需求会连续两个季度下滑。
senses.why: The word adds gravity to a number that may be a guess.
senses.whyCN: 这个词给一个可能只是猜测的数字增加了分量。

senses.title: Pompous prediction
senses.definition: to announce the future in a tone that expects to be admired
senses.definitionCN: 以一种期待被称赞的腔调宣告未来
senses.example: He prognosticated the end of the printed book for the third time.
senses.exampleCN: 他第三次预言纸质书的终结。
senses.why: The word can be a way of making a guess sound like an office.
senses.whyCN: 这个词可以把一个猜测说得像一份公职。

senses.title: Foretell doom
senses.definition: to announce disaster, often with satisfaction
senses.definitionCN: 宣告灾难，常带着一点得意
senses.example: The letter prognosticated ruin for anyone who signed.
senses.exampleCN: 这封信预示凡是签字的人都会毁掉。
senses.why: Doom is the easiest thing to prognosticate and the hardest to disprove.
senses.whyCN: 灾祸最容易预言，也最难被反驳。

senses.title: Forecast a match
senses.definition: to say how a game or a season will end
senses.definitionCN: 说出比赛或赛季将如何收场
senses.example: The pundit prognosticated a draw and got the score right.
senses.exampleCN: 这位评论员预测平局，比分也报对了。
senses.why: Sport offers the word a scoreboard, which most predictions never get.
senses.whyCN: 体育给这个词一块记分牌，而多数预测从来没有。

intro.en: Prognosticate is 'to know before': the Greek verb for knowing sits inside a Latin-shaped English word.
intro.cn: prognosticate 就是「先知道」：希腊语表「知道」的动词，躺在一个拉丁外形的英语词里。

items.en: Gignoskein meant 'to know or recognise', the verb behind diagnosis and prognosis.
items.cn: gignoskein 意为「知道、辨认」，是 diagnosis 与 prognosis 背后的动词。

items.en: Prognostikos meant 'knowing beforehand', used of signs that told the future.
items.cn: prognostikos 意为「预先知道的」，用于指示未来的征兆。

items.en: Medieval Latin made prognosticare, a verb for announcing what a sign meant.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁语造出 prognosticare，指宣告某个征兆的含义。

items.en: English borrowed prognosticate for forecasting in medicine and astrology.
items.cn: 英语借入 prognosticate，用于医学与占星里的预测。

items.en: Today prognosis is the sober medical noun, while prognosticate often sounds pompous.
items.cn: 今天 prognosis 是冷静的医学名词，而 prognosticate 常显得浮夸。

note.en: The look-alike group is the gnosis family; the near-meaning group separates predict, foretell, forecast and presage.
note.cn: 形近组是 gnosis 词族；近义组把「预测」「预言」「预报」与「预示」分开。

entries.definition: serving as a sign of the future.
to be a warning sign of.

normalIntro.en: The hooks keep the picture of a letter about the future being read aloud.
normalIntro.cn: 以下联想留住「一封关于未来的信被当众念出」的画面。

normal.en: Prognosticate is pro plus gnosis: knowing before.
normal.cn: prognosticate 是 pro 加 gnosis：先知道。

normal.en: Think of a doctor who will forecast a slow recovery but refuses to name a date.
normal.cn: 想象一位医生，能预测康复很慢，却拒绝给出日期。

normal.en: Prog-NOS-ti-cate: the stress sits on nos, where the knowing is.
normal.cn: prog-NOS-ti-cate：重音落在 nos，正是「知道」所在。

normal.en: Say prog-NOS-tuh-kayt; the long word sounds like a committee report.
normal.cn: 读成 prog-NOS-tuh-kayt，这个长词听起来像一份委员会报告。

normal.en: Pair it with prognosis: the noun is sober, the verb often is not.
normal.cn: 把它和 prognosis 配对：名词冷静，动词常常不是。

abstract.en: To prognosticate is to make a claim about a world that has not arrived yet, and to hope no one checks the date.
abstract.cn: 预言就是对尚未到来的世界作出主张，并希望没人去核对日期。

abstract.en: The word carries more authority than predict and less evidence than forecast.
abstract.cn: 这个词比 predict 更有权威感，却比 forecast 更缺证据。

abstract.en: Every profession keeps a version of this verb for the moment it must speak before it knows.
abstract.cn: 每个行业都留着一个这样的动词，用在必须开口却还没知道的时刻。

examples.en: No single scan could prognosticate the outcome.
examples.cn: 没有一张片子能预言结局。

examples.en: Sailors used to prognosticate storms from the colour of dawn.
examples.cn: 水手曾凭黎明的颜色预测风暴。

examples.en: The pundit prognosticated a draw and got the score right.
examples.cn: 这位评论员预测平局，比分也报对了。

dict_mnemonic.text: pro（在前）+ gnost（知道）+ icate：提前说出所知道的，就是「预言」。

root: 希腊语 pro-（在前）与 gignoskein（知道），经中世纪拉丁语 prognosticare 进入英语
